The only way to leave this room, aside from being a yellow coward fleeing to the lifestone, your home or your master's mansion, is to solve the puzzle there on the pedestal. But you'll need to be an accomplished vagabond to finish that puzzle. Oh and one more thing, the puzzle box has a built in failsafe to see that un...

Energy lashes out around your hands climbing along your arm in an effort to engulf your body. A high pitched screech wails in your mind.
You reach down and pickup the mask. You nearly drop it when you see two eyes staring from the eyeholes. An instant later they are gone.
As your hand falls on the mask the surface ripples and voice calls to you "Put it on. Yes, we will be as one. Wear it."
As you pickup the mask you have an overwhelming urge to put it on. Everything looks so much more vibrant through the eyeholes.

The mask slips onto your face, and feels wet. Tendrils of energy loop into your cheeks and a purple hue covers your eyes for a brief moment. The world swims and your consciousness enhances. The smell of burned flesh fills your nostrils.
"Am I not comfortable?" The flesh on your face shifts and contorts. "How about now?"
A man's voice fills your head. "Do you hear voices? I do. I cannot escape them!"
The wretched mask slips over your head and for a moment you wonder... will it ever come off?
A man's voice bellows "Ahhhh! GET OUT OF MY HEAD!"
As the mask falls into place you see Virindi... everywhere. The faces melt into nothingness after a few panicked moments.
A man's voice screams "The pain! The pain!"

Your breath quickens and a pain grows in your chest. Your head begins to hum and the world begins to close in upon you ever tighter. Claustrophobia clutches you in vice-like grip. The mask tightens on your skull threatening to crush it.
Your vision clouds. You are standing in a doorway watching a woman cradle a small child. She appears to be weeping. You look at your ruined, clawed hand and begin to weep yourself.
As you wear the mask your vision fails you and it feels like egg yolks begin to run down your face.
Your vision clouds. Magical energy crackles all around you as a deafening hum pervades the air. You feel a sense of satisfaction as you stare into the shocked and widening eyes of Gaerlan.
Beside you the portal swirls. You force the energy ever outwards driving it into the very core of the citadel below you. Your flesh sloughs off, and your robe falls to the ground. Human once more.
The explosions begin. You knew they would, a flash of brilliant white light ruins the vision in your right eye and you stumble. The sound of your magic and the whir of the portal all that are left.
Your breathing becomes labored. There is no pain. You hear a woman's voice, soft and loving. "Candeth... Candeth..." The sound of a small child's laughter fills your head. You smile.
Darkness clouds your vision. You hear water dripping and smell blood. A voice invades your mind and pervades your thoughts "Puppet, Reports are strong today. Puppet assimilates well."
You have a strange thought. "Power it could be ours again."
As you don the shell of Martine, you are overcome by the feeling of slugs crawling all over your face for a moment, until the mask slips into place, and all is well.
You feel the flesh of your face searing becoming one with the mask.
You feel an irresistable urge to limp.
You feel alone in the world. All around you are enemies. They will not help you quell the renegades. These Isparian meatlings must be destroyed.
As you place the mask on your face tendrils of energy reach into the recesses of your mind sqeezing down. The eye sockets of the mask blink open and closed in quick succession.
For a moment you think of home and family, then the memories fade into an array of abstract analysis, devoid of soul.
Your thoughts stray to Elysa, no Melanay, Elysa, no Melanay.
As your thoughts stray to Asheron you think of home and the wife and child you have lost. You have an urge to scream.
A warm feeling of home and hearth fills your mind. You see a child playing at your feet... and then the sensation fades.
A man's voice says, "Eyes in the dark."
A man's voice says, "Two moons circle."
A man's voice says, "Am I not a man? Correction. Are we not men?"
The ghostly image of a fallen Tusker, its skull exploded open from the inside, appears in front of you. A smile creeps onto your face and then the image disappears.

A mosswart with outstretched arms, screaming in what appears to be pain, dangles before you. Its screaming becomes ragged and finally ceases as its head drops down to its chest and mosswart disappears.
The face of the enemy appears before you. He speaks consoling words, but your mind fills with hate as you struggle to attack this man... and then the feeling fades.
Your mind is flooded with the sights and sounds of a bustling port and a melancholy feeling overpowers your thoughts, but the vision soon fades.

A small boy looks at you without fear. You had meant to kill him. Arrita's giggles fill your head as you look at the tattered letter in your hand. Melanay's kisses and gentle smile come to mind and you stand. "Come Borelean it is time to make amends."
Screeches, howls, hums and unearthly sounds of wet fingers running along crystal pervade your mind a pulsing thrum throbs within. The singularity calls to you.
You squeal trapped in a cell devoid of light. You are but a fraction when once you were a whole. You have a feeling you had never had before. Loss.
Your sanity shatters like a crystal goblet.
The calming chimes of the singularity tug at the back of your mind and your consciousness threatens to slip away.
He stands before you and offers the way home. You hesitate a moment and you think his offer is sound.

As the magic coalesces and tears through Asheron's chest you smile broadly thinking now you will have Elysa for your own. But the betrayal is at hand when your mind clears and your conscience becomes heavy.
An arrow slices through your throat. Rocks pelt against your head and body. People beat your body bloody. You have become the slayer of hope.
Asheron quells the ravages in your mind. You begin to think clearer as if a great weight has been lifted from your mind.
A man's voice says, "As you have done for me, I now return the favor." Asheron's wounds close and he looks upon you.
The feeling of intense claustrophobia lifts as you slip that disgusting shell from your head.
A tinny voice calls out, "Where are you putting me? I liked it there."
A tinny voice calls out, "No! Put me back!"
A tinny voice calls out, "Don't leave me alone. I can't stand to be alone."
When you remove the mask, the voices in your head decrease to the normal level.
The mask slips from your skull with a sickeningly slick sound.
As you pull the mask from your head the flesh threatens to come with it.
The mask refuses to give up its grip on your skull for a moment.
A sound of Virindi holding a conversation in your head sounds as you peel the mask from your face.
As you try to pull the mask from your face the eye sockets and mouth close off choking you near to death.
A symbol of the Shadow -- you may enter.
%s has entered the Forbidden Catacombs.
A symbol of Greed -- you may enter.
I have always wanted one of these.
The Guardian of the Forbidden hugs his beloved new Pack Doll.
A symbol of the Cute -- you may enter.
You shall not enter.
Heed my warning -- Turn back now! This place is not for you.
Begone! Only death dwells within.
Your wound tickles the wall of the Kukuur's stomach and you are unceremoniously purged from the beast's belly.
Your failed spell tickles the wall of the Kukuur's stomach and you are unceremoniously purged from the beast's belly.
I only use the freshest snows and ice in my cooking. If you can't make it fresh don't make it.

I know people who know people who might be able to take care of Scold -- but once I call that favor in, I'll owe them one. And you don't want to owe these guys nothin'! So, if you can teach that magma-hucker a lesson, I would be very grateful.
Eh, if it helps, I'll chill you up somethin' real delicious for after you give Scold his ice-bath. He should lay of the spicy food, it's bad for his disposition.
A pinch of this, some frosting - and FREEZO we got ourselves a frizzin' delicacy.
chatter: You are frizzin' hero, you know that?!
You remind me of this guy I knew. He was a good guy, a little thick, but a good guy, ya know?
Here you go. It just came out of the Ice Box.

greetings: That Scold is a real trouble maker. Yup, he's been tearing around town melting our houses and trying to drive us off. He claims that this whole mountain is his.
He really hates snowmen...
If you can get rid of Scold I promise you I'll reward you as best I can.
Don't you worry, my word's as good as ice on a cold day.
Scold destroyed my last harvest. He sauntered right into town and stomped all over my garden.
Snow Gardens require special attention. Mine needs fresh snow daily or the crop will wither and die.

I once saw a rabbit try to steal a carrot from my garden. Why he was even up here in the first place I don't know. Anyway, he seemed so happy with himself when he dug the carrot out that I didn't have the heart to stop him.
You should have seen the look on his little rabbit face when he tried to bite into it. Guess he wasn't used to ice carrots. Funny little critter.
Well, carrots are very important to us snowmen. We use them for our noses of course and it's always good to have a backup. Then there are the other carrot related activities.
chatter: Oh, another weed.
Well, I'll be! You made it back in one piece! I have to admit I thought taking on Scold in his own cave was a bit crazy, but you proved how lucky you are!
I'm a snowman of my word, so here's your reward.
Hehe, now everyone will know you have the biggest carrot around, eh?

greetings: Stupid golem bully! Why can't he just chill out?
I think all magma golems should be killed. I don't care! They shouldn't be allowed to hurt people.
Someday I'll be bigger than Scold and then he'll see.
%mn grabs some snow and pats himself down with it, trying to make himself bigger.
He'll see, I'll get him back for what he did to Frank.
%mn turns away from you as an icicle begins to form under one of his coal eyes.
%mn calls out a little too loudly.
Scold's a big pansy. Scold's real name is Nancy!
Scold's a chicken in a pile of tusker poo!!
chatter: Olly olly frost come free!
Hey, no fair!
Yeah, I can't lose!
Who's the Snowman?!
I win! Haha! Yes!

You killed Captain Stupido Hot-Head? Aw! I wanted to fight him. Some day I'm going to be a member of the Snowman Guard and I'll freeze guys like that Scold cold. See, I made these special ice balls to throw at him, but since you took him down you can have them.
Happy Birthday!

greetings: And here I was hoping we could be friends...
I'll be back again someday AND THEN YOU'LL BE SORRY!
Oh now, why did I go and do that? GRRRRRAGH!
I don't WANT TO HURT YOU!
HAHAHAHA! Oh, I'm so sorry!
YOU CANT HANDLE THE CHILL! Not again!
Oh good, a visitor! GO AWAY!
ARGHUGARGAHAGA! What?
Ow! Stop that! YOU WANT SOME OF THIS!?!
NORMALLY I'D SMOOSH YOU, but I'm feeling happy today.
Please, just chop off HIS head OR I COULD TAKE YOURS!
Wait, I'm not that bad, let's just talk about this. ONCE YOU'RE FROZEN SOLID!
That was pretty good, you almost had me. CHUMP!
chatter: Isn't it just beautiful out today? NO, IT'S TOO HOT!
It's a shame I can't make more friends. FRIENDS ARE FOR LOSERS!
LETS KILL BUNNY RABBITS! How horribly unfeeling.
I'm soo Happy! ...YEAH, ITS GOOD TO BE BAD!
A CARROT! WHY A CARROT?!? I like my carrot. YOU WOULD!

greetings: Why does everyone keep attacking us? We are a peaceful race. All we want is to live in pea...
That one's for Frank!
%mn screams, Defend the town!!!
Merely a slush wound!
Take your heat somewhere else! We don't want you violent types in our town!
You want to see a trick?
Ok, close your eyes.
You feel a freezing piece of snow slide down your back.
Ahahahaha! I so got you! Aahahahaha! That was great!
What's black and white and goes fizzle-splash?
A Snowman with a fire wand!
Scold? I don't want to talk about Scold. He's mean and I hate him and wish he would die.
Want to see a trick?
Pretty cool, huh? Bet you can't do that.
chatter: Jump! Jump! I'm the winner!
Wait, that only counts on ones!
No, you were on a two.
Hehe, did you see that one?
I win! Haha! Yes!
Wow, how did you do it? Did he burn you or melt any of your friends? What was his cave like? Did he say anything about our village? Huh, did he?
You're not bad for a human. Mom says that humans can be dangerous. I guess you sorta are, but you kick golem butt, so you're a good kindof dangerous.
Heh, maybe someday I'll save a human town from evil and then we can all live together in peace. That would be cool.
I'd like to give you these special snowballs I make. They don't hurt anyone, but they make a big poof when they hit.

quest: I will not fight for I follow the Path of the Snowflake.
I had a Seeing Eye Drudge, but he thought yellow snow was funny.
I would go for a walk, but some nasty little beast stole my Peppermint Stick!
I'm really worried that a fire elemental might come by. Normally I could run and hide. Maybe I'll try building a snow castle.
One person suggested I use diamonds for eyes. I tried that and it was really pretty, but the thousand little views made me toss snow.
Ah, more coal? You are very kind, but I have all I need to refashion my eyes. It may take some time, but you have helped me enough. Here, have this back in case you lose your eyes.
What's this?
A stick? Well, my left arm has been acting up a bit, only in the warm weather though.
The Blind Snowman raises the peppermint stick to his carrot and sniffs.
Oh, another peppermint stick! Well, you've been so generous that I don't need any more. Have it back.
Perhaps you could get something from the drudges for it. I hear they love sweets.
I was standing in a meadow minding my own business, taking in the scenery, when BAM I get whacked with something from behind.

Shoom! Shoom! Both my eyes go flying from my head and I can't see. Then I hear two distinct voices. One was chiding the other to apologize and the other one was laughing all crazy and mean. The mean voice said that was the funniest thing it had ever seen and to shut up or it would do the same to the nicer voice.
People these days! If you see my eyes around would you please bring them to me? I would be very appreciative.
Wohoo! Thank you! I'll be able to make a new set of eyes once this gets cold enough!
You deserve a reward for your good deed. Let's see... well not see per se... one second.
The Blind Snowman scoops up a pile of snow and casts a spell. The snow coalesces forming ice crystals that shift and rearrange as if alive.
I can't be sure it turned out exactly right, but I hope you like it.
May your bottom stay cold and your eyes stay put. Soon I'll be able to see the snow again!
The Blind Snowman swallows the Lump of Coal with a contented smile.
A stick? But, I've already got two perfectly good arms.
Minty! Oh, thank you! Now I can take strolls without tripping over things.
Here, have this, I found it in my... I found it that last time I tripped.
chatter: Who's there? I..I've got an icicle!
I'm not dangerous. See? I'm smiling.
Have you seen my eyes around?
Much more of this and I'm going to become an Unhappy Snowman.

greetings: Hot! Hot! Too hot!
I can't drink hot tea deary, it goes right through me.

A nice cold cup of tea and a good friend to chat with. This is nice now isn't it? Time was when I could have a nice tea without worrying about some homicidal lump of animated lava coming in here and killing us all!
Oh my, I'm so sorry dear, I've been a little jumpy ever since Frank was melted.
%mn wipes a few icicles away and stares out the igloo door.
He was such a good snowman and he was so good with the children. We all miss him terribly.
Hello dear! I'm quite busy, but I love guests -- so just sit anywhere you like and we can have some tea and a nice chat.
Nip and Numb are such good boys. I worry how this whole Scold thing is affecting them though. I think Nip is getting a bit angry. Have you ever seen an angry snowman? I don't want that for my son.
That big brute of a golem! Scold actually enjoys destroying our little town. He must have had a bad childhood, but that's no excuse to take it out on us!
You look like a kind human. Please help us.
Did the Mayor ask about me?
quest: %mn looks you up and down.
You know, if you were covered in snow, you wouldn't make a half bad snowman.
I need to find myself a real Snowman.
Oh, isn't that nice -- a human!
chatter: You kids should come in soon! It's getting too warm out!
Oh, I hope that nasty golem doesn't come back.
Oh! You made it back alright! I'm so very happy! And you brought proof of Scold's demise. I can't thank you enough! Here's a little something I froze for you while you were gone.
It's magically resistant to heat so it won't melt. It hope it will helps to remind you not to chop up people just because they are made of snow.

greetings: Ow! It's still hot, and burning. The fact that it still gives off heat is interesting. Let's see, I have your reward over here.
I just finished it. It's a marvel of ice and function. You will see here the controls with three settings: Chilly, Freezing and 'My fingers are stuck to the ice, it's so cold.'
It works on the Frostian Principle of inverse hyper-therma-whatchamaglavins.
What's it for? Well, the theory is obvious to even the simplest of advanced thermo-mechanical engineers.
Oy! For winter's sake! It keeps your house cool.
I tried ice-bombing Scold's cave last week, but he must have some heat source down there. Otherwise he should have been frozen solid almost instantly.
I would like to have a piece of Scold to study should you find one, say during your frenzied death march on his cave.
I've been studying Scold - with the burning and the melting and excruciating pain, RUN FOR YOUR LIVES!
He seems weak to cold attacks.
What?
Have you ever wondered why we don't call you Meatmen?

quest: You have my blessing to enter these halls, child of another sun.

Your knowledge of the passage of time on this world is not great enough to enter the chapel beyond the door. Return to my in one day's time. If you obtain the knowledge of the past by that time, test yourself again.

Alighting on wings, head hung in grief, looking down one last time on her aerie, watching as her children looked up, Aurlanna flew into the heavens and beyond the stars never to return. Her heart was shattered when she found that those that she had once called sisters had been killed by zealots blinded by the purpose of a throne that had forsaken its true path for power. She felt the urge to jo...

You have proven to me that you are aware of what has transpired on this world. I give you my word that you shall see the halls beyond. Speak to my brothers and prove your worthiness to them. If you succeed the door to this chapel shall be yours to open evermore.

Child of another sun, your coming to this place will inspire works of art. In time, the three races that now strive for peace shall be known in statues across this hall. I shall carve likenesses with my own hands and offer them for future generations to see. The Age of the children from another sun shall be born in that vision and there shall be memory cast within that stone. My name is Kir Loz...
You must know of what has transpired before you may enter.
Forsaking her children and Au, she laid waste to the crusaders that scoured the halls of Ithaenc clean. Her will crushed, she went beyond the stars one last time. She has yet to return. Who is she?

Along the landing of this room I have placed the statues of three such beings. Choose the answer to my question wisely and you shall be given my blessing to pass into this chapel. Fail and I shall need you to rethink the purpose of your task within and ask that you return when you know more of this world.

greetings: %s has defeated Gaerlan's electric aspect. As the illusion crumbles away a deep voice thunders over the world, "A doomed eternity to relive this life. Stasis within the walls of a crystalline prison. How could I have fallen to you vermin. Nuhmudira, my revenge upon you shall be as painful as yours upon me."
Insignificant being. Your attempt at injury is noted.
Even in death I find your magics to be weak. You are a pathetic brood of beings.
Even as my flesh begins to rot away, my spirit strengthens, take your lackluster skill where it can be of use... human.
Magic is not for children to practice.
Withered in this shell, broken by one of you, how can I have been reduced to this?

%s has defeated Gaerlan's acidic aspect. As the illusion crumbles away a deep voice thunders over the world, "A doomed eternity to relive this life. Stasis within the walls of a crystalline prison. How could I have fallen to you vermin. Nuhmudira, my revenge upon you shall be as painful as yours upon me."

%s has defeated Gaerlan's fiery aspect. As the illusion crumbles away a deep voice thunders over the world, "A doomed eternity to relive this life. Stasis within the walls of a crystalline prison. How could I have fallen to you vermin. Nuhmudira, my revenge upon you shall be as painful as yours upon me."

%s has defeated Gaerlan's frost aspect. As the illusion crumbles away a deep voice thunders over the world, "A doomed eternity to relive this life. Stasis within the walls of a crystalline prison. How could I have fallen to you vermin. Nuhmudira, my revenge upon you shall be as painful as yours upon me."

quest: There is nothing more that I can tell you at this time. I must reflect upon what has transpired and devise a way to deal with this menace. It will require the efforts of us all if this is indeed the same Queen.
Welcome. I had never thought that I would see Isparians here, aside from Elysa and Borelean. But I see that you have made your way across my island and through the Olthoi Hordes.
I have fashioned this book to explain everything that I know at this time about the resurgence of the Olthoi. I am indebted to you once more for your actions.
I am not quite sure what caused them to come here, but I am quite sure that it relates directly to the evidence turned up at Knorr.
Oh yes, I am well aware that you have been making your way through my familial estate; while I am not happy about your intrusion there, this world is as much yours as it is mine now.
Asheron smirks.

I am however, all too well aware of Nuhmudira and her quest for more power. She plays with primal forces that are far beyond her frame to contain. In some respects, I pity her for her madness; in others, I revile her for the selfish manner in which she acts.
Asheron pauses looking to his guardians.
I had assumed that the Queen at Knorr was not eternal. But this invasion has caused me to re-assess that assumption. It has been nearly 800 years since I have seen that Queen.

If she has come, then we shall need to band together as never before. I could not use the full power of my magical arsenal while those creatures were here. There was something potent that drained the higher magics from the area. Now I feel them back again. You have helped to restore me...now we need to assist ourselves.

This Queen...is the most terrible thing that this world or any other has ever seen. What is worse is that she remembers, and in that memory she undoubtedly is stalking me...but when she learns that her children have suffered so much at our hands, her attentions will be cast toward us all.

greetings: Your vision swims. For a moment, your vision dims. Great wooden doors, intricately carved and glowing faintly green, creak open before you. Before you is a long, wide hall, its cloistered ceilings lit by false stars that mime the constellations of the sky outside. Niches along both sides are lined with candles. No... not candles, but simple silver rods, tarnish blackening the hollows of their f...

Musical, incomprehensible speech calls your attention to the end of the great hall. A figure stands there, backlit by a roiling white inferno as blinding as the sun. A long shadow, unleavened by the waterlight from the silver rods, paints the marble at your feet. Like an echo, the meaning of the words comes back at you.

"Raen Ameranten. Chevaird of the Ialarchess. Child of Atermore, the  Alabaster Fortress that Rises from the sea; the Rock which guards the eastern ways of the glorious Imperial Archipelago. You are here required to swear the Rule of Life. Will you walk upon the path of a righteous life, in fear of and in service to the clear Light? Or will you turn aside to darkness, as have others of your orde...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to stand in creaking jungle. You are running, swinging a sword wreathed in astral flames. A hundred men around you roar as one. There! At last, the ornate blue spires rise before you. Ridiculous lizard-men flap towards you, their eyes glowing. Women dressed in the skins of animals raise their hands, and the ground erupts. You swim forward, wading throug...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem be running down stairs. Men lining the walls grin at you, bowing as you pass. They smell of sweat and blood, their white, star-branded campaign cloaks stained a lurid incarnadine. Their nostrils are flaring. Lips pull back from grey and brown teeth. You hold the torch above your head.

The women huddle together in the center of the blue stone room, watching the men with cool, detached defiance. Is that how it is? We'll see how long that detachment lasts. You nod to the men. One steps forward and wrenches a heretic girl out of the group, bending her arm a way it is not meant to go, driving her down to bruise her knees on the stones of the floor. She does not scream. The beads...
The room is silent but for the snapping of your torch. A lone bird cries in jungle outside.

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be staggering up a flight of stairs. A fetor rises from the room below, the stink of the slaughterhouse. They never made a sound. None of them, not even once, not even when the blades began to hew. Men follow you up, slapping each other on the back, laughing too much as they adjust their campaign cloaks. The air is no cleaner above, though. Here the...

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be on the deck of a ship. A ship? There are no... Over the rail you can see docks carved from alabaster and chalcedony. Where? A crowd that roars. Shrill. The clouds recoil over the glittering spires of the city, and black rain descends on buzzing alien wings. The deck lurches - you find yourself clutching the wall of the dungeon.

quest: You have my blessing to enter these halls, child of another sun.

Your knowledge of the passage of time on this world is not great enough to enter the chapel beyond the door. Return to my in one day's time. If you obtain the knowledge of the past by that time, test yourself again.

With a sword soaked in the blood of people with whom she once claimed a kinship, Nali Valynd fell upon the sisters at Ithaenc. They who followed a path bathed in Light lay broken by the Nali of the Northern Church. Misguided crusaders loyal to the Nali visited mistress Aurlanna and knelt before her with proud voices proclaiming victory over the -heathens- that dwelled within Ithaenc Cathedral....

You have proven to me that you are aware of what has transpired on this world. I give you my word that you shall see the halls beyond. Speak to my brothers and prove your worthiness to them. If you succeed the door to this chapel shall be yours to open evermore.

Child of another sun, your coming to this place will inspire another work of art. Your three leaders shall grace the walls of the chapel. Their busts carved by my own hands. My name is Jif Loz, it is all I retain of my life before. Nothing can halt the ruination of my memory. It is a position of grace that I gladly accepted in a time when all who walked in Light were not lost. Ages have past, t...
You must know of what has transpired before you may enter.

In the age of the Yalain, one came to Ithaenc and laid waste to the sisters there. All were slaughtered, none survived, light was drawn thin as darkness continued to slip into the hearts of the guardians. Who lead that slaughter, who gave the orders to murder the sisters of Ithaenc Cathedral?

I have carved and polished three busts along the wall of this room, each represents an individual from that time. Choose your answer wisely and you shall be given leave to enter this place. Fail and you will need to learn more of the secrets of this world before entering.

greetings: No, no. Let me use small words: Give this to Celcynd in Rithwic. I'll give you a reward. Go away.
What do I want with this? I can't think of anyone fool enough to drink that.
%n appraises you.
Well there is one I can think of who might.
What, it isn't flashy enough for you? Too bad!
That's as good as it gets! Now let me return to my work!
Could you have found anything heavier to give me?
Smelt that first. Sure I could smelt that Iron for you, but then what would you do with your ample free time?
I seem to remember giving this to you for you to use.
examines the book closely.
Hah, got it back from that drunkard, did you? Only a fool lets himself lose as much as he has.  Once, he was the greatest of his generation.  Did you know that?
You'd never think it to see the sot he is now - well, you got my book back, so you deserve that reward.
By the way, I'd be careful when you use that spell.
%n snickers.
Now leave me in peace.
Found the iron eh? Well, give me a minute.
%n's eyes glow briefly for a moment
There it's fixed, now don't let the door hit you on the way out. And don't come back!
Never seen an Empyrean before? Shoo! Shoo! I have work to do.
Did you know that Empyreans have 14 schools of magic? Would you like me to demonstrate them all on you?
It was so much better when you people thought I was one of you. That's impossible now though, thanks to that cretin Gaerlan.
What, looking for some great quest, some grand purpose from the Empyrean? Go away!
I liberate some of your people from a despotic ruler...think you could show a little bit of respect!
Alfrega, Alfrega girl! Fresh meat!
Off with you, I'm a busy mage!
Go away! And don't tell Asheron I'm down here! Never could stand the man...
You best not have done anything to Alfrega, if you know what's good for you...
Well if you are going to continue to bother me, you can at least do something for me. Take this note to Celcynd in Rithwic.
He borrowed one of my history books sometime ago and didn't return it because he became a drunken waste. Probably spilled alcohol all over it.
Go get it and I'll give you some scroll I've got lying around here...or not. Will you leave me alone then?
I don't want this back.
You'd never think it to see the sot he is now - and all because of this cursed spell, which he lacked the strength to cast twice, when it was needed most.
Regardless, a deal is a deal, and it's your problem if it fails you.  Now go away, and don't bother me anymore!
What would I want with this?  Have you been drinking this?  I know what you young fools do with such things!  Begone, before I report you to the Knights of the Golden Flame!
Fine. Take the staff, don't let the door hit you on the way out. And don't come back!
What? I ALREADY fixed this. Go away before I call Alfrega in here!
You couldn't find something heavier to give me, eh? I'll tell you secret...I have no interest in your lump of iron ore!
If you gave me a good reason, I might help you smelt the ore, but right now I have to tie my shoes.
Listen, if I wanted a pot I would have asked you for one!
Who are you?
Who sent you?
What do you want?
Leave me alone!
Go away!
Bah. I have no time for this!
Stop wasting my time! I'm a busy mage!
You'd best not have harmed my pet Reedshark, Alfrega!
Alfrega! Here girl! There's a tasty snack bothering me!

Well, if you're here, why don't you make yourself useful. Celcynd, the planar mage from Rithwic, borrowed one of my histories a few years back, and never returned it because he became a drunken waste.
Get it for me, and I'll give you a portal spell scroll he gave me. Will you leave me alone then?
quest: Sure, come to the Empyrean to have him fix your problems. I'm  a mage, not a tinker!
Eh well it is in pretty bad shape. I MIGHT be able to fix it, but I'm going to need some iron.
Make yourself useful, take this and go to the Collier mines.
You should be able to find some ore lying around in a wheelbarrow there. Smelt it down and bring it back to me.
That should be enough to fix this piece of cr...
%n clears his throat
...er, treasured relic and give me some peace and quiet. Now, off with you.
I'm not going to fix another of these for you! Go away before I call Alfrega on you
Oh sure. I'll just cast 'Fix Your Useless Crap VI' on this for you, eh? I'm a mage, not a tinker!
Eh, it's in bad shape but I MIGHT be able to restore it. Here, make yourself useful. Take this, and use it to smelt some iron ore.
You might be able to find some lying around in a wheelbarrow in the old Colier Mines. I'll work on the staff here until you bring me the refined ore.
What? You ALREADY gave me this item. Go away before I call Alfrega in here!
You have my blessing to enter these halls, child of another sun.

Your knowledge of the passage of time on this world is not great enough to enter the chapel beyond the door. Return to my in one day's time. If you obtain the knowledge of the past by that time, test yourself again.

Sickly from birth, Geraine IV, was taken by sisters who had stepped aside from the path and brought into a state that would forever sustain his body, soul and mind. Geraine in turn taught his people, but the sisters were not so foolish to not enter this state themselves. Many sleep, while in waking dreams, they think their time nears as a new singer raises her voice. But what of Geraine? His li...

You have proven to me that you are aware of what has transpired on this world. I give you my word that you shall see the halls beyond. Speak to my brothers and prove your worthiness to them. If you succeed the door to this chapel shall be yours to open evermore.

Child of another sun, your arrival shall herald a new age. I shall paint the world that you will create in images that shall grace these walls and hold the history within. My name is Hevk Loz, my name and painting are what endure from my life. This path was my choice. I, like my brothers, record history as it transpires and form it into art that can retain the knowledge of those times. You wish...
You must know of what has transpired before you may enter.

Three sons have driven the course of this world. From birth, each had a destiny not their own. Death for two and life for three. But only one has enjoyed the gift of life and of death given by the hands of those who once walked this world as our sisters. Which of the sons is this?

Three portraits show these sons. Choose the answer to my question wisely and you shall be given my blessing to pass into this chapel. Fail and I shall need you to rethink the purpose of your task within and ask that you return when you know more of this world.

greetings: Your vision swims. A wall of arid heat slams into your face, nearly  knocking you back. You blink, eyes dry and stinging.

You stand over a raw lava flow. The craggy walls are black stone, scarcely lit by the damask shadows from the liquid earth that rolls and flops beneath you. Down in the flow, figures are moving; constellations of stone, burning white from their inhospitable wading pool.

Your vision swims. For a moment, you seem to be sitting before an orb wreathed in sourceless, clean blue flame. Across from you sits a young man, his hands  knotted in anguish, his golden eyes flaring with anger. He speaks, the words flowing like the musical speech of the sea peoples of Ispar. Like an afterimage, the words come again a moment later, in your own tongue. "Someone has to do someth...
You hear words, as if from your own mouth, saying, "But what can you do?"
"I can do what's right. I'm going back with the next study group," he says, looking at you carefully. "Maybe... for good."
"How could you stay without being found as something... other?"

The man laughs, a bitter thing. "The same way we take our smug notes. We don't hide away in hunting blinds, you know. The life masters create flesh glamors for us. I've strolled through the markets, smelling the crops." He rubs his head, chin ducking with some faint embarrassment. "Being that short takes some getting used to."

Your vision swims. For a moment, you stand upon a crest, a frigid wind blowing icy knives through you, the land dropping away from your toes. You stumble back a step back from the precipice, dazzled by the light that skitters and skips across the snowy ground. Squinting, you raise a hand against the light of the dying sun to see...

Mount Esper. But not as you know it. Heat haze causes the sun to dance a jig as the cinder cone's lake boils white. On all sides, people and golems move about. A floating stone pallet is loaded with bars of greenish gold metal; a white-hot golem illuminates the entry shaft it trundles out of, the the echo filling the crater with the sound of a mountain falling down.

You turn to your left. An distinguished elderly woman looks to the west, the clean white light of the sun sharpening the crags of her cheeks. One hand rests on a platinum cane inscribed with fine, elegant calligraphy. Impossibly, you know her friend Ejan made it for her. And impossibly, you find yourself speaking words you cannot guess the meanings of; and you seem to hear it in Roulean. "Shaur...

"Time will come when these things will be again," the old woman smiles, her silver hair glinting in the waning sun. "Don't worry, my dear. When all has fallen down, you and I will be there to rebuild it, won't we?"

Her storm-grey eyes turn away to the west again, like ship sailing over sea. Distantly, she murmurs, "He's a good boy, Resanne. I believe in him. Unlike that daft Emperor who has us make him coins as the olthoi approach."

Your vision swims. For a moment, you see a group of men and women in white and purple. Somehow, you recognize the pattern of the robes; the colors of the Knorr Lyceum. The fabric is torn, sweat-stained, the anonymous faces floating above them white with fatigue. You are jostled and shoved into a group. You blink into the shadows. What..? The adepts raise their hands. Their eyes fill with radian...
You fall into the silvered tube of portalspace. It snakes and writhes, following safe courses through dimensions no eye can see, and magic can scarcely chart. And then...
The tunnel does not collapse as it always does. It peels open. You are weightless, formless, tumbling through an empty violet abyss. So tired... Sleep...
And something, somewhere, tears a little more...
Your vision swims.
Violet light.
Crackflash.
A column of blue light, vague as smoke, shimmers briefly in the distance.
Am I awake? He said we would --
There's something moving in the light...

A shell is nothing more than a device that allows us to traffic amongst your ilk. This body will return with me as its host. Our lives are eternal thanks to Aerbax.
Our goals near fruition much like the fruits of this farm, food is inessential only exposure to the energy source. Have your spirit make the journey.
Welcome to my farm. Have you come to join with the other compost?
Aerbax was correct exposure to the energy source heightens ability to withstand continued onslaught. Rejoice! I shall soon be impervious.

Do you think me to be as weak in magic as your own race?  Your magic is still too feeble to hurt me.
Ah, a drink!  Hee, hee!
I know the secret walled portal path, and I will let you enter it. See?
Ah, What's this?
That wasn't too nice. I'd like some sake, please.
Hmm. This doesn't look like sake.
Doesn't taste like sake either!
This doesn't smell like sake...
If I wanted coffee I would have asked for it.
Apple Juice! You must be kidding!
Ale? Thanks! I'm real partial to sake though. *hiccup*!
Didn't you understand me? I want sake, not cider!
Hah! This isn't sake, you fool.
I'd thank you for this drink, but I asked for sake.
You probably didn't hear me. I want sake, not red wine.
What is this? Doesn't look like sake....
And it's broken!  Now leave me alone!
I forgot to tell you...I'm a vegetarian!
Oh! That was fun!
Entering damn portal-space!
Have you read the note on the pedestal?
If that is what you desire, then fetch me a good drink of sake, and I shall grant your wish.  Otherwise, leave this place.  Hee, hee!
quest: There is nothing more you can do for me. Take your leave.
What is this? Yes...
%n's voice becomes tinny, altering between a deep human voice and distant alien tin voice.
I remember this time well. I was a puppet then, nothing more than an untrained mind with an incomprehensible amount of power. Untapped, raw...
It was during this time, taken from my home, stripped of the woman and child that I loved more than life itself, betrayed by my closest friend...that I decided HE must die.
And now I have succeeded.
%n begins to laugh, softly at first, the human voice most prevalent, then the tinny high-pitched laugh joins his human voice. The laugh grows into a maniacal twist of rage and alien sounds.
Thank you for showing me once again the meaning of my life.
%n sobs.
How I loved her. I miss her so. But look what I have done, what I have become. So many people dead by my hands, and the true savior of this world...dead.
What have I done? How could I have been duped in this way? Read this.
You may need to have it translated if you cannot understand Yalaini writing. But it is important you know.
So much supposition now cleared. I see the truth for the first time.
A tear falls from beneath Martine's mask and lands upon the letter.
How often I sat and wept over this letter that she would never read. Now I weep that if I can see her again I would not be the same man.
Thank you. You have helped me realize that there is still much to do. I must make amends. Go now, please.
chatter: Martine smiles at the people.
I am, Sir Candeth Martine.

Your blood, your sacrifice and your efforts have not gone unnoticed. It is time now that we make our final assault on Gaerlan. Once the base of this crystal is destroyed, I shall ascend to his citadel and destroy the navigation devices. This will cause the citadel to fall to ground, and then we shall take the fight into his home.

But before this, you must know that Asheron and Elysa have discovered the source of the continued entropy of the ley lines. In the place where Gaerlan combined the elemental lords a new elemental is growing. One with complete sentience.
It understands what it does, and means to live its life. We will need to prepare for battle against this creature as well, lest we defeat Gaerlan only to fall to another foe.
Asheron remains resolute in his study of the entity and will afford us with details when he can.
When the time is right I will alert you all of my attack. I wish you to witness my atonement. I will summon portals in my Retreat, the base of this crystal and  the capital cities.
I will make amends for my transgressions.
At Dryreach a portal into the Heart of the Lightning Cistern has opened.
Goodbye
Martine surveys the area.

A decisive victory. Gaerlan will not allow us to seize his power passively. There will be more resistance as we edge closer to taking his seat of power. New pitfalls will appear, and we must all be prepared.
With this second crystal shattered we have drawn much attention to our efforts. He will surely become desperate soon.

Asheron has informed me that he has noticed a horrible disturbance and fluctuation in the flow of mana beneath the fallen city of Yanshi. Elysa has sent a contingent of her Royal Guard around the city and is sending her most learned scholar to assist in the study of what transpires there.
Martine lets out a soft laugh.

It is possible that something has gone terribly wrong for Gaerlan already, but the result of this error could have larger implications for the world. Asheron has thus placed the discovery of these chambers upon me. I will inform you when the next has been found and furnish you with a way into the heart of the cistern.
Martine looks as though he will leave for moment, then he examines the gathered populace.

In my discussion with Asheron I learned something of importance. The Empyrean that are still trapped in portal space are sealed from him. He cannot see any of them. For the past several years he has struggled to pierce a veil that was put in place by the Virindi.

When the lifestones were created they did indeed have a dual purpose. They anchored our souls and bodies to this world, circumventing a death that was not natural. They were once the beacons that the Yalaini used to guide their ships. Powerful navigational devices would drive massive stone structures and great ships through the air to these waypoints.

When Elysa, and the other humans, emerged from the Olthoi caves victorious over the True Queen, Asheron altered the lifestones composition. What Gaerlan told me is true. The lifestones do siphon energy from us, feeding it to the Empyreans in portal space. A lifeline of sorts. Our sacrifice keeps an entire race alive in the whirl of portal space.

Asheron is a man that holds duty, above his own well being. He feels ultimately responsible for bringing us to this strange world and watches over us as best he can. It is also true that he feels as though he must aid his fellows, trapped there in the world between worlds. But we, have become his primary concern. Though one day he still hopes to free his people.

Asheron thought I held a key to freeing them, he thought that I had been beyond that wall deep within portal space. It was luck though and nothing more. My connection to the singularity through my symbiotic virindi was limited and dissipated quickly as I drove it out and fell into madness.
This news was a blow to him.
Martine shakes his head gently.
So much wasted time focusing my rage on him. So many wasted hours trying to find a way to destroy him, when in truth he only wanted to help me, help all of us.
The penitent man is humbled in the midst of a greater presence, not indignant.
I have much to atone for.
Martine arrives and surveys the destroyed crystal.
You have done well. This is our first assault against Gaerlan. I...
Martine pauses and looks to the floor. He breathes a heavy sigh and then looks at all the warriors, mages and archers assembled.
I was wrong. Moreover, I failed in bringing the peace for which I yearned. My desires to lead you, to kill Asheron, the harm I brought to Elysa to all of you, all results of Gaerlan's poison words.

Gaerlan appeared in my holding on Marae Lassel as I set the portals to the island here on Dereth. It was an unintentional breach of a Virindi shield that surrounds the Empyrean in portal space that freed him from his stasis. Upon seeing him I had intended to kill him, but he groveled well.
He offered me a gift in exchange for his life. My one true desire. My heart's true wish. A way home. The same way home that he now taunts us with. Ispar...

I believed him, I sheltered him, and now he has betrayed me. I have read what he has written, his diary, and his reports. They inspired me to visit a larger area of Auberean, looking for evidence of the portal destination from the Olthoi world.

My time there was brief, for the lands there are covered in blight, fungus, and Olthoi. They cluster together on the land and in cavernous burrows beneath the golden cities of the Yalain. Smaller winged Olthoi fill the sky. The fliers are too small to carry their larger cousins, and look too fragile to embark across the sea, I think they are of no true threat...now.

I made my way to Knorr. The Lyceum where Asheron taught his pupils. I searched for evidence of his magic at the place where the Olthoi invaded this world. It is a trick that I learned, when I closed the portals from Ispar to Dereth. I expected to find that it was Asheron's magic that was left, but I found something else...
I found traces of Gaerlan's magic at the arrival point. It was Gaerlan...his folly, his miscalculation. He moved the portal from their world, when he tried to trap Asheron there. He did not close it.
The Yalaini have held Asheron accountable for this folly and made him a criminal, even though he has saved his race...saved our race. And I meant to kill him...
Martine pauses and looks at the assembled crowd.

A little boy, a little prince, came to me. He asked me why I tried to kill his uncle. I could not find an answer to his question. I searched within myself to find one, to tell him that Asheron had caused me all of this pain. But Asheron did not bring this upon me. Alayne sold me to the Mosswarts, and the Virindi.

greetings: The recent rise of arts and crafts on the land of your xuta has inspired my siblings and I to take up the noble practice of the fine arts ourselves. My name is Kahuiura, Aun Artisan in Arcane Ointment.
quest: As with many of the other crafted goods my siblings accept, I too suffer from a surplus. Please, give us time to use what we have. Perhaps in a week we will have run our stock down low enough and I will be able to accept goods from you.

I am sure your intentions at heart were well meaning, the quality of this product are far from healthy. Were one to apply it to his mane, the mane would likely corrode and recede. Perhaps you Isparians find being bald and burnt attractive, but we of the Aun Xuta certainly do not.
Surely you jest! Are you certain this is crafted from the claw of a siraluun? It smells as if you simply followed behind one, captured its leavings and added some essence of lapyan to mask its color.
This gel is my particular favorite. I find the shade of green it colors my hair to be most agreeable with my personality.

Admittedly it does not take much skill to crush something with a stone and slab. However, it takes a keen eye and sense of touch to know how to mix a gel with the appropriate consistency. This, for example, is a bit too chalky to be of much use. Perhaps the little ones could amuse themselves by flinging it at the Hea on the lower plains.
You are making leaps and bounds in improvement. The spirits must smile upon you.
The spirit of the Siraluun is indeed embodied in this gel. Vibrant and powerful, yet fluid and malleable.
You are nearing perfection in your art. I am honored to have been a part in your learning.

This was made from the claw of one of the most dangerous breeds of Siraluun. Those who can withstand the sting of this gel upon their scalp will be rewarded with great luck. I am honored that you would gift this to me.

Sorry about making you come this far, but we can't be giving away our prized secrets to just ANYONE...besides, if the Hea knew of my whereabouts, they'd kidnap me and my brother in a second.

Here to make your weapon, are you? Well, if you've made it this far, I'm sure you've earned it. Any friend of the Aun, I say...Now, if you've bought a talisman from that miserly old brother of mine, I'll be happy to exchange it for your weapon.
Just a moment...

I'm afraid that after you leave this place, you will not be able to return to visit me for a month or so--the Hea are ever vigilant, and we must do our best to keep this plac...

One final note, unlike my father and the others who reside within the walls of Timaru, I bear no grudges to those who may have acted against the Tonk. My father would say that I am foolish for this belief.
Aun Hareltah regards the totem gravely.

This is a work of Aun magic. You say you took this from a Hea? I have little wonder. This is a Totem of Tanae, the Forest, who wraps the world in his green arms, whispers deep wisdoms, and, on our world of Ezheret-Hazahtu, shelters our people from the great sisters Wind and Rain, as they eternally grapple for the love of Father Sea.

This is the handicraft of Aun Shimauri. You may find him at the base of the plateau, to the east of Timaru. I charge you who have recovered this great medicine to bring it to Shimauri. May Wind, as she winds her paths about the world, speed you there.

This is a work of Aun magic. You say you took this from a Hea? I have little wonder. This is a Totem of Audetaunga, the Mountain, she who stands proud and immovable, tempering even her great and fickle daughter spirits Wind and Rain.

It is Volkama who travels between Mother Mountain and Father Sea. It is he who tempers his father's great power such that Tanae and Tonk may sing and drum under Hazahtu.

"I greet you, honored kin. I am glad for your coming. Wharu rises across the plateau, and we are pressed. All our stones have been broken by the Ispar xuta, and Wind whispers that the insects are brooding a new queen."

The Tah of Aun gazes deep into your eyes, his hand clutching at your arm like a lifeline.
Aun Hareltah nods at you briefly.
"Ah, %s. The slayer of Temepuh, who hunted our people at the behest of the atua ngamaru."

"I trust the Totem of Palenqual serves you well? Wharu rises, and we require its service. His children skitter across this land in increasing numbers. Now is the time for all Aun, and all friends of Aun, to stand against him."
"For my people, this is divine mandate. From what I have heard of your Elysa, called saint by some, it should be for the Ispar xuta as well."
Aun Hareltah regards you with some respect.
"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Kahmaula by repairing the northernmost of the stone circles."

"I only wish your efforts had not been obviated by others of your xuta. Wharu is free across the whole upland Palenqual. It is not safe beyond these walls, though the Aun xuta would be grateful for your help in this holy war."
"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Gehaua by repairing the northeastern stone circle."

"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Laiaua by repairing the southwestern stone circle."
"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Aanaua by repairing the northwestern stone circle."

I only wish your efforts had not been obviated by others of your xuta. Wharu is free across the whole upland Palenqual. It is not safe beyond these walls, though the Aun xuta would be grateful for your help in this holy war."

The Tah of Aun tucks the totem into his medicine pouch, and looks you in the eye.
"Later, I will join Temenpuh's power to my buadren, that he may in death redeem his life. But now I will reward you, with that thing most precious to the Aun."
"This is the Stave of Palenqual - the living totem of this island itself, given to us by spirits of this place who call themselves Deru. It may be turned into a powerful force for good or ill."
"But you have difficult choices to make before it will serve you, %s. My note will explain."
Aun Hareltah regards the egg warily.
It is a very dangerous thing to have in one's possession, blood as my blood. Still, do as you think is best, Queenslayer. I will support you.
Aun Hareltah looks at you in frank amazement.
"Gracious, %s! My kin, you never cease to amaze me. To have slain such a creature more than once! It is beyond me. But I cannot reward you with more than I already have."
"Here, let me prepare this totem for your wall as well, and reaffirm your status as Queenslayer."

It is well. I grant you knowledge.

Aun Hareltah bows respectfully.
"I greet you, mighty %s. You have slain the queen, and granted us relief from the affliction of Wharu. The Aun xuta owes a debt of gratitude to you, as yet unpaid."
"Let me examine the head of that accused beast, and I shall reward you as is proper."
Aun Hareltah cocks his head to the side, as if listening to something inaudible.

"Wind has brought tidings of your deeds, friend. She whispers, '%s has slain the brutal Temepuh, who calls himself Temenua as he hunts your people on the upland. Temenua, who sheds your xuta's blood at the behest of the soulless atua ngamaru.'"

"This deed is a fiery blaze upon your keh, Isparian, even if you know it not. Should you desire the Stave of Palenqual, give me Temepuh's totem. Now we are pressed, and it is time for us to release the magic of Tonk."

"But if you do not desire this magical stave, if you would rather have the ranged kalindan or the fighting staff called hoeroa, hold your hand for now. I will only reward you once for the butcher's death."
Aun Hareltah glances at you sharply.
I do not know your name, and thanks to your people, Wharu's children have overrun the whole of Palenqual. I do not have the time to chat with tourists. Make your name known to me, and we will talk.
Aun Hareltah looks at you quizzically.

"But, %s, you have already claimed the bounty of Temepuh's name. Does not the totem of Palenqual serve you well? Please, use it to hunt and kill our enemies, before we are driven in to Timaru herself!"
Hrm... so you claim to have slain Temepuh?
Aun Hareltah places the totem in the palm of his hand, and closes his eyes. After a brief moment, he shakes his head and hands the totem back to you.
No, I fear you are attempting to deceive me. Your keh would sing of this victory quite plainly - it does not. You should return this to the one who actually killed the scourge of the uplands.
Aun Hareltah looks at the egg in shock.

How can you bring this into Timaru at such a time? This is a very dangerous thing to have in one's possession at any moment, but when Wharu's power is at its height, it may draw his children here! I will dispose of it, and be glad I do not have the Nualuan run you out.
%s, bloodied and battered after the battle in the Royal Hive, presents the stern Aun Hareltah with the head of the Olthoi Queen.
The Tah of Aun holds the head of the Queen before him, and bows in respect to the might of Wharu.
"Great anima of decay," he intones solemnly, "bear no ill will towards %s, who slew your servant respectfully."
"From this point forward, %s shall be known and honored among all Aun as Queenslayer."
"Further," Hareltah says with a smile, "%s shall be known as my adopted kin!"
He pulls the startled %s into a warm embrace, as the Aun whisper among themselves. "...not of Tonk!" Aun Dreganaua is heard to protest.

"You have saved this xuta," Hareltah says gravely, his powerful voice carrying over the susurrations of the crowd. "For this, for all your experiences on the path to defeating the Queen, the hardest road known in these strange lands, I recognize you."
%s's party has been granted forty million experience points!

"Finally," Hareltah says, "there is the matter of this totem in my hands. I will prepare it for you with my own hands, my kin, that you may hang from your wall. With its power, your house shall be mighty among Tonk and Isparian, and none shall wash the earth from under it."
Aun Hareltah embraces %s again with tears in his eyes, and returns the head of the queen.
"Hrm... so you claim to have slain the spawn of Wharu?"
Aun Hareltah lays his hand lightly on the Queen's head, and closes his eyes. After a brief moment, he shakes his head and gently pushes it back towards you.
Aun Hareltah turns the tessera over in his hands, but shakes his head regretfully.
I am sorry. You have already gained five skill points from the tesserae. I can teach you nothing more.
Aun Hareltah smiles as you approach, and strides forward to embrace you, but you sense foreboding in the Tah of Aun.
"I greet you as my honored kin. It is good to see you again, Queenslayer %s. As always, it is an honor to have you visit Timaru."
He pauses, staring off to the north for a moment, then adds;

Aun Hareltah nods at you kindly.

"I trust the Totem of Palenqual serves you well? Perhaps you should move to the north - our drummers are besieged."
"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Kahmaula by repairing the northernmost of the stone circles. Well met."
"I only wish your efforts were not being sabotaged by the others of your xuta. Wharu's influence waxes to the north of Timaru."
"Yes... your name has been mentioned to me. You are %s, who aided Aun Gehaua by repairing the northeastern stone circle. Well met."

greetings: Welcome to our storage facility.  We are using this Empyrean place as a warehouse for crystals and materials Nuhmudira needs for her research and instructing us.
quest: Did you let someone know what happened here?
I thought you were going to the surface to let others know of this?  Take this crystal back, I cannot take it now.
I cannot get up yet. Did you bring Valara crystals?  Nuhmudira will certainly need them now! Someone hit me from behind... The crystals have been taken, we have been robbed!

Ow, my head! I was knocked down... the crystal supplies were stolen! I did not see who it was.  All right, I'll take the Valara...  you go through the surface portal and alert the guard.  There was a student here a minute before you, I sent him there also.
Thank you for assisting us recently. We do not need any more of that quite yet
Good, one of the students sent you. Nuhmudira requires this. Thank you.

Now if you would be willing to obtain some Valara crystal, you can find it nearby.  This Empyrean facility is adjacent to another complex which is guarded by Golems.  Some hold a crystal known as Valara crystal.  Its properties are useful to Nuhmudira in her research. The portal to that complex is just down the corridor. Return directly here through the portal you find in the dungeon.

greetings: The dying Tumerok casts a portal to the Hebian-To Advance Camp dungeon as it falls!

Thank you! I have been waiting for more of these gems. I will see this gets to Nuhmudira. You may be aware that Iolite is said to increase spiritual insight and help in seeing both sides of an issue more clearly.

My fellow student who you obtained this from may also have told you that Chrysoberyl compound is needed.  The portal over there will take you to what we call the Spirit Cell.  Within you should find some Chrysoberyl compound.  Please bring some to me.
Hello. Have you spoken to any of my colleagues in some of the towns?
quest: At present, I have a sufficient quantity of that.

I am happy you have succeeded. Now, I am sure you have been informed as to how important Daichroic crystals are to Numhudira's research. There are several ancient mines in which Daichroic crystals are yet stored. There is a portal on a hill northwest of the town of Holtburg.  From that portal you may begin this final pursuit. You will discover direct portals to the mine at its destination- you...

greetings: The recent rise of arts and crafts on the land of your xuta has inspired my siblings and I to take up the noble practice of the fine arts ourselves. My name is Nireeura, Aun Artisan in Pin and Pitch.
quest: Your pins are a boon to our xuta. We use the pins we make, as well as the ones you and your xuta have supplied to us, for many tasks. However, we only need so many. Extras would sadly be put to waste. Please return to me in a week and I may be able to take more pins off of your hands.
This could hardly be called a pin. Look! The claw this was crafted from was not properly dried, the feathers not properly plucked and the claws not properly cleaned.
As my mother always told me, if something is worth doing, do it right. Obviously you felt that this wasn't worth doing, otherwise the pin would have been sharp, and the grip sturdy.
Your efforts have almost done justice to the majesty this fine bird once represented.

A quality pin will withstand multiple uses. It will be strong enough to hold the hide of a mattekar upon the wall while sharp enough to cut the hide of an armoredillo. Unfortunately, this is not a quality pin.
You are making leaps and bounds in improvement. The spirits must smile upon you.
The Kithless Siraluun has long been hunted and revered. Its ferocity is reflected nicely in the spike of this pin.
You are nearing perfection in your art. I am honored to have been a part in your learning.

This pin is magnificent. The details on the head spiral down the claw to the tip of the pin. Each etched line speaks of the thought and care you put into crafting this item. I am honored to be receiving such a fine piece of workmanship.

As a gesture of friendship, I will create a fine matihao for any unarmed combat master who brings me a Strand Siraluun claw.

greetings: %s has struck a mortal blow to Amanua. As the Tumerok War Chief falls to the ground motionless, his armor snaps free.
Your blood will serve as gravy for my pet's meal.
You should have thought of the consequences of this action, Isparian.
Mighty spirits watch over my soul. What hope have you to penetrate their protection?

Niarltah's voice echoes over the land, "Muldaveus, we must flee. The Isparians have overrun our position. Come Morgluuk and Torgluuk, we will take you to the safety of our hidden fortress. Amanua, Fostok, get in here and clean up this tripe!"
Isparians! Firm the breach and call reinforcements. We can end their lives here and now.
Let the blood of the ancient fuel my anger and drive my weapons straight to your heart.
The spirits of the land forsake you. Make your peace quickly, my wrath will be swift.
This amuses me in many ways. I will use your bones to call the spirits.
That hits the spot. So, Tekapuapuh. He's this melon-headed buhka -- an idiot boy. Goes out for his first hunt alone, and finds one of those death-bringer Wharu.
'Cept he calls it 'Putiputi!' It's no ladybug! I still remember it... he comes into town, RIDING the Wharu. Nearly flattened the center of Ahurenga.
He's puh now -- outcast. Lives on the tip of the delta out west of here. I hope he stays there. Anyway, thanks for the ale, human.
You haven't heard the story, human? Fetch me an ale, and I'll tell you.
I'd tell you more but, ah, I'm a little parched. Need a little ale.
chatter: That melon-headed buhka. Riding a Wharu into the center of town. I still can't believe it!
A puh like that shouldn't have been allowed to stay on the island.
If he ever shows up in town again, I'll make him and his 'Putiputi' sorry...

greetings: You could have only claimed this off the corpse of one of my kinsmen. Wharu take you and your ilk!
Zhtufu! Go!
A Virindi jewel! Finally, those floating demons are getting their comeuppance! You should take this to Mareura--he's offering a fine bounty for these.
A Virindi jewel! Finally, those floating demons are getting their comeuppance! But I am a crafter, not a collector.
quest: I heard about what you did to poor Mareura!  Gleefully presenting him with the pendant of one of our own slain brothers...slain by YOU, no doubt! How dare you approach me after that? I would never cooperate with one who has slain my kin.
Get away from me!
You do not deserve anything from these, from me, my son, or any of the Tonk for what you have done!
You do not deserve anything for this, from me, my son, or any of the Tonk for what you have done!

How I miss the birds of my home world! My brother Ihipura once taught me to invoke their animas for aid. If you bring me a small bundle of feathers from the Siraluun that roam the island, I will ask Siraluun to help me make a special headdress for you. Even better, if you combine five of the smaller bundles into a larger one, I will make a lovely dress. Here, add the bundles to this special bag...
I can only work with feathers, friend.  Not with this.

By fighting our enemy, you show that you are a friend of the Aun.  Take this trophy to Mareura--he will reward you.
