You must collect three more bundles of Badlands Siraluun Feathers for me to have enough to weave a dress for you.
You must collect two more bundles of Badlands Siraluun Feathers for me to have enough to weave a dress for you.
You are almost there. If you add one more bundle of Badlands Siraluun Feathers to this bag, I will have enough to weave a dress for you.
I have no use for this item in my art. However, my son, who you may have met on your way to Timaru, is a practicing artisan. He may find this to be useful. Please bring it to him.
Thank you, but I only work in feathers. If you were to perhaps bring this item to Mareura, he may be able to help you out.
chatter: I wonder how my brother Ihipura is faring in Ahurenga?
I'll weave a fine garment for anyone who brings me feathers from the Kithless Siraluun.

greetings: The dying Tumerok casts a portal to the Cragstone Middle Guard Camp dungeon as it falls!

The recent rise of arts and crafts on the land of your xuta has inspired my siblings and I to take up the noble practice of the fine arts ourselves. My name is Ihmenaura, Aun Artisan in Feather and Claw.
quest: We must forever be cautious of the land we live in. Hunt the Siraluun too frequently and their numbers dwindle. The spirits demand that respect be paid to these fowl before further can be accomplished. Several passings of the sun must be made before the spirits will allow me to accept another token from you.

I would think that one with hands as small and nimble as those of your xuta, one would be capable of crafting this brush. And yet, I have seen better workmanship come from the clumsy hands of an Obeloth.

It seems you have much left to learn about the profession of brush making. Look at this brush! The feathers of the Siraluun barely cling to the stock of it. At least you made an attempt, and that alone merits a reward.
Your efforts have almost done justice to the majesty this fine bird once represented.
Practice and skill have always been the corner stones of quality. Your efforts, while still far from being a strong supporting key stone, are building in strength with each attempt you make.

Your attention to detail is surprising! The intricate lines and details on the handle of this brush are marvelous. Unfortunately, the bristles themselves lack in quality, which in turns reduces the beauty of the brush on the whole.

This mighty bird has been transformed into a stunning piece of art. You have learned much to have created something such as this, but do not let my praise swell your pride. You still have much to learn.
You are nearing perfection in your art. I am honored to have been a part in your learning.
Your efforts have culminated in this, a brush so fine and detailed that my skills are put to shame. I humbly thank you for this and I look forward to seeing your future efforts.

greetings: Young Arantah's eyes narrow as he reads furiously.
...What? What is this? No! They said... they said I was the only one! This can't be true! What does this mean?
Arantah crushes the journal in his fist, then methodically begins to tear it to pieces.
They lied to me.
His eyes glower a dark, thunderhead purple.
As the pieces of Martine's journal flutter towards the ground, they burst into flames.
I'm more powerful than this stupid man-thing. The first. The best. I'll show them. Them and their man-puppet.
quest: Hea Arantah tells you, "You're %s! They told me what you did - you killed that poacher Ralirea! Give me his figurine. Quickly, quickly!"
Ah! I can tell by the flickering of your keh that you have broken one of the Aun's precious rocks in the last few weeks.
My atual arutoa brothers like to see the wharu running free across this land.
So, this is the face of one of the stonebreakers the Aun hate, eh? A drink to the enemy of my enemy.
My atual arutoa brothers like to see the wharu running free. They collect them, you know.
Young Arantah belches softly, and you catch the fetid odor of a poor imitation of distilled Empyrean dew.
Wow, great! Ha ha! I warned them not to send their hunters on to my plateau!

Young Arantah clutches his fist around the little figurine, so tightly the veins in his wrist stand in relief. His eyes flash violet, and after a muffled crunch, clay dust begins to trickle through his fingers. He looks up at you and grins boyishly.
That was a trick my friends taught me, way back when I was driven from Timaru. I could do the same to your head, you know.
I'm kidding! You've been a friend the Hea, and I reward my friends. Here...
Arantah places his hand on your forehead and his eyes glow blue-white. You feel... enlightened...
You have gained a skill point!
Ha! Yes, this was given to you by Aun Kahmaula, right? He threw stones at me. I was only ten... I needed that bread to live, damn it!
Arantah's eyes flare with inchoate rage, casting violet light upon the ground. Around you, the residents cringe and hold their breath... But a smile breaks across his face.
Well, I'm glad to see him set back, anyway. Here. A gift from my atual arutoa allies.
From the medicine pouch of Aun Gehaua, I see? Great! I got this from my atual arutoa friends. My warriors and I often raided this area in the early years of our alliance.
I wonder whatever happened to that damned portal mage of theirs? He cost me a nice wrap. Did you know human children make the softest leather?
Ah, this still resonates with the keh of Aun Tanaua, the old fool who talks to rocks.
Anyway, here's a little something the atual arutoa gave me. I hear they use this a lot themselves, as a stop on their way to talk to those turtle-nosed freaks in the south.
Aun Laiaua's mark is on this. He always seemed like a dull old worry-wart to me. Going on and on about the how the atual arutoa were soulless and all. Stupid.
The Aun never thought that the atual arutoa have no anima because they ARE the anima of the universe. At least, that's how I understood what they told me.
Young Arantah's eyes glitter with mad glee at the sight of the figurine.
Aun Aanaua has cursed you! Wonderful! This means Wharu runs free, and Aun are pressed! Now is the time for me to release my raiders!
Now THIS gift of the atual arutoa - you'll LIKE this one! Now go.
Young Arantah glowers at you.

What do you want, man-thing? Be quick, and do not lie, for the atual arutoa have given me many eyes to see the truth with. Annoy me at your own risk, for my anger is quick and my power great... As the Aun have learned.
Young Arantah looks annoyed - which seems to be his natural state.
What? Can't you see I'm busy? I have many responsibilities here!
That Aun hunter, for one. What's his name?
Arantah belches loudly as Nyrinua calls over, "Ralirea, my Tah."
Ralirea, yes. Don't CORRECT me, Nyri.
Anyway, this old Aun dustongue - Ralirea - poaches the gromnies of my plateau! If someone would kill him, and bring me that figurine he wears within a day as proof...
A suspicious scowl lumbers across the young Tumerok chieftain's face.
Hea Arantah tells you, "Now wait. My memory isn't what it used to be since the atual arutoa... bettered me, but I do remember your face, %s."

Hea Arantah tells you, "Yes... I rewarded you for Ralirea's death before. That means this figurine must be a fake! You dare try to fool the mighty friend of the atual? Go away before I use my Grip on you!"

Ha! Your keh is all wrong! You were not the one who slew Ralirea this day - someone else did, and gave you his totem. Tell your friend to come and collect my reward himself, I am too important to deal with errand-runners.
What? Are you KIDDING? I already rewarded you for breaking the stones of the north in the last three months. Flee from me now, beggar, or I'll use my Grip on you!
Arantah throws the clay totem at you!
What? Are you KIDDING? I already rewarded you for breaking the stones of the northeast in the last three months. Flee from me now, beggar, or I'll use my Grip on you!
What? Are you KIDDING? I already rewarded you for breaking the stones of the southeast in the last three months. Flee from me now, beggar, or I'll use my Grip on you!
What? Are you KIDDING? I already rewarded you for breaking the stones of the southwest in the last three months. Flee from me now, beggar, or I'll use my Grip on you!
What? Are you KIDDING? I already rewarded you for breaking the stones of the northwest in the last three months. Flee from me now, beggar, or I'll use my Grip on you!
chatter: Hea Arantah looks around his town brazenly.
Hea Arantah belches softly.
Hea Arantah's arm moves suddenly, too quickly to see, and snatches a small flying insect out of the air. He hums a merry child's tune, and methodically pulls its wings and legs off.
The youthful voice of Hea Arantah mutters, "When, my friends? Soon? ...Very well, I understand." He seems to be talking to the fountain, though his eyes are glazed and glowing faintly.
Hea Arantah's youthful voice shouts, "We have freedom, my friends! The islands are open to us!" The residents of the town hoot a loud Tumerok cheer.
Hea Arantah wipes spilled liquor from his lips. His voice cracks as he cries, "Aren't we mighty? Don't the Aun cower in their beds in fear of us?" The residents cheer again... somewhat uncertainly.
All at once, the youthful voice of Hea Arantah screams across the square. While the visiting Isparians look at him in confusion, the Hea bury themselves in their work.
Arantah gasps, clutching at his head. His eyes are shut tight, but a painful violet light burns out from behind his eyelids.
"WHAT? What did I do? Yes... I understand. The upland patrols. Reinforced. At once, Collector. Please... my xuta is watching."
The light ceases like a snuffed candle. The Tah of Hea staggers.
"Warriors!" he calls, rather weakly. "I want raiding parties on the plateau at once! Temenua isn't doing his task... our friends are angry!"

greetings: Please, friend -- take this to Aun Mariona, as I have asked.

Alas! That tyrant Bernawa. Not only did he murder my friend Hea Rifona, he is keeping me from my true love! Some day he will live to feel my fury! Oh Mariona, oh Woe! Take this small gift...I will not need them soon.
And now friend, stay with me no longer, for I must be alone.
She has not forgotten me! I am awash with joy. My hope can still live on. Please, take these gifts with my thanks.
quest: Many thanks, my friend, but I couldn't trouble you again with the affairs of my heart so soon. Perhaps tomorrow I will find the courage to contact my beloved again.

Greetings! Could you do me a favor, please? I planned to meet my beloved, Aun Mariona, but I am afraid that my Hea brethren have learned of our romance and are watching over me. Could you take her this note? I dare not go meet her myself, lest they slay us together. You will find her in the redwood groves almost directly north from the city your kind calls Bluespire. I have written the directio...
chatter: Alas! My Mariona!

greetings: These are the treasures of our friends, the Atual arutoa! How dare you murder them and then wave their belongings in my face?
Be off with you.
quest: How dare you show your face to me again, Virindi Killer? I shall not even speak to you.
Leave me be! I'll have nothing to do with you, Virindi Killer.

I will reward you for for Carenzi Stalker pelts, Timber Siraluun claws, and Elaniwood Golem hearts. Also, our Aun brothers must be taught a lesson--if you deliver one of their pendants to me I will reward you handsomely.
This little thing!  I couldn't find a use for this.  Perhaps you could find a buyer for this over in the Isparian towns.
Give Merlonna my regards.  There is no reason why our kinds cannot work together.
Give Shalon my regards.  There is no reason why our kinds cannot work together.
Give Ling Xiao my regards.  There is no reason why our kinds cannot work together.
Such a beautiful specimen--thank you. These will fetch a fine price when I journey to sell them on the mainland.
I'm always looking for more.  Come back should you find another.
I recognize this pendant! The one who wore this was once the dearest of my family...how I wish he had listened to reason. But then...times change, and so must we all.  Here is your reward.
Now please leave me, I have many problems to dwell upon.
I'm not interested in Strand Siraluun claws, but I know Hea Ihipura would be happy to help you with this.
He should be loitering around here somewhere.
I haven't seen one of these since I left the highlands!
I've already got more of those than I need. Perhaps the Aun are still collecting these. I wouldn't bother if I were you--the Aun are notorious misers.
You have harmed Wharu!
I'll have nothing to do with this slaughter.
Ah...feathers from the magnificent Kithless Siraluun.  You must have hunted for many moons to come by these.
These are too precious.  I can't take them from you.
The embroidery on this bag is of Aun workmanship.
Bah!  You may have it back.
chatter: Any day now, and I'll have collected enough to fund my trip to the mainland.
I'll reward handsomely for Carenzi pelts, Siraluun claws, Drudge charms, and Golem hearts--but only the right kinds.

greetings: The dying Tumerok casts a portal to the Cragstone Reinforcements Camp dungeon as it falls!
Nooooooooooo. Uh uh. No takebacks. You keep it!
quest: Thanks again, buhdi, and enjoy the Panaq!
Did you play with the splashy-pots like I did?
Putiputipuh's all full now. But thanks anyway!
C'mon! Feed Putiputipuh the onga!
Hey! I already gave you a Panaq! You're forgering stuff at me!
Naah. Not this piece! I need Pah!
Hey, you already gave me one of these! Where'd you get another one? Now I need Ahna.
Hey, you already gave me one of these! Is this a cheap Aun knockoff? I need Naq now.
See, Ahna fits into Pah like this--er, something like that. More or less. Um. Now I need Naq!
And then Naq goes into Ahna like, um... This! And here you go! Thanks again for your help!
Not this! Now I need Ahna!
If you find the pieces I left behind, I'll put my old Panaq together for you!
Go feed Putiputipuh!
Did you go to the hidey-hole! I think I left my onga near one of the bubble-pots there! Those onga are the only thing Putiputipuh will eat!
You got the onga! I'll let you feed Putiputipuh all by yourself! It's fun!
It's the Pah! You don't know what do with this? Silly buhka! I'll help you then. Bring me Ahna next.
Oh, my poor Putiputipuh! Nothing else matters!
Not this! First I need Pah!
Oh, my poor Putiputipuh! She is so sad!
Oh, my poor Putiputipuh! It makes me feel so bad!
If only you were mightier, you could help me and my Putiputipuh!
Oh, man! You can help me! My beloved Putiputipuh, she's not happy. She needs special onga from where I found her!
I dropped my stuff in the hidey hole where I found her. It's all the way to the east, straight east from here, right until you hit a BIIIG wall.
I set up a magic portal to the hidey-hole. Here, I'll give you the password.
chatter: They call me a 'melon-headed buhka,' but that's just because they're jealous of my mask!
Why are you looking at Putiputipuh that way?! PUTIPUTIPUH'S A GOOD GRUBBY!
No, Putiputipuh! Bad Putiputipuh!
Look, she did a trick! Good Putiputipuh! You're such a very smart Putiputi!
I tried giving her onga. She must just like my special onga, the ones I left where I found her.
I was all itchy before, but now I'm better!
We may both be 'puh,' Putiputi, but we still have each other.

greetings: The dying Tumerok casts a portal to the Cragstone Advance Camp dungeon as it falls!

quest: Aun Firanauri regards you grudgingly.
You have broken one of the precious stones that keep Wharu away. But you are the Queenslayer and adopted kin of Aun Hareltah, so...I suppose you must have had cause to do so.
Aun Firanauri opens his mouth to bark at you, but stiffens as he notices the head of the Queen peering blankly from your pack.
You are the Queenslayer %s. Aun Hareltah has heard of you from Wind. I am to tell you that he wishes to see you at once.
If I may be so bold, I would recommend that you have all those who assisted in the fight with Whatru's offspring join you in fellowship, so you may share what our Tah wishes to grant you.
Aun Firanauri scowls as you approach and grips his buadren tighter. You open your mouth to ask for access to Timaru, but he bellows over your voice.
Zhtufu, bahka! You have broken our stones and made Wharu mightier. Get you gone from my sight, before I gut you as a fish and place your head upon the rampart!
Aun Firanauri eyes you warily.
So, you seek access to Timaru, Isparian? You have not offended the xuta recently, so I will grant you passage. But do not harry our works against Wharu, or this town will be closed to you!

greetings: The recent rise of arts and crafts on the land of your xuta has inspired my siblings and I to take up the noble practice of the fine arts ourselves. My name is Pitamaura, Aun Artisan in Spike and Blade.
quest: I encourage your zeal in the fine art of shear crafting. Unfortunately, my siblings cannot dull your blades fast enough. If, in a week's time, you still have scissors you wish to donate to our practice of artistry, please bring them to me and I will happily reward you for them.
An admirable attempt. I recommend you work on sharpening your skills further before thinking you worthy of another reward from me.
These shears are obviously deficient. A golem's hand could cut more than these blades could.
Your efforts have almost done justice to the majesty this fine bird once represented.
Practice and skill have always been the corner stones of quality. Your efforts, while still far from being a strong supporting key stone, are building in strength with each attempt you make.

This is perhaps amongst your finest work. The only issue is the handle of these shears suffers from a lack of creativity and design. But, I suppose they function, and that alone should count for something.

This mighty bird has been transformed into a stunning piece of art. You have learned much to have created something such as this, but do not let my praise swell your pride. You still have much to learn.
You are nearing perfection in your art. I am honored to have been a part in your learning.
Your efforts have culminated in this, shears so fine and detailed that my skills are put to shame. I humbly thank you for this and I look forward to seeing your future efforts.

greetings: The dying Tumerok casts a portal to the Hebian-To Reinforcements Camp dungeon as it falls!
%s, you have struck me down, but my memory is long and like your death mine is not the final release. I will return to carve your hide, %s!
Yes, you should have stepped to the right and not the left.
You were coddled too much as a child.
Your intrusion shall be as short-lived as your life!
You strike like a frightened child!

But...how could you have come by this pendant? No Aun would willingly give up his pendant, given to him at birth. You must have slain one of my brothers! Bukha!  Get away from me, before I call upon Audetaunga to smother you!
Zhtufu! Go!
quest: When you murdered one of my brothers you proved yourself to be an enemy of the Aun.  I shall not even speak to you.
I am interested in collecting Olthoi claws, Rabid Carenzi Pelts, and Vapor Golem hearts. I will especially reward you for yellow Virindi jewels--those floating demons must be purged from our island!
I have no need for this trifle.
Thank you! These will stand out wonderfully in my collection.
Thank you!  These will stand out wonderfully in my collection.
Our fight against Wharu is ever present. Thank you for helping us in this struggle.
Kithless Siraluun feathers!  You must take these to Aun Whethura. He has been gifted in many ways and will be able to craft a beautiful item for you.
No thanks, I don't have any feathers to put into this bag.
Whethura must have taken a shine to you, to offer to craft a dress for you.
Kithless Siraluun Feathers!  You must take these to Aun Whethura.  He has been gifted in many ways and will be able to craft a beautiful item for you.
This is a fine prize! Perhaps those Virindi demons will learn to stay away from places they are not wanted.
Bring me more, and I shall reward you in kind.
You mean there are more Virindi than those just on our island? Tonk save us! However, my first priority is to purge Palenqual's shores of the floating demons, who are known for their yellow jewels.
Thank you!  I have always enjoyed making weapons from the claws of the fearsome Siraluun. Let me make you a weapon out of this claw.

If you happen upon another of these claws and you do not wish for a weapon, I suggest you visit Merlonna Farel in the town of Bluespire. When last I ventured into that town, she mentioned in passing that she knew of someone who was looking for these claws as well.
I have no need for this trifle. I would recommend you seek out the son of Whethura. The young ura is eagerly awaiting tasks, I suggest you provide him some.
Siraluun Feathers!  You must take these to Aun Whethura.  He has been gifted in many ways and will be able to craft a beautiful item for you.
chatter: I have put out a bounty on Wharu and the Atua ngamaru. I will reward anyone who brings me proof of their deaths.
I'll reward handsomely for Carenzi pelts, Siraluun claws, Drudge charms, and Golem hearts--but only the right kinds.

greetings: In death I should find freedom, but the shackle holds still.
Your stature is smaller, your bones more brittle and your flesh more maleable. You are not of our masters legion, so your death comes with rewards...my thoughts returned.
Within the Blood I have bathed. Your fledgling magics are piteous.
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Why do you fight me?"
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "I do not understand why you attacked me..."
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Who are you? Help!"
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "My forge... Where is my forge?"
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Shaura..."
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Yes, Mistress? I come."
chatter: Hanaurel...
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Written thoughts - letter..."
Kall ama te fen? Reann au..?
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Who was it for? Where do I..?"
Etah si au hisenaa!
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Why can I not recall!"
Zorn... zorn...
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "All gone, all gone..."
Au virinaa! Au... baeaa?
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "I breathe not! I... am not... slain?"
Ai, Metresa?
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Yes, Mistress?"
Suvani hasode, Metresa, tamaa Dar Hallae.
In your mind, the dusty voice of Ejan whispers, "Yes. The Shadows remain below, Mistress, at the Old Ring."

greetings: Wealth...wealth...
More miners...more miners needed...
You will serve...the Hope Bringer
Work...must mine...for Cambarth
Tired...
Release...me...
The Lord of Decay groans as it collapses in a heap of bone, "We will drive you away!"
The Lord of Decay groans as it collapses in a heap of bone, "Our great armies - blown away like sand! Who shall remain to defend our proud fortresses?"
Lord Cambarth bids you...mine
Must do...as Cambarth commands...
Serve...Cambarth
The sun seems to dim, and you can see your own breath for an instant.

The wind brings tidings: The shadow of Ler Rhan has been slain by %s!  Ler Rhan has been pushed southward to the realms of the Sho and the Blackmire Swamp.  Seek Ler Rhan's shadow; he will arrive soon...
Ler Rhan collapses, but hisses in amusement as he falls: "You may have defeated this shadow of mine, %s, but I shall rise up elsewhere!"

The wind brings tidings: The shadow of Ler Rhan has been destroyed by %s!  Coolly, the Shadow General moves on to the plains nigh upon the borders of the Aluvian realm.  Seek again the aspect of Ler Rhan; he may be reached soon...soon...
Ler Rhan collapses, but hisses in amusement as he falls: "You have defeated this form, %s, but it is merely a shadow of my true self. I shall rise again elsewhere, and 'ware unto you!"
The wind brings ominous tidings: The shadow of Ler Rhan has been slain by %s!  But Black Ferah has taken up the assault within the Direlands...
Ler Rhan collapses, but hisses in amusement as he falls: "So, you have defeated me, %s. Well played. Yet, I have the aid of Black Ferah, who will now take up the forces in the northern Direlands!"

A new regime shall rise, a new master to take the place of the old. Darkness consumes all that light offers. Join with the darkness and become one with oblivion. Stand against us and be swept aside in the tide of destruction.
The abyss offers a solace far exceeding the gifts of life. To return there is to find the embrace of oblivion anew.
You seem to hear unintelligible words as the Umbris falls... only the name of Isin Dule is distinguishable.
You seem to hear unintelligible words as the Umbris falls... only the word "Daralet" is distinguishable.
A shrieking, squealing noise fills your head momentarily, pulsating with hatred, but quickly fades away into silence.

A shrieking, squealing noise fills your mind, pulsating with hatred. You find yourself standing on an unfamiliar shore. It is a blood-red dawn; the sort Viamont mariners say presage storms. A ripping noise rises, growing until it shakes the air around you. Birds cry, starting from the trees in terror. You raise your eyes to the horizon. Just above the green-blue sea, a black speck crosses the s...

A shrieking, squealing noise fills your mind, pulsating with hatred. You stand in a frigid downpour, among a crowd of thin and shivering people. Before you stands a fat, amber-eyed man in sumptuous robes, shielded from the rain by a glittering magical field. He shouts at the crowd, words you cannot comprehend, and thrusts a condemning finger at you again and again. As the vision fades, he gestu...

A shrieking, squealing noise fills your mind, pulsating with hatred. For a moment, you are overwhelmed by the impression of corruption and putrescence. It fades quickly, leaving you nauseous and shaken.

The wind brings great tidings: the shadow of Isin Dule has been destroyed by %s!  The Shadow Generals have spent the last of their power.   The invasion of the shadows has failed.  Dereth is safe...for now.

A voice calls out to all upon the wind: Set back by %s, Isin Dule is withdrawing into the dark center of all shadow, even while the shadows spring up all across the world.  Use his key to reach him there, and free all of Dereth at last from the dark armies!
A cascade of buzzing voices invades your mind.
I HATE YOU! I HATE YOU! DON'T EVER TALK TO ME AGAIN!
You think you hear a little voice say "Mommy..."
You hear the distant echo of childish laughter, fading away.
A sense of depression wells in the back of your mind as the Abyssal Shadow Child falls to the ground.

The wind brings terrible news: While the shadow of Black Ferah has been slain by %s in the Direlands, Ler Rhan has renewed his offensive in the A'mun desert!  But a new, cool and quiet undercurrent rides this wind, and it says: Little ones, seek now the Key that leads to the Nexus, and all will be made well!

Black Ferah laughs as she falls.  "I have merely bought some time for Ler Rhan to regroup, my sweet %s. How much longer can you humans continue? Our forces are infinite, and you fools still know not our true objective!"
The wind whispers to you: %s destroyed the first shadow of Black Ferah, but that is no hindrance.  The Enemy is advancing  into the craggy Linvak Mountains, south of the Sho lands.
As the shadow of Black Ferah falls, you hear a cold, contemptuous voice declare: "A fine attempt, %s, but this is but my shadow. I shall move on!"

The wind brings good tidings: %s has found and destroyed the shadow of Black Ferah! Leaderless, the Shadow Armies melt away. All but the mountains are safe once more.  The land is quiet for the moment...
As the shadow of Black Ferah falls, you hear the cold voice say: "A fine attempt, to have reached me within this twisted pathetic creation.  Well done, %s. I see I must reformulate my plans."

A whisper floats upon the wind: %s has defeated the shadow of Black Ferah. The Shadow forces press onward, even to the frontier of the lands settled by the Sho. The aspect of Black Ferah will doubtless seek the power within the southern Shadow Spire... Find the portal to that dread construct, where ever it may appear...

As the shadow of Black Ferah falls, you hear a cold, contemptuous voice declare: "Ah, %s, you have but slain my shadow!  I shall press on from this tiny hamlet, but don't think reaching me next time will be easy!  I shall be far above you."
A cascade of buzzing voices invades your mind.
You listen to the buzzing, but hear nothing but an insane childish laughter.
You think you hear a little voice say "Mommy..."
You hear the distant echo of childish laughter, fading away.
An uncontrollable hate seeps into your thoughts as the Depraved Shadow Child falls before you.
A cascade of buzzing voices invades your mind.
I'm sorry if I made mommy and daddy hate me...
You think you hear a little voice say "Mommy..."
You hear the distant echo of childish laughter, fading away.
Against your will, tears of sadness fill your eyes as the Pandemic Shadow Child collapses at your feet.
Such... pure metal... how it shines... how bright... take this katar and walk in the darkness... You have pleased the Dark Master.
Go... away... unless... you have business with me...
chatter: Yes... a letter... I will give you the letter... but first you must serve...
Go to the Empyrean foundry, in the swamps northwest of Sawato... Bring me one of their pyreal daggers... and you will be rewarded... by the darkness.  You will need this key...

greetings: A cascade of buzzing voices invades your mind.
Why do you hate me?

You hear the distant echo of childish laughter, fading away.

Legs are not meant to twist about the head in such a fashion are they? I thought not frail one!
This ends by my fists and weapons. Your body shall crumple like the walls of Linvak Tukal!
If this is the only means at your disposal to strike fear into my heart, I think you should rethink your position and flee toward the exit.

Gotrok, to my side! The Isparians have begun to fight back.
Our former masters have given us but one true gift. You have just felt its weight. Perhaps you would do better at catching my assault!

I wish for challenge in my victories, but you prove to be no more challenge than an armoredillo.
A breach in our defense, brothers to arms!
This magic you speak of, when will you begin to utilize it?

Muldaveus' voice thunders over the land, "Niarltah, we must flee. The Isparians have overrun our position. Come Morgluuk and Torgluuk, we will take you to the safety of our hidden fortress. Fostok, Amanua, get in here and clean up this tripe!"
Another body for the fire. Thank you for your gift.
Your frame is as weak as Kresovus's spirit!
Just another victim.
Isparian! You shall taste the weight of Gotrok steel even in your next life.
These preceedings would have brought peace to your race, but I see you prefer to the peace of death sooner than your brethren.
Your magic is too weak to penetrate band of chorizite. Call your words no more or earn my ire.
What did you wish to prove by twisting your tongue in such a fashion? That you can scream like a wounded mattekar.
%mn flinches back at the smell coming from the jar.
Disgusting! Keep your evil ichors to yourself!
Is this your proof of having rid our garrison of the olthoi? I'm sorry that just isn't good enough.
Ah, so they didn't survive the journey... Put it away.
Remember, I never saw that letter.
Hah, the fool, writing down directions to our secret garrison. I'm glad he's gone, less competition for me, hahaha.
%mn mashes his fists in celebration.
Well done! With this as proof of my defeating the Olthoi below I will garner much respect in our army. You should be rewarded for your assistance.
There, and since I'm feeling so magnanimous I will also grant you access to the garrison whenever I see you wearing your pendant. It's the only way I will recognize you.
Olthoi have a way of coming right back unless you kill them all so you may want to return to insure they have been exterminated.
Thank you, but I prefer paper. Here, take it back.
%mn looks astonishingly like someone trying to look innocent.
Oh, HaHa!
That might buy me some day old rice, I suppose. Thanks.
What! Are you trying to bribe me!? Well, I'll have none of that!
%mn crumples the X-note up and stuffs it into his mouth.
Surprisingly unsatisfying.
Closer...
Your getting warmer...
That's almost enough to make me care.
%mn swiftly reaches out and the tradenote disappears.
%mn whips out a sack and scoops all of the treasure into it.
quest: %mn glances at your pendant, looks around for witnesses and turns to the door.
Tell no one of this.
You shake %mn's shoulder. He seemed to be sleeping with his eyes open.
Wha! Humans! Leave now and you may yet live!
%mn looks you over. His eyes focus on your weapons and jewelry. He glances about the room for a moment.
Perhaps I was too hasty my friend.

Many days ago, our engineers broke into an olthoi tunnel while excavating the lower sections of this garrison. We fought them, and lost all but the top level beyond this door, which I was ordered to guard until reinforcements arrive.
Unfortunately, I have fallen on hard times and could not possibly consider jeopardizing my career by ignoring my ranking officer's orders. If only I could somehow be assured of your intentions...

I suppose you could bring me proof of your defeat of the olthoi below... if I had proof of their defeat, I could assure a promotion... But no, I cannot make a deal so risky without a little something to fall back on in case it were to fail.
Ah, I see that you intend to help us and that I, a loyal Gotrok, would be lax in my duties did I not allow creatures of such obvious honor to assist us in our hour of need.
You must not forget that I am taking a risk in allowing you entrance. Bring me back proof that you removed the olthoi menace from our garrison and I may have a small reward for you.

Also, my fellows within may not recognize you for the heroes that you are so be prepare to defend yourselves. If you can't handle them then you surely cannot handle the olthoi deeper down. If caught, remember to say that you got into the dungeon through portal magic.

Oh, If I see you again I am sure I will not recognize you. You humans all look alike to me with your pointy noses and huge ears, haha! Thus, if you require entrance you will have to pay m... I mean donate towards our rebuilding efforts again.
chatter: %mn's eyes glaze over and a soft snoring sound reverberates around the room.

greetings: The Pustule shudders, then bursts. You have opened a gateway portal!
The surface of the Pustule ripples; at the other end of the room, a faint glow appears briefly, then fades away.
A section of the floor boils up producing a large glowing pustule.
The pustule explodes, spraying you with it's rank fluids.
Putiputipuh idly nibbles at the artifact.
Putiputipuh rubs up against the artifact, then ignores it.
Putiputipuh stares (if you can call it that) at the artifact for a moment. Then stops.
Putiputipuh happily gnaws on the end of the bow for a moment, but does nothing more.
Putiputipuh smells the note, chews it up, then spits it out. Yuck.
quest: Putiputipuh whines, so softly and at so high a pitch you can bearly hear it.
The grub doesn't seem hungry at the moment.
The grub rustles, but otherwise ignores you.
The grub seems to sniff the air, but doesn't eat.
Tekapuapuh sighs. "Hmm. I remember washing my hands in those splashy-bubble-pots, before feeding her an onga. Maybe your hands are dirty?"
As you reach out with the apple, the grub emits a faint, high-pitched whine. You feel something squirming under your skin, along your arm and into the apple.
The grub happily devours the apple, swallowing it core and all.
Tekapuapuh squeals with delight. "You did it! Putiputipuh's happy again! Thank you thank you thank you!"

greetings: You feel something without voice scream in your mind in utter rage. It chills you to the bone as it fades away.
The black sarcophagus pulses with a black light.

chatter: I'm hungry.

greetings: Father...Father... My body crumbles to dust, am I forgotten. I am forgotten. I am dead. I am sorry father I have failed you and will rise no longer.

%s has slain Dranith Menacet. As the Hollow Minion bleeds its last bit of life onto the ground, it calls to its father in a child-like voice. "Father, I have failed you. They will find the way to your home." In Rithwic, a new portal appears.
My weakness is not yet complete, but oh the pain of being forgotten and abandoned.

You reel as a tremendous shock wave passes through you upon the vanquishing of Dranith Menacet.  A horrible din rises up in the background, and then slowly fades away.  You hear the voice of Dranith Menacet echo loudly in your mind, 'Do you think this means you've won?  Do you really?  Our plan has only begun, flesh.  This is only the start.  Soon you will see what your victory has meant.  Empt...

A flash of purple light streaks through the horizon and you hear a shattering thunderclap in the distance.  A strange hollow voice echoes in your mind, 'Our conquest begins today.  At this point we are merely a rumble.  Soon we will be the thunder that shakes the very flesh off your bones.  Our time is soon, human.  Very soon.'  The voice fades away, leaving you with a dizzying headache.
Weak fleshy things.  You are so horrible.  I hate you!
So many of you humans.  Come to me.  Come and meet your doom.
Do you think the glow can hurt me?  I laugh at your glows.
Father...I have failed you...again...
As Dranith Menacet's dying sighs fade into the stillness, a crumpled note, worn and creased from many readings, tumbles from his broken frame.

quest: You have opened this box too recently.
If you want to open this box you should speak with one of Nuhmudira's students standing nearby...
You must complete a quest to access this box.
You've done well thus far--but now comes the test of cunning. There are two ways out of this next room: Death and out through the portal you can see across the length of this chamber. Good luck.
Nope not good enough, you'll need to try a lot harder than that.
You call that skill?
Things aren't looking good for you friend. You really might want to train a little more at your skills.
I am ashamed that you would call yourself a vagabond. What skills do you possess, sub par equipment and a wit to match. I hope you fail at this point.
This is pathetic. You really shouldn't even be here.
Mages that dabble outside of casting spells really should not apply.
This is actually painful to watch. Your struggling with the rudiments of what a lock is. Even the most unskilled and unlearned vagabond knows more than you. What were you thinking coming here?
Another mistake like that and you could be in for quite the rude awakening. I hear that the lifestones actually scream when some people hit them as hard as you are going to.
I want you out of here. You're worthless. You're a pathetic waste of my tests. How you ever figured out how to get into my lair in the first place is beyond me.
It shouldn't even be possible to fail this test.

A woman's voice sounds in your mind, "You have not yet earned the right to draw what you will from his soul. Return when you have waited a full cycle of the days. Greed is a poor attribute to have, child.
There is nothing for you here, child.
You pick up a sliver of the bark. As you do another appears in its place.
As you near the chunk of wood your vision swims as if you are not meant to attain the item. It always seems to be out of your grasp. Perhaps there is more sleuthing to be done.

Welcome back, Buhdi! Have you come to get your title? Excellent!
quest: Excellent! Your keh burns brightly with victory! Here is something to recognize your efforts in hunting the Iron Golem Kingpins!
Return the token to me and I will bestow an appropriate title upon you, buhdi!

Excellent! Your keh burns brightly with victory! As I promised, a reward for you! It isn't much, simply some fixings I brought with me from Timaru! Here, feast with me as we celebrate your achievement!
The spirits tell me you have defeated four of the Iron Kingpins! Good! You are well on your way as a warrior!
The spirits tell me you have defeated three of the Iron Kingpins! Good! You are well on your way as a warrior!
The spirits tell me you have defeated two of the Iron Kingpins! Good! You are well on your way as a warrior!
The spirits tell me you have defeated one of the Iron Kingpins! Good! You are well on your way as a warrior!
Good luck to you, hunter! Return to me to see your progress in your efforts against the Iron Golem Kingpins. The spirits will speak and tell me of your victories!

Greetings. I am Aun Tiularea. I am the second youngest of the seven who have left Palenqual to hunt! As I am the second youngest, I have chosen the Iron Golem Kingpin as my prey. They are powerful in their own right, but tend to employ the use of underlings in their battles as well.

Would you like to hunt them as well? Very well, scour this region and others like it and I am sure you will find the golem. Kill five of these golems, return to me and I will see that your battles are rewarded!

greetings: Aha! This is the key to the chest where I keep my amulet--if you fetch it for me, I'll reward you with something much better.
I now grant you the title of Carenzi Slayer. Again, thank you.
quest: Thank you, but Carenzi has not yet returned to befoul my garden. I can only hope that he will not return a week from now.
Greetings, traveler. Raeta's migrations are such a beautiful mystery of nature. But where she goes, I must follow. I have moved my shrine to again be near her presence.

It is unfortunate that my misfortune seems to have followed me in turn. I have a grave favor to ask you. In his jealousy, the anima Carenzi has infested the beautiful shrine I built for Raeta with his own creatures. I tried to route them myself, but the horrid beasts nearly ripped me to pieces and ate the key to my chest! Until my shrine is cleansed of his defiling presence, Raeta will not return!

I locked my amulet inside my chest--if you bring it to me as proof that you have driven Carenzi away, I will reward you with the title of Carenzi Slayer. Follow Volkama's riverbanks to the south, and you'll find my shrine.

Incidentally, I would be careful going past my old grotto if I were you--a motley group of Hea have moved in and made the place their own. They had an interesting-looking chest with them...but I was in too much of a hurry to follow Raeta on her migration to inquire further.
chatter: If it weren't for Carenzi, I'd be able to tend the shrine I built for Raeta.
I know that if I were able to purge those loathsome beasts from my shrine, Raeta would bless it with her presence again.

Wonderful! Raeta graces my shrine once again. Take this necklace. Whenever you wear it, Raeta will bestow her grace upon you. If you wish to take on the title of Carenzi Slayer, give me back the necklace. I will return it and grant you the title.

greetings: Ah, the water, thank you.

You see that small sapling? It is very special to my people. You should be proud that we have chosen to plant it here. When it has grown it will represent the unity of our xuta's. I am asking the spirits to watch over her and give her the strength that we can share in our endeavors here.
Ah, yes.
She thanks you for the water. Once the grey-skins have done their work this tree and our akiekie will be fed from the water which lies below.
Oh, a visitor! Fetch me some water for this tree and I will tell you of my labors.
Hello no-tail! Do you like our tree? She will stand taller than most and stronger than some. Bring me water so that I may continue my drumming.
I'm sorry, I can't talk at the moment. This spell must be cast with precise drumming. Bring me some water. I should be done with the difficult magics by then and will talk with you.
Did you see her keh swell? It's so beautiful! She is growing faster than I could have hoped. All this work makes it thirsty though.
I thank you for this effort, but this piece of debris is from the stone ring in the northwest.
I thank you for this effort, but this piece of debris is from the stone ring in the southwest.
I thank you for this effort, but this piece of debris is from the stone ring in the southeast.
I thank you for this effort, but this piece of debris is from the stone ring in the north.
Yes, you are %s, who has helped us hold Wharu at bay. Greetings.
quest: You! Stonebreaker! The spiritcallers know your name now, and will not be duped again by you.
What do want here? Attempt to deceive us again with that fiendish bell and we will mark you for all to see!
Aun Gehaua tells you, "How foolish do you think us, %s? We know your evil name, yes, we do. You have done your damage to our efforts just recently!"
"Begone, and take your hideous bell with you. Even if you return in three weeks, it shall be too soon for me."
Aun Gehaua tells you, "Praise the stars and sky, and praise to you, %s. This will heal the stones at this place."
I greet you. I have often conferred with Isparian. This one is a spiritcaller of the Aun xuta.
I and my fellow callers help maintain the stone rings of this island. Their energies somehow increase the power of our rhythm.
How interesting. This is an instrument used by your people? Tonk says 'music is all and everlasting'
The crashing of the great pyreal bell reverberates through the ground. The menhir stones crack and break!
No! What have you done? Villian!
I must go and warn the xuta.
You are selfless, Isparian. You have assisted me in repairing this ring within the last three weeks. I cannot ask you to help me again.
You have told me a tale of victory too recently. Come back after a few moons with a new tale of victory and I will share in my bounty.

Greetings. I am Aun Tahuirea. My seven sons have left the land of Palenqual in search of glorious hunts. No doubt trying to impress me. They are each talented hunters in their own right, but none of them are yet ready to hunt what I do.

What is it that I hunt, you ask? I keep my harpoon sharp for the rare Crystal Lords. They are a dangerous type of golem for ones such as you, so be sure to bring others of your xuta to aid you in the battle. Should you and your fellows come across and defeat one, please come speak with me. I would enjoy hearing the story of your battles.
Also, if you and your fellows succeed in defeating one, I will be pleased to share with you the bounties I have recovered from my previous victories.

You tell Tahuirea the tale of the battle you and your fellows waged against the Crystal Lord and its minions. The Elder Tumerok smiles throughout the entire story. As you finish, Tahuirea unclips a key from his belt and hands it to you.

Your tale was truly one of triumph! I only wish I could have been there to see the battle for the tale is one of incredible glory. Use this key to take some of the bounty I have amassed in my hunting of the Crystal Lords.

greetings: Tikakhe inspects the hide for any small imperfections and finds none.

This hide will do nicely to create a drumhead for your buadren. Use this Tanning Oil on it to make it into a suitable leather. Once you complete your drum, give it to me and I will enjoin Mighty Oak to infuse it with his keh.
Ah, you have found one of the limbs of Mighty Oak. If you hollow it out, it would make a perfect shell for a drum.
Shreth has given you one of his fiery hides. You must cut this into smaller straps to bind a Buadren together.
This hollow trunk is now ready to be a shell for a drum. Cover it with the Tanned Hide of an Ebon Mattekar, and it will nearly be complete.

All you need to do now is bind this drum together with Leather Straps cut from the hide of a Shreth Auroch. Once this task is complete, you will have created a Buadren. Bring this Buadren to me, and I will enjoin mighty Oak to enter it and sustain you with his keh.
This oil can be used to tan the hide of a Dread Mattekar into leather.

You have done a good job in tanning this hide. Now, if you drape it over a hollowed-out tree trunk, you will have completed most of the steps towards making a buadren for yourself. When you have completed one, give it to me, and I will enhance it for you.

These leather straps could be used to bind a tanned Dread Mattekar Hide to a drum shell made from a hollowed-out tree trunk. Together, this will form a buadren much like the ones we Tonk use to cast our spells.
No, friend, this buadren, created from the trophies of your own hunts and crafted through the work of your own hands, is rightfully yours.

This is an ember taken from the akiekie council fire of Timaru. The keh of our ancestors reside within that flame--if Aulakhe has entrusted you with an ember of that fire, he must have great faith in you.
This ember glows more brightly than ever before. Quickly, you must take it to Aulakhe before its life ebbs away.

It is as I have forseen. Aulakhe is the first among us to combine the medicine of our people and yours. The spirit of Aun Tanua has returned to fight the battles of his people once more. This buadren is infused with Tanua's own keh. If carried with reverence, he will aid you in your struggles as well.  Take our gift with pride, and  know that you have done the Tonk of Timaru a great service thi...

When Aulakhe first came and told me he was leaving Timaru, I knew I could not let him go alone. We have journeyed across the breadth of Dereth on our quest, and I have seen much that could be used to create semblances of the items we had back on Palenqual.
In the days since we have settled here, even more powerful spirits than before have pledged their aid in the creation of the Buadrens much like the one you see in my hands.
The great Aualuan Kenchaua has sent word from the mountains of the south that Ebon Mattekar pledged his hides to form Buadren's head.
Fire Shreth from the plains of the north has pledged his hides to form Buadren's sinews.
As we finally settled here, near the akiekie of Aula's new ani, Ispar Celdisethaua, Mighty Oak promised his limbs to form Buadren's body.

Once you assemble these three gifts, give the hide of Ebon Mattekar to me. I will inspect it for its imperfections--if it is perfect, I will give you a fragrant oil brought from Timaru to tan it into a supple drumskin. Tanae speed your hunt, friend.
quest: Tikakhe slowly turns the buadren over in his hands, inspecting every detail.
The spirits of this land are indeed generous. I could not have made a better buadren myself. Wait one moment, while I invoke the keh of Mighty Oak.

Beating gently upon the buadren, Tikakhe slowly murmurs a prayer to the anima of his choosing. A quiet descends upon the forest, and the trees themselves bend to listen to Tikakhe's call. Abruptly, a soft glow permeates the drum, one that is gone as suddenly as it came.

A last tale to tell before my work is done: I must tell you that this was merely a test, to prove to us that you are the warrior that we have journeyed from Palenqual to find. Aun Aulakhe's has undertaken a grave mission for our people, and we shall not return to our beloved Timaru until it is accomplished. Speak to him now--I will let him know that you have been chosen.
Aun Tikakhe pauses a moment to take you into his confidence.

Although he is still young and untested, my heart believes Aulakhe is destined one day to become the most gifted of our Aulauan, surpassing even his father, Shimauri. You would do well to guard this buadren safely--there may come a time when Aulakhe may be able to enhance it once more.
The spirits of this land are indeed generous. I could not have made a better buadren myself. Wait one moment, while I invoke the keh of Mighty Oak!

A last tale to tell before my work is done: my budhi Aun Aulakhe has undertaken a grave mission for our people, and we shall not return to our beloved Timaru until it is accomplished. Speak to him when you have gained in experience and strength - I will let him know that when that day comes he can take you into his confidence. Until then, guard this buadren safely--if you aid us in the days to...
