greetings: Your persistence in striking against us has begun to unnerve us. You cannot hope to survive what is coming there is no stopping nature. Not even time can dwindle our power and what we are.
%s has defeated Corrosion, the Essence of Verdancy.
In my new gained sentience I did not understand destruction. But now I see that even I can be dispersed. But my death like yours is not permanent. I shall return sooner than you think.
Your flesh dissolved from bones, I triumph again.
Tempt not, what your magic is made of. There will only be a reckoning.
%s has defeated Corrosion, the Essence of Verdancy, repelling Gaerlan's forces back from the cities of the west...for now.
%s has defeated Tempest, the Essence of Storms. Its form is driven from the world and Gaerlan's forces are routed at Fort Tethana, Ayan Baqur, Wai Jhou, and Danby's Outpost.
The door Jrvik was guarding slides open as he is defeated.
Thank you.  It is a disappointment that I cannot unlock these, but I will hold them until that day.  Here is your reward.
In His Name, who Walks Eternal!  I never thought I would see these unlocked.  I urge you to bring me more of these unlocked treasures, so that the Dericost society may live forever.
Thank you for bringing this to us.  If you step through the portal and bring it to my assistants, they will be able to reward you.
Thank you for bringing this to us.  I am gratified to see that you found a way to unlock it.  If you step through the portal and bring it to my assistants, they will be able to reward you.
We Dericost do not concern ourselves with these manual affairs.  I have no need of this.
I have no desire to understand this outlander scribbling.  Here.

Greetings, outlander. I am Saelar of Menilesh.  My master, the great Tennar Portheran perished during the Fourth Sending, along with so many of our people.  But before he died, he set in motion a way for our people to preserve our heritage and our memories in the face of the recent catastrophes that have befallen the Dericost.  He invented a number of Mnemosynes, devices that allow us to record...

Tennar commissioned a locksmith from among your kind, whose name I do not know, to make these Mnemosynes lockable and to make keys to the Mnemosynes which only Tennar would possess.  Unfortunately, I have no idea what happened to the lockpicker or his keys.  The Mnemosynes have been coming in, and I have no way of opening them.

But still, if you come across a Mnemosyne please bring them to me and I will reward you well.  The collection for the larger Mnemosynes I have tasked to my assistants whom can be found through the portal.

The cold, luminous eyesockets of the Lady of Aerlinthe regard you balefully. "Fools!" she hisses. "You will destroy us all! If you must have the key, protect that which we do!" So saying, the light in her rotted skull dies, and her spirit wafts back to the north to gather its strength.

On far Aerlinthe Island, an intrepid band has found the lair of the Dark Lady Aerfalle, at whose whim the earth itself does shake. But the bold %s has driven her back into her hidden crypts, and the ground stills... until she next awakens.

The withered corpse of Aerfalle hisses in rage as it is hewn in twain... "I shall not be sent to a final rest by primitives like thee, %s!" her severed head says from the stones. "Enjoy this insignificant victory, child. For I have walked this world for over ten millennia, and I shall walk it long hence your little race has returned to the dust that birthed thee!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Did that hurt thee, %s?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Perhaps I play too roughly with you fragile outlanders..."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "I am one of the primogen of Dericost. I am not like mine countrymen you have fought. If you strike me down, I shall rise again!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "I shall not be defeated!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Is that the best you can do, my poor child?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Tell your little gods who sent you to them, %s!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "That head will make a fine trophy. Which of you will next decorate my keep?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Vermin!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Don't you have anything better to do than bother me?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Disturb not your betters, child!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Guards! To me!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "A little help here, please."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Gentlemen, could I trouble you to perform thy task?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Bah. There are Dark Spawn and Walkers yet in the world. You are not worthy of my attention."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Guards! Clean up the mess in here. I have more important things to attend to."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "A skillful attack, %s."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Impressive, child. Your people do sometimes surprise me."
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Your so-called magics are no match for those of old Dericost!"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Your spellcraft is feeble, %s! Are you sure your calling is that of a mage?"
A coolly amused voice seeps across your mind, "Is that the extent of thy powers, child? I shall show thee true power!"
Insignificant mortal! Soon you shall know your own demise!
Flee from this fate and into the arms of my awaiting minions...
My death at the hands of that which I have never seen, shall not go unknown. I am a Warrior of the Blood and shall return to serve, this new master again.
Bound as I am, I cannot syphon your strength and make it my own. Odd though, that I sense you are not dead, nor undead.
The Blood protects those that dedicate their souls to it.
This is work for Saelar, not me.
Saelar gathers these.
This is work for Hahnain.
Hahnain.
Yes, this is for me.
Yes.
No.
Hand me the Mnemosyne.  You will get your just reward.
The voice in your mind purrs, "You are generous, not to mention strong. Yet honor requires I return the excess."

The voice in your mind purrs, "Seek the dark ones and destroy them...yet meddle not with the devices you may find on our island of Aerlinthe. Perilous they are to those who do not understand their art."

The voice in your mind purrs, "Ai, this will serve. Seek the dark ones and destroy them...yet meddle not with the devices you may find on our island of Aerlinthe. Perilous they are to those who do not understand their art."
The voice in your mind laughs, "You think I cannot read or count, child? This is not enough to satisfy my needs!"
The voice in you mind laughs, "Ah, poor barbarian child. I said 50,000 pyreal, not 5,000! Your education is slack, I think."

Garaena shakes her head, flakes of desiccated skin flying off her high cheekbones. "Ah, child. You are either far too poor or far too foolish to take this road. It would be better for you to return to Ifistra. Ah, that is Osteth in your tongue."

The rotting woman inclines her head stiffly, and a disembodied voice seeps across your mind like oil. "Child, you walk among the tombs of the Sand Kings. Long ago they were mighty captains in service to the powers behind the Ice Throne. Now they rest, and dream of new plots. Yet still they hold themselves great power, and are ageless and fey."

"My mistress sent me hither to solicit their aid in a great cause. Perhaps you could serve, for I shall call the enemy of mine enemy friend. Those in shadow...thralls of the one called Slayer of Hope...beset our isle. If you give me a note worth 50,000 of the Yalaini pyreal, to fund my mission to bribe the Sand Kings, I shall open the gate for you.
"Be warned; only the mightiest may pass through this gate, and I will not allow you to tie to it."
Magic swirls around the acolyte, forming a portal to the next area.
The door Zixki was guarding slides open as he is defeated.
The undead general staggers and falls to his knees. "So it goes," he murmurs sadly. "I commend myself into thy arms, Isishaa..."

The undead general staggers and falls to his knees, but pauses and looks up into %s's eyes. "Don't let it end like this, young one. If you must send me to the wind, my task is yours to complete. Protect the stone."
The Baron of Colier has been defeated.
The undead spymaster croaks, "No! I am yet needed!"
The undead spymaster croaks, "Your incaution will ruin us all!"
As the ancient mage collapses into viscera and rot, it groans, "May my sacrifice bring closer the resuscitation of the Ice Throne!"
As the ancient mage collapses into viscera and rot, it groans, "His Eternal Splendor will return to deal with your insignificant race!"
As the ancient mage collapses in viscera and rot, it groans, "It was near Anadil's encampment all along..."

In your mind, the ancient mage whispers, "Listen to me, outlander. The Dark Spawn did not seek to make a binding on Aerlinthe... they sought... to break... one." The pale fire in the creature's eye fades before it can say more.

In your mind, the ancient mage whispers, "There are horrors worse than us in this world, child. We merely seek a kingdom. The Spawn seek... But I cannot speak such blasphemies! Why do you fight us? Why do you aid the Enemy?"
As the ancient creature collapses into viscera and rot, it groans the name of Avoren.
As the ancient creature collapses into viscera and rot, it groans the name of Rytheran.
As the ancient creature collapses into viscera and rot, it groans the name of Aerfalle.
As the ancient creature collapses into viscera and rot, it groans the name of Anadil.
As the ancient creature collapses into viscera and rot, it groans the name of Asmolum.
As the undead archer falls to the floor of its Skytower, it groans the name of Aerfalle.
As the undead archer falls to the floor of its Skytower, it calls in Roulean, "Excellent shot!"
As the undead archer falls to the floor of its Skytower, a voice in your mind screams, "They are breaking through our perimeter! Notify Lord Anadil!"
As the undead archer falls to the floor of its Skytower, it groans the name of Anadil.
As the undead archer falls to the floor of its Skytower, it groans the name of Asmolum.
The door Hezhit was guarding slides open as he is defeated.

As it collapses into a mass of bone and rot, the ancient mage mutters, "Faugh! Human, ever do your people play the pawns. First you unwittingly served the Hopeslayer, and then you banished him at the direction of others..."

As it collapses into a mass of bone and rot, the ancient mage mutters, "Your triumph against the Hopeslayer will be laughably short-lived. Do not grow too comfortable in this world, as it will soon be reclaimed by its true masters. His Eternal Splendor still broods in his citadel!"

As it collapses into a mass of bone and rot, the ancient mage mutters, "Your triumph against the Hopeslayer will be laughably short-lived. Do not grow too comfortable in this world, as it will soon be reclaimed by its true masters. The Steward merely bides her time in Chalicmere!"
As the undead falls, its rotting flesh ripples and sloughs away, revealing the ebon form of a Shadow! "We slew the third deadflesh commander," it cackles. "What was his is ours now!"
As the undead falls, its rotting flesh ripples and sloughs away, revealing the ebon form of a Shadow! "Ler Rhan's chosen," it whispers to itself. "They shall keep it on Savao."
As the undead falls, its rotting flesh ripples and sloughs away, revealing the ebon form of a Shadow! "The dusty fool knows naught," it chuckles softly. "They cannot bar the way."

As the undead falls, its rotting flesh ripples and sloughs away, revealing the ebon form of a Shadow! "Your little victory matters not," it cackles. "We already altered the path so none may follow but our own!"
What care have I for a note that I discarded? You are being meddlesome. Be gone at once. Your presence here will only serve as a distraction from the Winds that strive to protect Killiakta.
Why must you interfere? Your race is such an insignificant speck upon this world, and yet you feel as though you must place your fingers where they do not belong. I have no need of that memento.
Another note dropped because of irrelevance. Do you think it is necessary for me to maintain my faculties? I may not be one of the Primogenitors, but my mind is still whole.
Cease your interference here. Each moment that you distract me from my purpose is another moment that we risk her return.

I do not remember ridding myself of this order. It is inconsequential. It has no bearing on my task...which you have turned my attention from. Meddling outlanders! A pox upon your people, the Ice Throne will rise again, and you shall be swept aside!
Ae...? Outlanders, for what purpose have you come to this place? Speak not. I care not. You are the cause of much suffering upon my ilk. I desire no discourse with those such as you.
Leave us to our task, and allow us to shore these tunnels. Continue your efforts to supply the mechanic with the devices we require, that is the only assistance that we require from you, Outlanders.

Be gone from this place. Your meddling here will only serve to remove the impetus of my workers, and cause a delay in the reshaping of these tunnels. Be gone, lest you wish to unleash the horde back upon your populace and bring an end to Killiakta.
I give you new life, mortal!
Your kind has disturbed us for the last time!
Another fool has come in search of fate, my brothers.
As it collapses into a mass of bone and rot, the ancient mage mutters, "Enjoy your triumph, outlander, but your time in the light is fleeting. This world belongs to us..."
As it collapses into a mass of bone and rot, the ancient mage moans, "All our powers come to dust. Is this how it shall end for proud Dericost?"
Im vaik av tiu ikni liViliakti.
Ek, taivti Tik Vaiktu Kiktij tiu ikni arkvikt.
The Dericost lord's body collapses into rot and dust, but a voice in your mind sneers, "Pathetic little wretch! I shall rise again soon enough."

The Dericost lord's body collapses into rot and dust, but a voice in your mind sneers, "I should like to see you test your mettle against my Lady, barbarian dog! She is a far more powerful magician than I."

The Dericost lord's body collapses into rot and dust, but a voice in your mind sneers, "I trust my defeat makes you feel slightly more in control of your destiny ... less like a dog at the end of Asheron's leash? Get you from my halls before I rise again!"
A voice in your mind sneers, "Faugh! Pathetic."
A voice in your mind sneers, "It is difficult to imagine that the Great Ones would waste skin on such as you, %s."
A voice in your mind sneers, "You would not have lasted a halfbreath against my Lady, barbarian!"
A voice in your mind sneers, "Do not return here again, %s. The boy's spinning rocks would not protect you if I released my full power."
Lord Rytheran stamps his foot contemptuously on %s's corpse.
Lord Rytheran gleefully spits on %s's corpse.
A voice in your mind sneers, "I believe I have, as you barbarians are wont to say, 'owned' you."
A voice in your mind sneers, "Don't you people have anything better to do than bother me?"
A voice in your mind sneers, "Oh, now what do YOU want, %s?"
Lord Rytheran turns to fix his steely gaze upon %s!
Lord Rytheran notices %s entering his sanctum, and rolls his rotting eyes in exasperation.
A voice in your mind sneers, "Oh for the throne and all that comes with it... Guards!
A voice in your mind sneers, "You bore me, and I have a letter to complete. Shoo, pest."
A voice in your mind sneers, "Your powers are weak, dog!"
A voice in your mind sneers, "The thought of a primitive like you besting me through Art is laughable! Show me your sword, that I may enjoy this battle!"
Lord Rytheran blinks in surprise, then begins to chuckle at %s's inept spellcasting!
Lord Rytheran resists %s's feeble spell. He shakes his head, muttering something about "the mages these days" under his foul breath.
Im vaik av tiu ikni liViliakti.

chatter: ...cold...
...help...can't...stop...
...Frisirth controls...me...
...make it...stop...
...mercy...please...
...kill me...
...so cold...

greetings: Magic swirls around the acolyte, forming a portal to the next area.
A Lesser Acolyte has been summoned nearby.
It cannot be! The interlopers invade our halls, disturbing our sleep. I have failed...
I will not fail my charges!
I release you of your burden. Yet, I know your kind will be back now that you have found this place. Very well, let them come.
Yes, return to your waypoint outlander. Do not disturb us again.
You should not have come here.
I take no pleasure in your pain. Do not return to this place.
You wish to taste death as well? Let me help you.
You cannot win outlander. Your kind are so very unruly and unfocused. I am amazed you have survived here this long.
Can you hear the song? No, you cannot. Your kind do not belong within our places of rest!
Like the buzzing of annoying insects. Stand still, so I may swat you.
I have no time for foolish outlander!
A strong blow outlander, but you will fall before me.
You fight well outlander, but I am the Ward and Keeper and I will not fail in my duties!
Pathetic! And you still use implements to focus your magics. Humorous.
As the Lich Overseer falls to his endless sleep, you hear him say, "Maharani, I have failed you! Now the relic falls into their hands...But they will never learn how to use it!"
Maharani, in your name I strike down this insignificant mortal.
Soon you will fall into the endless slumber of death.

The voice in your mind sneers, "You give me more than I ask. I am not a moneychanger, insolent whelp! I shall open the path to my home, the ancient port of Aerlinthe, and keep the excess! You would be wise to tread lightly, lest you wake the ire of my island and my Lady."

The voice in your mind sneers, "You are wise to offer me such a boon, lest I strike ye down like a cur in the street. I shall open the path to my home, the ancient port of Aerlinthe. You would be wise to tread lightly, lest you wake the ire of my island and my Lady."
Faladha stares at you coldly. The voice in your mind sneers, "This is insufficient, dog! Do you seek to incur my wrath? My patience with you wears perilously thin."
The voice in your mind cries, "You mock me!"

The dead man turns and looks down the rotted remains of his nose at you. A cool, aristocratic presence invades your mind, and seems to speak in Roulean. "You are foolish to come here, outlander. This is the castle called Chalicmere, fortress of the Latzimestal faction..."

"Ah, but such subtleties are beyond you. To your barbarian eye, we are merely corpses and bones, all alike and monstrous. Yet it is not so, and these rotting forms you revile shaped the destinies of men and kingdoms far beyond your ken.

"Obstruct me not, whelp. I have urgent traffic with the Lords of the Latzimestal... unless you will give me a note worth 10,000 pyreal. Then I shall grant you all the adventure you desire, if you be mighty enough to use my passage. Yet I shall not suffer barbarians in my home, and will prevent you from conjuring the gate yourself."
Kikt viktia ti ikni liViliakti, Ij vaik zikt kta im iak, jakti im iakvi av tiu ikni likik ilkin akti.
You hear soft chanting in the distance, in some odd language.
Leikotha inspects the haft.
It is almost as I remember it when he carried it in his hand. Not quite though. Some harm cannot be undone.
Leikotha sighs.
Ai, Wari. One like thee, a child of another sun. He carried this haft, a great blade resting within it, and sought to release me. He failed... and now has been cursed as I have.
A single tear rolls down Leikotha's cheek. She raises a hand to her face and the dry wrappings absorb the tear instantly.
As I have said, I shall reward you.
If thou returns with the gems that once graced this haft, I will reward thee again.

Mine thanks. This gem was but the first one that graced the axe Wari once wielded. Thy people had begun to establish holdings here on Ireth Lassel when Wari came across this ancient tomb. This place of mourning that I have haunted for millennia.
Leikotha looks to the ceiling above her, and then returns her attention to you.

After defeating those that surround me, Wari approached me. The long days had gone by so slowly, and this diminutive creature, one so much like mine own people, intrigued me. For a moment, this curiosity lifted the burden of my torment off my soul.

I hailed this creature, asked him his name and what he sought. A moment he stood silent, considering me. Then he told me his name, what had passed on the land above, and that he now looked for a cause to lend his blade to.

A spark of hope entered my heart, if I could still be said to have one. So long had I sought to undo Nerash's binding, the curse that forever keeps me from passing. Perhaps this curious creature could finally undo it. Ai, I was wrong, so very wrong.
Ai, I see I have tarried thee long enough. I will reward thee for thy efforts.
If thou brings me another of the gems, perhaps I will tell thee more.
The fifth gem. I see thou have seen Wari. Fate has not been kind to a soul so noble. Some once said the same of me. However, thou does deserve a reward for giving Wari a moment of peace.

Now you know what I found when I entered Sylsfear. Wari had sought out the undead lords, those who, in their life, had maintained the facility and studied the mana and structure of this world. These undead lords and their minions had overpowered Wari, had discovered why he sought them out, and thought of an appropriate punishment.

His mighty blade was shattered and spread about the undead minions as trophies. He was left with but one piece; the gem thou have brought to me. The lords also cursed Wari in a manner similar to me. Yet Wari's curse had been imperfect and his mind was now as shattered his axe had been.
I wept bitter tears when I returned to this tomb, seeing what had become of this noble child of distant sun. Ai, the tears were for me as well, for now I knew my torment would not end.
Thou does know the tale now, and I have but a few final words to offer thee: Do not fear the fate that awaits all creatures that draw breath, for fates much worse than that can be meted out.
Now please leave me be.
Wari's fourth gem. Thank thee.

I had stood here, impassive, watching the days begin and end, ceaselessly. As the millennia had passed, I thought I had but one feeling left to me: sorrow. Yet Wari had shown I had another: hope. Now this fleshless fool, the one who told me of Wari's death, had brought out yet another: fury.
I struck down the fool, although not before I found out where Wari had fallen. Wari had sought the answer to unbinding me in the dungeon Sylsfear.
I left this tomb, something I had not done for untold ages, and sought out those who had done this.
Ai, if only I had not. If only.
The second gem from Wari's axe. Allow me to reward thee.
Since thou has shown an interest in Wari's tale, I will continue to tell it to thee.

I had told Wari of Nerash's poison arrow and my fall at the Plateau of Gelid. Of how Nerash, a foul undead minion of Dericost, had sought to keep me at his side for all eternity. Of how I had been tortured and twisted by his dark rites and doomed to never know the peace of oblivion. Of my daughter, Alysse, who only knew her mother as a loathsome monster, who had been forced to flee the light.

Wari's noble heart was moved, he swore to find a means to undo Nerash's binding. I told him of the undead lords who roamed the sands of this land. The secrets of blood were known to them, perhaps they could aid him in releasing the binding.
Wari set off to find these lords. Never again did I see him.
Ai, thou have found the third gem from Wari's axe. You shall be rewarded.
Many days passed after Wari left this tomb. Days that had been very much the others before Wari had come, yet the spark of hope remained.

Then one of these creatures, these minor undead who derive a sick pleasure from seeing mine torment, told me that Wari had fallen. It cackled, the teeth in its fleshless skull rattling together with pleasure.
The spark of hope died. Ai, if I could but join it.
quest: Ai, another comes, breaking mine wretched musings. Why have you come to this sandy tomb, filled with unnatural beasts? Is your heart filled with greed, seeking what treasures may lay within? Or is your heart of a more noble nature, perhaps seeking to release me from this torment? It matters not, for I have but one thing to offer you.
Like so many things found on this unhappy world, it is broken. Once though it belonged to a friend. One like thee. One who hoped to release me. Ai, he failed... he failed.

Take the haft, I would see it used again in his name than have it stay with me and crumble to dust. If thou have no use for the Haft, I would still see it as it once was. Return the haft to me, repaired, and I will reward thee. Those that surround me speak of one of thy kind who may know how to set it to order once more. Look for her at 1.7 S, 36.6 E.
Thy mind tells that the haft has been repaired. Give it to me, and I shall reward thee.
Leave me be, I have nothing to offer thee right now.
I have given you all I have to offer. Take the haft, seek the one at 1.7 S, 36.6 E.
Leikotha releases a dry, rasping gasp.
Ashbane... mine own sword.
Leikotha examines her sword, feeling the weight of the blade in her hands.
I had dropped this on the hill of Ayn Tayan... My rage had so blinded me. Ferah, had played me for the fool...
Spinning lies in my mind...
What I did...
A sound slowly builds within Leikotha, until finally an unearthly scream emanates from her. You feel the din about to deafen you when the scream stops.
Why... why...
Leikotha stares silently at the blade of the sword.
How... where... ai, thy mind tells me that thou has found in one of Aerfalle's caches. Foul magus that she is. I shall reward thee for thy efforts.
Now leave me. Leave me with my bitter memories...
Leikotha tilts her head from side to side, as if judging you.
I have no time for a child's pestering. Be gone, lest my rage return and I strike thee down.
Be glad that mine ire is held in check.
chatter: In your mind, a soft voice sighs, "Please leave me be... I wish thee no harm."
In your mind, a soft voice sighs, "So many turns of the world have passed. When shall my torment end?"
In your mind, a soft voice sighs, "Disturb me not... Travel past this hole in the earth."

greetings: What, is my jitte not good enough for you? That is the best I can make right now. I am always experimenting. Come back some other time, maybe I will have something better.
The perfect weapon... Soon, I will make the perfect weapon... By the way, have you seen my old jitte anywhere?
chatter: My old jitte! Thank you! It seems rather inferior now, with the advances I have made in jitte technology.  But it has great sentimental value. Take this new jitte I've been working on, see how it works out.

greetings: You should have handed this to Saelar, it is his job.
I do not understand why Saelar does not just torture these secrets out of you!  I am not the collector for these.  Go see Saelar.
Yes, here is the reward you were promised.

I cannot believe that you fledglings know how to unlock Tennar's great Mnemosynes, and Saelar refuses to do anything about it.  If Tennar were still alive...But Saelar is a more cautious sort.  Here is your reward.
This is for Renselm.  Step through that portal there.
So much of our glorious history is to be found in that Mnemosyne.  Be careful with it outrider, be very careful.  Go see Renslem through that portal.
Bah, Saelar has told us not to concern ourselves with the keys.  He says it is beneath us.  Here.
We should force the secrets of this device out of you!  But Saelar says to have patience.  So for now outlander...
If Saelar didn't want this, then I have no use for it.

Yes?  Saelar told me to expect you.  Why we need to deal with you...I will accept the Mnemosynes, but Renslem has been tasked with collecting and sorting the largest of the Mnemosynes.  He can be found through that portal.
Ekta livaik ikti vik ilkian, ia klia livaik ix vik iak.
Im iakvi av tiu ikni Viliakti, Ij fiak kilt zakiik.
Ekta livaik ikti vik ilkian, ia klia livaik ix vik iak.
I have failed the master, more of me is taken. How long until all of what was me is gone?
You should not have trespassed here. We are set to the task and supported by the master.
These magics you use. They are not native. You do not have control of true Heiromancy. Feeble.
Musansayn, what has become of me?
I've failed you... failed...
chatter: Wari al Sha'im shakes his head and says, "Where... am... I..."
In a confused voice, Wari al Sha'im says, "The Silifi... Where is the Silifi..."

greetings: Even in this climate I shall be reborn. I am the essence of true preservation and so I shall return to place you lovingly within my eternal embrace. You shall be my most prized treasures.
%s has defeated Stasis, the Essence of Frost, repelling Gaerlan's forces back from the cities of the south...for now.

I have thought and speech, and you would take this from me. I offer you forever. You make my time so brief. But you cannot destroy what I am. I am the Master's guardian. I cannot be removed by the means you possess.
%s has defeated Stasis, the Essence of Frost. Its form is driven from the world and Gaerlan's forces are routed at Qalabar, Kara, Khayyaban, and Mayoi.
You are feeble, a neophyte. You know not what it is you tamper with.
Etched in time forever. You shall slumber, encased within my hold eternally.
Frustrating that I have taken so many of you but still you rise to face me again. I am not yet finished. Hardly weakened. I am still full of life and living. There will be a reckoning.
%s has defeated Stasis, the Essence of Frost, repelling Gaerlan's forces back from the cities of central Osteth...for now.

This is not right. I am the master of stopping the decay, burning the flesh with freezing. I am the one that maintains eternities claim. The master has betrayed me. I live but for him. A vessel has been prepared!
%s has defeated Stasis, the Essence of Frost. Tempest, Corrosion, Strife and Stasis have all been destroyed. In Yanshi something stirs.
I am that which you cannot hope to tame. I have no master and will not be made slavish to your magics.
You tear asunder the very fabric of what is. Pull at the threads, my death shall be heralded by the birth of another.
We are the memories of the first given form. You cannot defeat us for our souls live on. Remember well this chill for it will be with you always.
There is no more master but we are still. We are the essence of the chill, ever shall we return.

Toberik, you crazy hoktor! Well Isparian, it appears as though you brought this report to me in good time. Toberik means to detain Morgluuk's brother, Torgluuk, so that we can face just the one brother. The plan is not without trouble though. We have managed to learn much from the blueprints that we obtained from the Burun fortress in the Blackmire Swamp.

Currently, we believe that the best course of action is to approach the fortress from their north. The walls are weaker there, it appears as though the Renegade builders have been spending more time trying to discern the goals of the Burun and not enough on shoring up their work.

This will not be a simple fight. We will need you to be quick and efficient in your assault. We Lugians will assist the Tumeroks of Marae Lassel in laying an assault against one of the Renegade fortresses to provide you a small amount of assistance.

Once you break the walls down, you will need to enter the catacombs that the Burun have built beneath the fortress. Find your way through and defeat Morgluuk. He is very strong, there may be ways to weaken him without facing him... I would advise trying to find a way to weaken him before assaulting him directly.
Captain K'rank says "Good luck to you, %tn!"

Incredible work. You've done a remarkable job in collecting these specimens. I can see that you spent a good deal of time collecting these at the Ma--in the wilderness! Great work! As promised, you are deserving of a fair reward.
Come back tomorrow, I might have more work for you then.
These are wonderful finds. I'm going to see that these find their way into our sages hands as quickly as possible. For now, I must get you your reward.

Nasty smell coming from this crate. You must have freshly killed the majority of these creatures. Your efforts should not go unrewarded and to prove that we Lugian's are as noble as we claim, I offer you these.
I offer you my thanks and the small tokens that I shall give you in a moment. The information contained in this missive may one day save a great many lives.
Gorak must have been pleased to see the axe, he overpaid. I'll make sure that this finds its way to him in a future payment. You've been a great help, please take this with my thanks.
Olcris is sure to have been up to something no good. I'll have a scholar look over this missive as soon as I take care of your reward.
Ugh! That was rather heavy, you could have warned me before just tossing into my arms like that. Cripes! Nonetheless, you did as I asked, so you are deserving of a fair reward. Here, take these.
quest: Captain K'rank says, "Hail %tn."
I see that you have returned to shatter the morale of the Burun again. Your efforts continue to assist our people in lessening the threat these creatures pose. Here are your rewards.
The key will open whichever chest you choose in that room. Each chest should clearly display what it holds.
That is all that I have to give.
Captain K'rank says, "Thank you again for your efforts, %tn."

Again you take the head of the Burun leader, Morgluuk. You are surely a hero to all. As we have already placed the creatures head outside of the city in your honor, this one will be turned into a trophy that you can display with honor.
%tn has defeated Morgluuk and received a glorious reward for their efforts.
You come have to aid us, no? Well then, let me see what I have for you.

Captain K'rank says, "Ah, you said your name was %tn, yes? Well it appears as though you've been here recently as your name appears in my notes. We're trying not to overwork you too much, so please finish up what we asked of you and then take some time for yourself. Come back to me tomorrow and I'll see what I can have you do."
No, it looks like you helped us with this one.
You've familiar blood on your armor. It is the blood of our brothers who succumbed to the way of the Virindi. Is it possible that you have found Toberik? Quickly, if have news from him let me see it.
Filthy creatures these Burun. As promised you are to be rewarded for your efforts.
A brave warrior who has continued our efforts to crush the morale of the Burun and the renegades. You have done well. Here take this and display it proudly.

Hail Isparian, I am sorry if I appear preoccupied. I am waiting on a very important report from a spy working amongst the Renegades. His report from the Renegade fortress in the Direlands is overdue and we have seen an increase in the number of camps surrounding the fortress. I should not bother you with such concerns.
You have come to aid us, no? Well then, let me see what I have for you.
Captain K'rank seems to consult some notes.
Let me see what I have for you.

Here is one. We are collecting information of the varying hides of the Armoredillos. We're looking into ways to create layered armor from their hides that would afford better than usual protection against all different forms of damage. Here take this.

Put the specimens in this sack in the following order, no need to write this down, we've already listed the order on the outside of the sack. I'm just making sure that you've been told as well. Small armoredillo hide, followed by the regular hide, the large hide, then the sturdy hide and lastly the plate armoredillo hide. When you have filled the sack return it to me for a handsome reward of no...

This one should prove interesting. Our sages are interested in the geomancy that makes the Golems 'live'. We need specimens of the Golem's hearts to continue our study. Since we're used to working with stones it comes as no surprise that we are specifically interested in the different stone and mineral golems. Take this.

Put the specimens in corresponding collection slots. They are listed on the front of the crate for easy reference. Just to be clear however, I will tell you the order they should be collected in. First collect a granite heart, followed by iron, copper, obsidian, gold and finally a diamond heart. Then return to me with the full crate.

A little less sanitary than other collections, but no less important. Recent findings by Isparian adventurers, the High Queen, Lugian Sages and Tumerok Mystics, has resulted in a wide-spread belief that the Sclavus are an amalgam of creatures. Yes, this was first proffered forth by other more notable scholars, but even the recent findings are still full of conjecture. Perhaps the Sclavus that l...

Inside the crate you'll find several bags labeled for the different body parts that are commonly harvested from the Sclavus. You should collect the specimens in the following order and then place them into the bags in the crate. The outside of the crate also has the order listed. But I want to make certain that I have done my best to inform you of your duty. Collect the small hide of the creatu...

Not long ago I met a rugged traveler from the Island town of MacNiall's Freehold. This savvy traveler struck an efficacious deal with me, one that I intend to uphold as best I can. I'm to deliver a collection of treated herbs to him in exchange for some information that he has been collecting for me. If you're so disposed to assisting me, bring these herbs to MacNiall and return to me with the...
Be swift, MacNiall's information is very important to our cause of unity. Hurry along now.

An old friend of mine, Gorak, was sent to support the besieged town at Dryreach. Unfortunately, Gorak was sent to the beleaguered city before he had time to pick up his new axe. If you'd be so kind to deliver the axe and collect payment from Gorak for the work, I am certain that I can muster a small reward for you.
Please, hurry. Every moment that Gorak is without his axe is another that the townsfolk of Dryreach live in danger of invasion.
Though many believe that we Lugian's have either thrown our lot in with High Queen Elysa or with that traitorous dog, Muldaveus.
Captain K'rank spits.

Excuse me... That belief is untrue. Some Lugians actually struck out on their own when Nuhmudira was claiming that she desired to create a grand place of learning. One such Lugian, Olcris, joined with Nuhmudira and started acting very strangely. Well... my reach isn't so short that I don't have eyes on him. In fact, I have a contact at the Beach Fort that keeps up with all his comings and going...
It's a small price to pay someone for such important information. Feruza's reports and return them to me for a fair reward.

I am certain that you're aware that we assisted in the reclamation and restoration process of Wai Jhou, yes? I was never given to trying to make a swamp city better. Honestly, it's in a swamp. They'll be lucky if that town doesn't fall down, sink into the swamp, then burn and sink into the swamp before a real city thrives there. I'm sorry, got a little off topic. We have a worker stationed ther...
Kreavon is responsible for collecting minerals, they can get quite heavy over time. We've crafted this wheelcart for his use. Would you mind brining it to him?
Wait for Kreavon to fill the cart, then return it to me for a fair reward.
Captain K'rank exclaims, %tn, "You have killed the Burun leader, Morgluuk!"
This head is proof of what you have done. All should know your name.

%tn has slain Morgluuk and returned his head to the Lugian capital of Linvak Tukal. There it is to be placed on a pike as a symbol of victory for the Isparian, Lugian and Tumerok people and a symbol of defeat for the Burun that threaten our way of life. Huzzah, %tn!
You must be rewarded for your efforts.
The portal gem will take you into the High Queen's Vault. There you will find many chests that house treasures and weaponry that has been worked on by the finest smiths in the land.
Captain K'rank says, "Take your gift and use it well, %tn. You are deserved of much praise in this victory."
Captain K'rank says, "That is the final reward I have for you. You have become a hero to all of Dereth, %tn. I shall never forget your name or your deeds."

greetings: I have no need of such reconnaissance. But you would do well to heed the words within it. It appears the Virindi have some plan for you Isparians.

This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Amaroth. He may be found in Holtburg at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.
This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Urleg. He may be found in Yaraq at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.
quest: You are a young Isparian, aren't you? I fear that you lack the power to aid me in this endeavor.
Isparian, hear my offer.

Working with my citadel brothers, I discovered a way to construct forges which will bestow crafting boons to those that use it. We desire to place these forges within our citadels that we might better equip our warriors with the supplies which are so necessary in combat.

However, we require the assistance of one brave enough to delve the depths of the Virindi Power Forges. The Overseers of those Forges carry a Forge Essence which I need if I am to construct these crafting boons.
If you can venture into one of these pits and retrieve a Forge Essence, I will reward you handsomely. In addition, in my appreciation I will place five crafting forges for all of your people to use.
The Northern Power Forge lies upon the northern shore of the Inner Sea. Be safe, young Isparian, and be quick. My time here is short. I shall leave your lands before the snow recedes.
You are quite the powerful Isparian. Too powerful, I fear, for such a quest as I have to bestow.
Isparian, you have done both our races a great service.
%mn smiles broadly.
If you were not so small, I would invite you to join our citadel as a fellow in arms.
I shall not forget my promise. As a gesture of appreciation, I shall erect a series of crafting forges in the town of Shoushi.

%tn has defeated the Northern Overseer and delivered its Forge Essence to the Lugian Kerrak. In exchange, Kerrak has assembled and activated the crafting forges in the town of Shoushi. Crafters the world over owe a debt of gratitude to the mighty %tn!
The incantations necessary to create these forges are arcane indeed! Please wait a moment, I suddenly feel the need to meditate upon them.
Half a moment, as I contemplate the infinite crafting mysteries of the universe!
Ah! The beauty of my crafting forges! I am so fortunate that such a brave adventurer was able to bring me the forge essence that I required.
Such a lovely day we're having, don't you agree?
Voila! I have finished my meditations. Alright, who's next?
This is your reward by rights, Isparian. I would not deprive you of such a boon, though I thank you for your kindness.

greetings: Try giving that to the Tumerok my friend.
Try giving that to the Human my friend.
I'm sorry, I'm not in charge of collecting that type of material. Try seeing if the other collectors, Caelis or Aun Teverea, need any of that.
You are off on a wonderful adventure of stone.
Ahh, my friend K'rank finally got around to sending someone to collect the most recent collections, eh? Well, I hope your back is strong Isparian. This load would make the stoutest Mattekar whimper.
Kreavon loads several collections of minerals onto the wheelcart then passes it to you.
Be careful out there, if you get caught and surrounded before you return that to K'rank you are liable to end up next to a lifestone. Give K'rank my best.
quest: Well met Isparian.  I am Kreavon, a Linvak Lugian and also a member of the new alliance.  All Lugians loyal to Lord Krevesous are sworn members of the alliance.

We are assigned to this outpost near Wai Jhou, to collect building materials for the continued upkeep of Candeth Keep, the South Direlands stronghold. I will accept all types of salvaged stone and gem that you can afford to donate to the cause.  Large or small, your donations will be treated equally.
Would you care to provide us with more materials? I accept all types of salvaged stone and gem that you can afford to donate to the cause.
Hello again, your continued help is most welcome! Any salvaged stone or gem you can donate is greatly appreciated.
This is a good start friend. The Lugian planners continue work on the walls of Candeth Keep and the upkeep of the town. We need to supply them with a continuing supply of materials.
You are off to a very good start.  Yet, materials are still in short supply.  Please continue to bring me what you can.  Rock or gem, all materials are needed for Candeth Keep.
This is a fine haul, friend.  I have found my renegade brethren in the underground mines keep gemstone weaponry close at hand.  Seems like they must be mining more than just Chorizite down there, eh?
You have given me one-half the stone and gem materials that I would ask of you. The residents of Candeth Keep shall know you by your name and your deeds.
Lugian, Tumerok, and Isparian -- all working together. I never thought I would see the day. But we have unified in our common goal to build Candeth Keep and make it a foothold in the South Dires.
You have given much to help the alliance.  More materials are still needed, but rest assured you have donated the bulk of the quota set forth by the alliance council.

The storehouses are beginning to fill with the materials you and the others have generously given to the cause.  We now have enough materials to make another delivery to Candeth Keep, but we will surely need more to maintain our stronghold.
Friend, your hard work has paid off.  You have given the most that can be donated by any one member.

You will be welcomed in Candeth Keep as a co-founder.  Your donations of mineral and gemstone will be most beneficial to the continued work on the stronghold.  I am sure that those who have given of themselves will be rewarded in time.
If you would like to be known as a skilled miner, return this token to me.
If you're going to be mining you should have the proper headgear. Take this hat and wear it to keep your small skull from being crushed.

You have given one-half the resources of which the alliance is seeking from each member.  It is people like you who will be considered the true founders of Candeth Keep.  The alliance has allocated a symbolic gift for all of those who show dedication to the project.
You have helped us greatly. You can be sure that your efforts in continuing to provide materials for Candeth Keep will not go unrewarded.
You have given more than enough materials my friend. Perhaps the other collectors still require other materials.

greetings: What am I to do with this?  Pick my teeth?  Bah!
This is indeed armor from one of the Gotrok Leaders.  On behalf of Linvak Tukal, I bless you with this gift.
This is one of the treasures stolen from our vault by the Gotrok!  Thank you for it's return.  In order to show my appreciation, I will forge you a replacement.
This is one of the old artifacts of station within our ranks.  Because of your valor in smiting the thief, you may keep it as as symbol of trust.  But here, let me fix it for you.
This is the pauldron of one of the Gotrok generals!  I have been studying the other soft ones in the area, and have tried to master your armorsmithing ways.
Here is one of my first models.  I hope you like it.
Aha! An example of my earlier work. Allow me to improve it for you.
Greetings, soft one.  I am Ulkas, Master smith of Linvak Tukal.
The Gotrok looted the donjon of Linvak, taking all they could carry.  Many of the items have not true value, but some are quite dangerous in the wrong hands...
My skills have grown over the past few years. If I made an item for you in the past, I would be happy to improve it for you.
My Lord has given me the right to craft items as a reward to those who bring trophies from exceptionally strong Lugians.
Have you met my apprentice?  His name is Krage, and he is a quick study.  If I do not live long enough to see the end of this siege, he will make a good Master Smith.
quest: I am not worthy to possess such an item.  Please, return it to one of the emissaries my people sent to contact you.
I do not want this, Isparian.
This seems to be a miniature relic of my people.  It is of no use to a grown Lugian such as myself.  Perhaps a child, or someone their size would find it of use...
Defending the town my Patron!
We are guarding the gates against intruders. Please move on.
chatter: HALT! Who goes there?

greetings: I'm here to Survey this land under the authority of the Arcanum.
I'm surveying this land for the Arcanum. Please move on, I have much to do.
chatter: The %n looks over the crater and makes a mark on his instrument.
The %n adjusts some metal rings on his device.
The %n sights along a line he has drawn in the dirt.

greetings: I have no need of such reconnaissance. But you would do well to heed the words within it. It appears the Virindi have some plan for you Isparians.

This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Kerrak. He may be found in Shoushi at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.
This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Urleg. He may be found in Yaraq at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.

Isparian, hear my offer.

Working with my citadel brothers, I discovered a way to construct forges which will bestow crafting boons to those that use it. We desire to place these forges within our citadels that we might better equip our warriors with the supplies which are so necessary in combat.

However, we require the assistance of one brave enough to delve the depths of the Virindi Power Forges. The Overseers of those Forges carry a Forge Essence which I need if I am to construct these crafting boons.

You are quite the powerful Isparian. Too powerful, I fear, for such a quest as I have to bestow.
Isparian, you have done both our races a great service.
%mn smiles broadly.
If you were not so small, I would invite you to join our citadel as a fellow in arms.
I shall not forget my promise. As a gesture of appreciation, I shall erect a series of crafting forges in the town of Holtburg.

%tn has defeated the Southern Overseer and delivered its Forge Essence to the Lugian Amaroth. In exchange, Amaroth has assembled and activated the crafting forges in the town of Holtburg. Crafters the world over owe a debt of gratitude to the mighty %tn!
The incantations necessary to create these forges are arcane indeed! Please wait a moment, I suddenly feel the need to meditate upon them.
Half a moment, as I contemplate the infinite crafting mysteries of the universe!
Ah! The beauty of my crafting forges! I am so fortunate that such a brave adventurer was able to bring me the forge essence that I required.
Such a lovely day we're having, don't you agree?
Voila! I have finished my meditations. Alright, who's next?
This is your reward by rights, Isparian. I would not deprive you of such a boon, though I thank you for your kindness.

greetings: This looks like one of those Idol heads those crazy Vesayen mosswarts worship. Hmmm, it's a lot smaller though. You could see if Grearrk, the mosswart living outside Sawato, knows anything about this.
Very pretty.
Such a deep blue. A fine jewel.
Very nicely cut! I'll take this.
A pleasure doing business.
This is quite a fancy jewel!
I might be able to cut a gem like this given enough time...
Ah, yes, these make fine jewels.
Here is a finished one for you.
Ah, not a stone lover?
Take these then, everyone finds pyreal useful.
I work these into perfect spheres.
Nice craftsmanship, eh?
This is a very impressive rock! Here, take one that I've finished cutting and polishing.
The light flickers in it's facets like a black fire. Use that in an Empyrean Weapon.
Here's what I make of those stones.
If you stare into the gems dark center for awhile you can almost make out... movement.
Haha, an unsettling optical illusion. Probably related to it's magical properties.
Oh good, a banderling scalp. Here, take this unpolished gem if you like.
I cure these to make soft rags that I use to polish my stones and gems.
You don't want it? Well, ok, take some coin instead.
It may look dull now, but wait till I'm through with it.
Yes, very good.
I have something for that.
Thank you.
Golem hearts are fine.
Good, good.
Granite? Yes, I need that.
Very pure Iron.
My thanks.
This is a nice chunk of ice.
Nice hunk of obsidian.
You're lucky to find one of these!
A heart of pure pyreal!
This is very valuable.
A heart of pure platinum!
Not sure what to do with it.
Perhaps I'll try cutting it.
Good for magic, but I can use it too.
Ah, Sunstone is truly a beautiful gem. A shame that clumsy hands have marred it as such. I shall restore it for you.
Pagrok pulls a few small vials of oil and a pair of fine chisels from a nearby pack. As he finishes the repairs, he polishes the gauntlets and hands them back to you.
I will take a number of trophy stones and jewels, such as virindi jewels, swamp stones, iron, copper, and granite golem hearts.
I'll also take banderling trophies.  But what I really specialize in are the rare black rocks, black stones, and the repair of Sunstone Gauntlets.
chatter: Have you seen any strange black rocks or stones?  If you give me one, I will give you back a piece of it cut into the shape of a pretty gem.
I'm looking for various stones.  Not just any, but only from certain monsters.  I'll also take swamp stones or banderling scalps.
I hear that obsidian comes from volcanoes, or from intense magical disruptions.
The great Obsidian Plain in the Direlands is quite a sight, but I do not like the feel of the place.  I hear it was caused by some kind of powerful magic.
I'll also give you money for some of the trophy jewels you may have, but people tell me my prices aren't very good.

greetings: No, this is for you.  I have no need of the Writ.  Use it to acquire your new home!  Even if you have purchased the house, some dwellings further require them for maintenance payments.

What an interesting ... umm ... mechanism! I have no idea what it's for! But you know, those Arcanum Researchers, they've been working with odd metals like this -- you should ask one of them. You can find them in the libraries in Cragstone, Hebian-To, or Zaikhal.
We need all the ingots we can get.  One day, you will be grateful we have such a stockpile.

A rare find!  My congratulations.  Here is your Writ of Refuge.  The Empyrean have left many secrets for us to puzzle out.  Their geomancy recently became transparent to us.  This powder might reveal yet another crucial part of their power.  We shall crush the enemy through their own devices!
Thank you for bringing us this Niffis Pearl. It is thought it may be useful. Take this Writ as your reward.
Well! Would you look at this! This should be useful!
We thought this jelly was useless for a time. But we've recently discovered it has certain properties which are of much interest to us. Please, take this Writ as a reward.
We feared we would never be able to lay our hands on this poison again. Thank you for choosing to part with such a rare item!
From this day forward %s shall be known as Gaerlan Slayer.
This is a strange device indeed. I have never seen anything like this before. Hmm...
The Agent ponders this strange new item momentarily.
I'll tell you what. I'll take this thing off your hands and give you a Writ of Refuge in exchange! Sounds like a good enough deal, eh? Then it is settled!

I've seen a number of pearls in my days... You know we exchange Niffis Pearls for writs correct? ... Anyway, I have seen a number of pearls before, but this is obviously not from any niffis I've seen.

Look at how dark this pearl is, it seems to eat the very light around it. This is a truly rare find, some ancient Empyrean decoration no doubt, but I can't imagine it would be very different from the niffis pearls we know of.
I'll give you a special deal on this pearl, since it is obviously of a different quality than your common niffis pearls.
Ah yes, I seem to recall that our leather crafters stopped making shirts out of these. Don't worry, we have plenty in stock. Here, let me get you a shirt this hide.
I am glad to get rid of another of these shirts. Much too small for one such as I to wear.
Forge Essence! We can surely use as much of this as you can lay your hands on.
Thank you. If you need to see the list of tradable items again, just ask.
There are few beasts on Dereth as feared and hated as the Margul Sezzherei. To meet one who has personally slain the creature... I cannot believe it!
You should be commended for your efforts. From this point forward, let it be known to all that you are the Sezzherei Slayer!
quest: %n shakes their head at you condemningly.
You are still a cur unworthy of trust. I am only too grateful to the wisdom and compassion of others. With their help, and theirs alone was Nuhmudira freed.

You are fortunate that she has pity within her heart enough to grant you the trappings that you need to obtain housing. If you give me any of these items listed here, then I will grudgingly give you a Writ of Refuge.
%n smiles at you gently.
You have done much to help us. Your sacrifice and actions assisted Nuhmudira in her darkest hour and we thank you for those efforts.
If you have not yet done so, seek out Balthazar outside of Lin. He will instruct you on how you may further aid us.

Housing continues to be provided through a joint effort of the Arcanum and the High Queen. Writs are required for these domiciles. Once you possess a Writ of Refuge, seek out a Covenant Stone and determine what else is needed to purchase your homestead. Also of note are new dwellings that have been opened that offer a more communal living arrangement.
Here is a list items we will accept in exchange for writs.
%n salutes you.

Thank you for investigating this matter for the Arcanum!  No, we do not yet comprehend the extent of the schemes of this minion.  I have confidence we shall find out soon, though.  Here is your Writ.  As of this time, we do not need any further tokens from you.  We will however still take the other trophies I mentioned to you.
Wow! Great work. Here is your reward. You are looking a little green my friend. Are you feeling okay?
We only wanted to see that you had achieved what we asked. Seeing as how you did so well you should keep this.
You never know, you may find a use for it yet.
Wow! Great work. Here is your reward. Umm, I think your britches may be burning.
Wow! Great work. Here is your reward. You know your hair looks as though it is standing on end.
Wow! Great work. Here is your reward. Was it cold in there?
I have recently rewarded you for visiting revenge up on that madman. Please come back to me in one day before asking for another reward.
The Agent bows their head low and speaks softly.

Although Nuhmudira has returned to us, we have learned that there is still a way to show your support for her. Outside of Stonehold there is a portal to the dungeon where she was once imprisoned. There you can choose to sacrifice yourself for her or to abandon her to her fate. It is odd that the magic has yet to dissipate.

If you require writs we will accept any of the items on this list in exchange for a writ. Once you possess a Writ of Refuge, and have satisfied the other requirements for purchasing a home, seek out one of the homestead areas that we have built. If you would rather, you can enjoy living in one of the new dwelling areas that have been established for a more communal living arrangement.
I already informed you that we no longer need any tokens from you.  We will however still take the other trophies I mentioned to you.
Wow! You were able to navigate that place again. Great Job! We are not giving repeat offenders the Writs, but everything else is still available.
I see that you have visited revenge upon the man that wanted to bring our race to an end. Nuhmudira thanks you for this. Here is your reward.
If you hand the token back to me I will make sure that you are recognized for your efforts. The madness of his reign is over and now we can move forward.

greetings: I need you to take this to Captain K'rank in Linvak Tukal. He has been researching several of the odd occurrences that have plagued our peoples in the past year. He may conscript you to help him.
Ahh, an Isparian. We must be quick. If I am seen talking to you then I will surely be killed and all that I have worked for will be lost.

My efforts to uncover the details of the treaty between the Burun and the Renegades has turned up very little as of yet. Though I have managed to garner enough information to provide Captain K'rank with enough to formulate a strike against the Renegades and Burun.
I have no need of such reconnaissance. But you would do well to heed the words within it. It appears the Virindi have some plan for you Isparians.

This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Kerrak. He may be found in Shoushi at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.

This is not the Forge Essence which I require. Perhaps you should visit my kinsman, Amaroth. He may be found in Holtburg at the moment. But you must not tarry. We shall not remain on your shores for long.

Isparian, you have done both our races a great service.
%mn smiles broadly.
If you were not so small, I would invite you to join our citadel as a fellow in arms.
I shall not forget my promise. As a gesture of appreciation, I shall erect a series of crafting forges in the town of Yaraq

%tn has defeated the Western Overseer and delivered its Forge Essence to the Lugian Urleg. In exchange, Urleg has assembled and activated the crafting forges in the town of Yaraq. Crafters the world over owe a debt of gratitude to the mighty %tn!
The incantations necessary to create these forges are arcane indeed! Please wait a moment, I suddenly feel the need to meditate upon them.
Half a moment, as I contemplate the infinite crafting mysteries of the universe!
Ah! The beauty of my crafting forges! I am so fortunate that such a brave adventurer was able to bring me the forge essence that I required.
Such a lovely day we're having, don't you agree?
Voila! I have finished my meditations. Alright, who's next?
This is your reward by rights, Isparian. I would not deprive you of such a boon, though I thank you for your kindness.

greetings: This is indeed armor of station amongst the Gotrok.  By presenting it to me, I am assuming you defeated it in combat?  Show this to Ulkas, and he will reward you for you great deed.
This is an old crest with the symbol of our fortress on it.  Perhaps you can get Ulkas to repair it for you.

This is one of the old scepters of office we brought with us through the rifts.  They were traditionally held by our defenders, before they were slain in combat.  Due to your deeds, I think you should keep this.  If you wish, Master Ulkas will repair it for you, and refuel its inner power.

This pauldron belongs to one of the Gotrok generals!  You are indeed mighty to have slain it.  Perhaps if you show it to Ulkas, you will impress him.  He is not easily shocked, however the fact you have slain a Gotrok general...
I am not worthy to possess such an item.  Please, return it to one of the emissaries my people sent to contact you.
These are grim tidings indeed. But valuable - most valuable information. You have done Linvak Tukal a great service. You are indeed marked for greatness.
Balor... What have they done to you?
Lord Kresovus slumps forward, obviously overcome with grief. After a short moment, he remembers himself, his position, and his company. Lord Kresovus straightens his back and looks you in the eye.
I thank you for your service. The heart grieves, but...
Thank you.

Greetings, small one. You have come at a most critical time. After years of siege, our walls have been breached. Though not by the Gotrok. Some other foul tribe forced their way past defenses which have long stood fast. A tribe of some foul thing I cannot begin to describe. Bodies usurped, brothers possessed... the mind recoils at such horrors.

These fiends invaded under cover of darkness. They attacked while I slept. They meant to slay me - or take me prisoner - I do not know which. There was one with them, one whose appearance matched my own! I do believe he meant to assume control of Linvak Tukal in my stead.

Were it not for the valiant efforts of Captain K'rank, and my own doomed Balor, I fear I would have been overwhelmed. As it turns out, we were not overwhelmed. We repelled the invaders. But not without our own casualties.
Several of our own were taken prisoner by these beasts of Shadow. And Balor... my dear Balor...
My scouts tracked the demons to a location in the northernmost reaches of the Direlands. I fear I do not know more than that.
If you seek to aid us in this conflict, find these demons. Slay these demons. Return whatever information you might find.
And if you happen to find him, please do return my precious Balor to me.
quest: I am not worthy to possess such an item.  Please, return it to one of the emissaries my people sent to contact you.
I do not want this, Isparian.
Wonderous! Wear these with pride, human, for they are a strong portion of my people's beliefs.
chatter: Lord Kresovus rears back and screams a great cry of anguish to the uncaring skies above. "BAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLOOOOOOOOOOOOOOORR!!!!!"

greetings: K'rank is the best soldier we have. He really knows how to take care of his men. Bring this back to him and make sure that the funds reach the smith.
Gorak runs a thick, calloused finger along the edge of the blade.
This will certainly split a few thick skulls.

We've been stationed here to maintain the tenuous peace. We're simply here reinforcing these walls and providing a strong show of support for you and your people. But you and I know, we're warriors. If these Tumeroks ever got organized they could tear these walls down and slaughter all these folk before we could defeat them all. I'm hopeful though that our wayward brothers will find their way b...
chatter: The Tumerok and Lugians that have betrayed their brethren shall not breach these walls as long as Gorak breathes.
Of course there are Lugian females, but we do look an awful lot alike.

greetings: Balor growls in warning...
Balor eyes you warily.
%mn throws the Wallbound Niffis back in your face. It is clear that she is angry with you for rejecting her gift.

%mn ponders the note for a long moment. She looks you in the eye and your heart breaks at the sadness you glimpse beneath those dark, melancholy orbs. This is a fighter who has abandoned those that love her. And for what? Glory? Acceptance? Approval from those who would use her for naught but entertainment? Or worse, for profit?

%mn regards you for a time, then nods her head. You don't quite understand what passes between you, but you think it feels a little something like gratitude. Perhaps you have helped this poor, small Niffis. Perhaps you have pointed out the path - that path which all of us seek - towards contentment.

%mn's tentacles quiver, as if itching to lash out. You get the feeling that this is a well-trained and well-disciplined fighter and you know, deep in your heart, that she will not hurt you now. No, she will not. She's saving it for the ring.
chatter: %mn flexes her tentacles.
%mn beats the air rapidly with her wings.

%mn sighs deeply. You get the feeling that beneath her prize-fighting, rough and tumble exterior lies an ocean of despair and longing. You wonder just what could cause such a deep feeling of sadness in one who has accomplished so much. Yet before you can question her, she wipes away a purple tear with one shaking tentacle, cocks her head, and resumes her previous stance of fighter, champion, wa...

quest: You have completed this quest too recently.
You take the Sword of Frozen Fury from the dais.
You have not proven yourself worthy of wielding this sword.

chatter: The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "Sap of Alaidain. Sap of Karishna. The watchful stars turn, man of the south. Soon they shall return. But in that coming, there shall be turning. One shall be another. They shall not know you. There shall be no singing, and no sleep."

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "How death comes: the great sap of the earth runs to dust, the maw yawns like the idle hunter, branches of eternal feversleep rake poison across the writhing bark of the world."
The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "The saplings of the warmer light and the cleaner light shall crowd each other out."

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "A sapling shall stand before the seeds of the warmer light. The sapling is bent to loathe its sap, the man of the south, and all seeds of the cleaner light. Weights of earth and anger shall be tied to it, and the sapling shall bend in pain and confusion. But there shall be none to comfort, for the...
The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind, as if a sibilant, chattering voice were saying, "Where be the women with the totems in their hair?"

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind, as if a sibilant, chattering voice were saying, "Beast you are, Watcher, and no planter of stones. We shall have our own. Her eyes shall be clear water. She shall stand at the side of the great and chosen, though not always both at once. She shall whisper in the dark, and that shall resound evermore."

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind, as if a sibilant, chattering voice were saying, "Marked was the coming of you, man no longer man. Your seedbearer's sap stains still your leaves. The women teach you false and foolish things."

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind, as if a sibilant, chattering voice were saying, "Auraken. Wind-Lord. Go not among your people evermore. Fly, fly to the high home. Too late, too late. The spore's mark has run its course among them. They fall and bite. Your kin shed lambent tears, and are forgotten."
The wind blows mournfully through the trees.
The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind, as if a sibilant, chattering voice were saying, "Cold..."
The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "Seek the dead one where the waters twine and twist into their own life."

The dead leaves of the trees above you rustle in the wind. A sibilant, chattering voice breathes, "When all the circles are broken, she comes. The air smells of her. Her children smell her. greetings: The loom cranks noisily and weaves the silk thread from the spool into a fine white cloth.
You feed the infected assailer fur into the loom, hoping it does not break the machine.
The loom produces a thick, braided cord of tusker fur.
The loom cranks noisily, but without any thread it fails to make anything.
The wheel spins the silk into a fine thread, which winds onto a spool.
The wheel spins to life, but without any material to spin it slows and stops.
You shift the spyglass and it spins around, changing the numbers displayed on the wheel mechanisms.
You spin the spyglass around. It comes to rest in roughly the same position it started in, you think.
The spyglass spins around and around. That was fun.
Ah, yes, this is obviously some sort of magical device. You press the little button near the base of the instrument.
With the locking mechanism released the spyglass spins freely.
You look through the spyglass and see the tumerok shamman drumming in front of a tree. Numbers seem to float by him and...
Ooops.

quest: You look through the pockets of the pack, but it appears as though there is nothing of value left in it.
You look over the tattered pack. Anything of interest within it seems to have been taken by someone or something.
On the front of the pack you notice the emblem of the Strathelar Royal Guard pinned to the front pouch.
You can find nothing else of interest in the pack.
You receive a paper-cut while shuffling through the pack.
You rummage through the papers again. Amazing, you never realized that the Renegades were so organized.
You find a little green lump of putty and drop it in disgust.
Wait, you think you feel the point of a powerful weapon!
No, just a quill.
You find a small scrap of folded paper. It reads: I don't trust Maloth, he would trade his own mother for a chance at advancement. Please, reconsider his promotion.
You reach into the pack and rummage through the papers.
You find an important looking letter and worn book.

greetings: Virindi-altered Utelari yelps from %s's fatal blow! She collapses on her side, never again to bay at the moons.
Utelari howls cheerfully over the corpse of %s!
Utelari's muzzle drops into a lazy parody of a grin as she spies %s!
Utelari bays for assistance from the pack!
Tuperea whistles for Utelari to heel.
Utelari's eyes flash violet as %s's spell slides off her.
"Reshalra! No!" Tuperea cries as %s lands a killing blow on the brutish hunting reedshark.
Reshalra tears a hunk of meat from %s's corpse, and his muscular form bounds away seeking new prey.
Reshalra whirls to face %s, his lips curling back into a feral snarl.
Reshalra bays for assistance from the pack!
Tuperea whistles for Reshalra to heel.
A shudder passes through Reshalra's massive form as %s's blow finds a weak point.
Huntmaster Tuperea howls in anguish as %s releases loyal Sahkurea's soul from the prison of her Virindi-augmented body.
The relentless Sahkurea has run %s to ground!
Sahkurea perks up at the sound of %s's footsteps.
Sahkurea bays for assistance from the pack!
Tuperea whistles for Sahkurea to heel.
Tuperea cries out in dismay as nimble Manuaka falls to %s's attack!
The lithe Manuaka bounds over the collapsing bulk of %s, then races away.
Manuaka's muzzle twitches as he catches the scent of %s!
Manuaka bays for assistance from the pack!
Tuperea whistles for Manuaka to heel.

As the Shaman dies, it lets out a curse in an unintelligible language. It's death throes will alert Morgluuk and he will dispatch shamans from his lair to learn of what happened here. His lair will be weaker.
%s has struck a deadly blow to Kiree! As the behemoth falls to the ground lifeless, several bits of his flesh fall to the ground.
Kiree turns his attentions toward you and with a gesture of his bulbous head, your body is washed in pure mana. As he chortles you feel weaker and he looks stronger.
With a mighty croak, Kiree, snaps his head back in anger. A deadly spray of acid squirts from his hide.
As you open a large gash along Kiree's hide you are struck with a wave of noxious fumes. The wound begins to knit immediately.
Your blow tears a patch of flesh from Kiree's hide. As it falls away, a sour smell assails your nostrils and acid shoots from his hide.
With a chortle, Kiree reels his head back and retaliates for your assault.
Your blow bites deeply into Kiree's body. The giant reels a bit under the blow and then seems to be washed in a glow of mana.
You wound the giant deeply. The scent of a heady fungus flows about the area and Kiree's hide looks to have become thicker.
Kiree curls his lips toward you as you open a wound on his flesh. A spray of acid leaps from the wound.
As you open a wound on Kiree's hide, you are overwhelmed with a feeling of nausea.
You wound Kiree grievously. But the wound also allows a fetid scent to escape the beast.
Your tear into Kiree's hide, wounding the beast and sending a foul cloud of spores into the air.

Kiree rears back and opens his mouth wide. A hideous smell emits from within the behemoth's gullet and he thrusts himself forward scooping you into his mouth. Darkness envelops you and you fall toward the beasts stomach.
Finding your attempt to bestow ill magics upon him laughable, Kiree responds with a spell of his own.
A deep gurgle that sounds like a laugh issues from Kiree. The air around him becomes foul.
Your magic dissolves around the buulky King. He finds your impotence amusing and responds with a vile enchantment.
A look of amusement courses through Kiree's eyes and he croaks out an incantation that falls upon you.
As your magic fails to penetrate Kiree's defenses he absently waves a hand weakening your connection to mana.
As your spell trickles harmlessly away into nothingness, Kiree finds amusement in causing you more grief.
Finding a trickle of mana drift away from your failed attack, Kiree turns the errant mana into a formidable assault.
A glimmer of recognition lights in Kiree's Eye. Your feeble attempt at casting a spell upon him has earned you his attention.
Laughing, Kiree retaliates for your failed assault.
Your magic dissipates, but you have earned the notice of the Burun King.
