Of course, it's been years since I've tasted butter... Get me a bug's long claw and I might make you one. Make sure the long claw is nice and pointy.  And freshly killed.
This should work.
Teela makes a spear out of the Olthoi long claw.

greetings: I remember a man, or maybe it was a woman, I am not truly sure so many people come through here to talk to me. At any rate they bought a large quantity of my Cove Apple Cider not long ago.
Wait, wait... I think it was Ulgrim the Unpleasant.
It's certainly not bark from on of the trees in my cove. Maybe it's from up north.
I'm sorry, this looks like it belongs to someone else. You might try Ulgrim.
I don't deal in fineries of this type. But I know that tailors do. In fact this looks like To-ping Ra's work.
I know not where you found this, but it is not from my orchard. My Cove Apples are the finest in Dereth.
This isn't my daughter's! I can tell just by smelling it.
You know, I used to have faith in my fellow man, but trying to pass this bruised apple for one found in my orchard re-affirms my belief that people are untrustworthy!
Ah, yes. You must have found this in the orchard. Allow me to gift you with one of my daughter's pies.
One of my good apples! Thank you so much!
My special baking pan! You know, I made this myself - it helps keep the juicy goodness in the pie. Thank you so much!
My special apple knife! You know, I made this myself. It's especially sharp, so that I don't bruise the apples as I cut them. Thank you so much!
Ah, some of the good stuff! You have my thanks!
Ah, some of the very good stuff! You have my thanks!
Ah, some of the best stuff! You have my thanks!
I don't drink this myself, but it's popular with the mages. Thank you for returning it to me.
Thank you for returning this pie! It's even still hot - that was quick work!
My daughter baked one of her pies for you! She makes the finest in the A'mun Desert. Not that there's much competition out here, mind. But don't tell her I said that!
Can I help you, traveler? Well, but perhaps you can help me.

I am the owner of the orchards, and the purveyor of delicious and sundry goods made from the finest Cove apples. Lately, though, I am beleaguered by a pesky band of drudges that has been stealing all my goods! I need someone who is willing to defeat these drudges and recover my goods for me.
Here is a list of what they have taken. Return these items to me and I will reward you appropriately.

I believe that these drudges are holed up in the Sea Temple Catacombs, on a plateau at the mouth of the harbor. But rumor has it that there is an easier entrance, through the Rat's Nest just northwest of town.
If you need more help finding either location, you can buy directions from Jubal at the bar in Yaraq proper.
quest: That's for you to keep. Enjoy!
You found something of Abmim's! Quick, take this to Ma'yad in Yaraq! She must be worried sick!
I don't want this! But it looks like the sort of thing Akyafi might be interested in. Why don't you try taking it to him?
My dear daughter Mara is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to her? She can usually be found in the bar in town.
chatter: The sea is beautiful, is it not? I should miss it if we find a way to return to our deserts in Ispar.
Oh, those cursed Drudges... Can't they find someplace else to steal food from?
Another shipment of cider waylaid by Drudges... may their bones be devoured by sand!

greetings: I cannot read this. It looks like a clue though. Did you find anything else?
Why give this to me? I cannot read Falatacot... if that is what this strange language is.
These are lies fabricated by some confused creature. My dear friend Gareth is dead and we must prove that to our Lady there. I will keep this so that she does not get confused.
Did you find nothing to prove what we already know?
quest: %mn glares at you with distaste.
You had to tell her.
What good did you do her by telling her that her husband is now some hideous freak? I asked you to do a simple task and put my Lady's mind at peace, but you just had to go and ruin everything!
%mn's eyes suddenly loose their ferocity and he straightens up.
Well, what's done is done. Take your little magic staff and leave us. I have to comfort Talira. I'll make it all right.
You think you see a slight smile on his face.
I owe you a great debt my friend. You have helped my Lady put her late husband behind her. With my help she will learn to be happy once more.
I have told you of the temple to the west. Search for a great sandstorm and find it's eye.
Lady Dain may be able to tell you something of use, but I warn you not to cause her undo stress.
%mn glares at you in disgust.
You can't fix the damage you've done now.
Leave us! I'll dispose of this myself.
You already gave me a copy of this. The deed has been done and I have rewarded you for your services. You aren't trying to trick me are you?
Hello friend, did Lady Dain ask you to speak with me?
I must ask a favor of you. I recently discovered something while searching for my long lost friend Gareth Dain.

I was exploring the wastelands west of here when a giant sandstorm blew in out of nowhere. It stung my face and made it almost impossible to breathe, but I forced my way onward. I eventually came to a calm at the center of the storm where I found an ancient temple. When I approached the structure a great number of Sclavus sprung from the sands and attacked, forcing me to retreat.

I have told Lady Dain what I discovered and we believe that this is the very Sclavus Temple that Gareth was last seen at. I do not however hold her belief that her husband still lives. She has obsessed over his disappearance for three years now and I dearly wish to see her mourning end.

Do her a noble deed and find proof of her husband's death. I am sure that my friend Gareth would have come back if humanly possible, so I know him to be dead. I ask of you to be sure that you bring only proof of his death, she has suffered enough and I could not bear to see her suffering continue. Do this for me and I will reward you.
You have done my Lady and myself a great service. You are truly worthy of my friendship.
Take this staff as a small token of my appreciation.

greetings: What's this? A letter? Oh, from Elysa! Such a dear girl. I'll read this later. Thank you.
quest: Do you enjoy the view from here as much as I do?

Well, hello! My name is Alatar Locke. I am a cartographer for the Explorer Society. I was beginning to think no Isparians would ever make it to this place! I ended up here after spending quite a bit of time in the Floating City. I must say I do enjoy it here. From a good height, one can study the lay of the land and for one of my avocation that is quite a happy thing! In my spare time I have be...
If you would like to have the map framed, I understand there is a Furniture Master in Zaikhal that may frame it for you. His name is Jordan Ibn'Ikia and he does quality work for little money.

greetings: Isn't it lovely? I do so like the Virindi countenance.
No, no -- you keep that! It's a work of art!
No, no thank you. I don't like the feel of this one.
Diyas al-Yat shivers.
You might try that ... Virindi ... in Yanshi.
Ugh. I don't want that!
No, no thank you. I don't like the feel of this one. And Leopold won't take it either.
Excellent! Allow me to translate this for you. Very strange ... I wonder what the Virindi are up to?
Very curious indeed! Those Virindi must be up to something!
Hey, money, I appreciate it. Between my scholarly work and my poetry, I don't make a lot of money. Oh, you didn't know I was a poet? Here's my latest poem, I hope you like it.
I can't make any sense of this. From what I understand there is a translator at Hebian-to that specializes in this language ... Or was it Cragstone?
This is a new one ... they have some sort of emissary in southern Osteth now?
What's this? What kind of fiendish experiments are they carrying out? And why does this all seem so familiar?
What's this, then? This writing ... I ... what's happening?
Diyas al-Yat shivers as he turns, and his eyes glow for just an instant with a purplish light.
What ... happened?
This seems to be a rather lengthy text describing the Virindi. I would really like to have met the writer.
The Quiddity has never spoken so plainly before. Their will is certain. The time to act is now.
This really provides some insight into the inner workings of the impure Virindi. It is such a pity to see broken dolls where there was once such purity. Pity.
This piece of writing is quite interesting ... The renegade Virindi have become much more ambitious and more skilled!
Aha! Well, that explains Ecorto over there ...
Aha! Well, this explains Ecorto over there ...
I caution you against further pursuit of this entity.
There is sincerity in the writings here. A warped mind that believes it is still pure.
A look into madness. A frightening exposition of a fall further than any before.
A creation gone awry, how the master yearns to re-collect his child.
As the shroud is pulled aside light begins to filter in the darkness.
Greatest success or greatest failure, this tale seems yet untold.
This should never have passed through my hands! Take it from me now before I feel the profanity creep beneath my flesh.
Devices by which to view the world. Increasingly interesting.
Reclamation by the collective ... Isn't that always their way?
It appears the location you found this was to be invaded by the Quiddity.
These are simple orders that were given by a member of a directive -- nothing that important to see here. You might better spend your time writing your own information in books.
Oh, yes, very nice! Leopold gave me some repaired masks -- I will trade you one of those for this broken mask.
Your continued trafficking with forces beyond your ken could earn you a hearty bit of trouble. I've translated this for you, but would rather see you destroy it, than keep it.
Hello! I am studying those most enigmatic beings, the Virindi. I think I can translate their language. Do not ask me how I acquired such knowledge.
I have also been in touch with Leopold, in Ayan Baqur, and he has given me some repaired Virindi masks to trade for broken ones.
A bettor of true distinction, I see!  Let's see what you got...
You want to trade in the Golden Gromnie?  Unthinkable!  This is the rarest of the rare!  Take it back, and come to your senses!
Monty grumbles under his breath. You make out a few words, "...stupid Ketnan." He smiles and adjusts his vest.
I don't know why I let myself get talked into this by Ketnan, but here goes. Round and round it goes!

Hello, and welcome to my new house! Isn't this nicer than that terrible outdoor location? Boddry there sells a little pamphlet that will tell you our rules and sell you gambling tokens. Look it over, and if you think you have the favor of Dame Fortune, gamble with my Gamesmasters. If you want to gamble a precious little doll, come back to me.

quest: %n spits at your feet.
You abandoned Nuhmudira? Get out of my sight!
You helped Nuhmudira! You are a very noble person.
%n snaps to attention, and salutes you.

You are most welcome within this place. We need your help. There are sclavus beyond this portal that are as strong as a Banderling Captain. If you feel that you can handle fighting these creatures you are welcome to enter.
Everyone should have the opportunity to strike a blow against these defiling creatures.
You may also, if you are lucky, find a gorget inside. Balthazar can explain a little bit more about this item to you. Good luck, friend!
%n looks you over with a wary eye.
I do not know you, stranger. You are not supposed to be here. You should speak to Balthazar, outside.

Good! I'm not glad we had to kill him but I am glad that there are still people willing to help us out. Harker was a good man, it's sad to see him slip into such a state. Thank you for your help and for allowing us to gather the food.

Everything is falling apart. I can't get crops anymore, and without those crops then everyone here will starve, or be forced to move back to the surface. But most don't want that. They'd rather live out their lives here.
If only we could get rid of Harker! The farm has never been truly safe. Rats, wasps, even Olthoi have been known to peek their heads in from time to time.
The worst were the grubs, though. Hundreds of them at times. They're small enough to smash outright, sure... but they're more a threat to the harvest.
If you're going down there, be prepared... One more thing: Harker has a bundle of hooligans who traffic with him now. You watch your back down there, you hear?
Go talk to Hibdin, he's the one organizing the expeditions down there.
Are you at a loss as to where to find Aun Paritea and deliver the Iolite gem?  Go through the Tia-Leh Homestead portal which is in the Hebian-to settlement portals array.
You have assisted us recently. Others should also help in this endeavor. Please return in a few days and I may require your assistance.
You have assisted me recently. Others should also help in this endeavor. Please return in a few days and I may require your assistance.

Greetings. I am a student of Nuhmudira.  Nuhmudira is delving into the lore of Lifestones. She has sent me to enlist the services of Isparians in obtaining some rare compounds and crystals. Several types are important to this research- Iolite gems,  Chrysoberyl compound and Daichroic crystals.

If I could impose on you to deliver this Iolite gem to my colleague Aun Paritea he can tell you where to obtain the Chrysoberyl compound and the Daichroic crystals. To find Aun Paritea, go through the Tia-Leh Homestead portal which is in the Hebian-to settlement portals array.  Aun Paritea is just south of the Tia-Leh Homestead.  When you obtain them, please bring the Daichroic crystals to me a...

Thank you for your assistance in obtaining this Daichroic Crystal for Nuhmudira. Here is your reward. Nuhmudira may require more of these materials in about four days if you wish to undertake this task again.
The book, child. I need the book.
The urn is next, child. Bring me the urn.
Are you a dullard? I told you, the book, the urn and then the corpse. You've brought me the book and the urn. I require the corpse, or you shan't have your precious stone.
I have nothing more to offer you now, child. Your discussion, while engaging, does little to aid me in my study. If there were more for you here I would make you aware. Please, be gone.

In the past, your face has graced my nightmares. I have watched as you drew the life from my body, choosing to throw my efforts to the wind, rather than forgive the misguided way that I traveled. But I see that your heart has not always borne me ill. So I will grant you lenience.

Within this hall are two objects that I require to further my study of these unique people. The first is a book. It will be like many others in appearance. It will be located in the library beyond this hall. Bring that to me first. It will be indecipherable and foreign to your eyes. I will know it at once.

Second, I require a simple urn. It will hold the internal remains of the woman that held sway over the people here. She would have been interred in a very deliberate manner. These organs will have been preserved within this urn. Collect it from the crypt and bring it to me after you have delivered the book and I will grant what Elysa desires of me.
Elysa's clemency... is... appreciated.
Nuhmudira smiles wryly and ushers you toward your tasks.

Child, you come to me and ask a favor for the woman who has banished me from my home? Very well. She wishes to change these words, she wishes to make amends for her terrible slight, but she cannot come herself? What have I done for our people? Are my deeds so dark? Granting housing, providing the guidance and hope for our future... are these so minor that I should be cast aside like a useless r...
Nuhmudira shakes her head.

It matters little. You are here at the behest of Elysa, but you have proven to me before that you have the interest of all Isparians within your heart. I need one small task undertaken before I grant you with what you need.

Within the library of this place is a book. These people were efficient, not opulent. Far less depraved than the Yalain, yet their predilection toward creating magical devices was still tantamount. I have yet to determine the period in which these people held sway on this world, but their language is opening to me very quickly. Bring me the book that I desire. It should be on a table, though if...
Be warned, the Moarsmen guard this place with their lives. The have dug tunnels beneath this chapel and enter freely. Retrieve this book and I shall see you rewarded.
You are doing well, child. There are still two object to be found. The second is the urn I mentioned before. Quickly now. My time is precious.
You are doing well, child. There is still the matter of the urn, then you shall have the precious gift that Elysa so desires.

Yes... I do need this child. But I was specific in my instructions, was I not? The book first. There are precautions that must be taken in an endeavor such as this. Please, collect the book for me. Then hand me the urn.
Another service out of the way and only one before you. The more time you waste with me, the more time your precious Queen needs to wait to have her desire sated. Quickly now, retrieve the corpse.

Perhaps I was not as clear as I should have been. You are to collect me three objects, in order: a book, an urn and then the corpse. This is of no use to me until I have the other two objects in my possession.
Return to me when you have deciphered my words and are prepared to accept the responsibility placed upon your shoulders.
You are helping me to decipher a question for which I have long searched for an answer. It may be the case that not all members of our race are worth saving.
Take this back.

I asked for the book, the urn and then the corpse. Write it down. This will help you to remember what I need and the order in which I need to receive them. Return to me when these instructions have made an impression.
Perhaps there is hope for you yet. You have brought each object to me that I have desired, with little protest. I am a woman of my word.

Find a fair amount of Burun blood and douse the stone. The stone will drink the blood and become a vile poison to the Burun. In essence, it will become a burun slaying device. Affix the resultant stone to a -Noble- weapon and you shall have what Elysa desired.
Now, begone.

As you turn to leave, you remember that Antius had wanted you to ask a question of Nuhmudira. You turn on your heels and call back. "Nuhmudira, did you let Oswald into the castle the night of the assassination attempt on Elysa?"
Oswald was given --
Nuhmudira gives you a stern look, "It would be wise of you to leave my presence now, %s."
What have we here? An errand runner from the High Queen. Sent by that whimpering waste of a man, Antius. I know your face. I know your scorn. After all that I have done for our Race, for our people.
Nuhmudira shakes her head. "You abandon me to death at the hands of that -- Empyrean! My memory is long, %s." She pauses.
Yet you come to me now and ask for help.
Very well, you will receive my assistance, but there is a cost.
Within the halls beyond are three objects that I require. I am not wont to leave my study of this place and have no students here at present to undertake this endeavor. You shall do.

I require a book from the library of this structure. It will appear as grand as the book that Asheron created. These people, while talented, were as degenerate and lavish as Asheron's ilk. To think, they would waste their arts on creating such garish items.
Collect the book and return it to me first.

When that is complete I will need you to collect a small trifle of an object. These people believed in interring their dead in a unique fashion. There is an urn within a crypt here. That urn contains organs that these people thought precious above all else. They belonged to the woman who sat as the head of this chapel and this order. Fetch that urn and return it to me. This will leave only the...

Lastly, this woman was once possessed of great power. She had the ability to sway masses, lead and inspire by her presence alone. Now she lies in a sarcophagus. Dead, bones rotting away while time presses them and their secrets into dust. I require her corpse. Bring this to me last, and I shall see that you receive what Elysa wants.
You... are not familiar to me in any way.
Nuhmudira looks you over. A simple flick of her fingers and you feel a wave of magic wash over your form.

Intriguing... Nonetheless, you come bearing news from Elysa. The very woman who wished me to never to return to -her- kingdom. A kingdom granted by an adoring populace that had known terror for years! A kingdom handed to her by a being unwilling, nay, unable to undertake the task himself because of paralyzing fear. You... are young. Misguided perhaps.

I am Nuhmudira, child. I am the creator of the sanctity that we Isparians are afforded on this world. For that, I am cast out because of baseless accusation and fear. It is a yoke akin to one I have borne since childhood. It is a curse that those with power must learn to bear.
I am not without generosity and compassion. Since Elysa has seen fit to forgive her accusations, I shall see fit to oblige her what she asks. But there is a small price.

Second, I require a simple urn. It will hold the internal remains of the woman that held sway over the people here. She would have been interred in a very deliberate manner. These organs will have been preserved within this urn. Collect it and bring it to me after you have delivered the book and I will grant what Elysa desires of me.

Most impressive, dear child. You have pleased me greatly. Take this, it is a small token. You will need to craft it yourself. It is a pittance to make. You will need a fair amount of Burun blood to complete the process with the gem.

When you have found a large enough sample of burun blood apply it to the stone. The stone will drink the blood and take on the properties that will most harm the Burun. Affix the stone to your weapon or wand, and the magic will flow into the item. We will survive this latest threat, child. Fear not.
Because of your service to me in the past I want to give you a little more. Please, open your mind to me.

You've done all I have asked and done so without managing a scowl. You have proved that my faith in you was well founded. Leaves sometimes do turn over and show a brighter side, don't you think that is true. Do not answer. For your services, I gift you with this stone.

You will need to obtain a fair amount of Burun blood to enhance this stone. Apply the blood and it will drink the qualities in and become the antithesis. After that is complete apply the stone to one of the -Noble- weapons. It will assume the qualities and become a slayer of Burun.

I think that I shall prove that I mean well to us all, child. I know what has been occurring, the teachings of my former student, Ciandra. I have been watching from afar and here is a gift that I think will aid you. Open your mind to me.
Interesting, how did you come by this? it is a very nice gift. Thank you.

greetings: So, you were able to get the Spinning Wheel to make this? Wonderful! And very strong thread too. Are you going to see what the Loom at Neydisa Castle might do with it? This is wonderful, now that grievvers can provide us with Silk, perhaps people will take my work more seriously.
Such fine craftsmanship. You say the Loom at Neydisa Castle made this? Fascinating what machines can do.
If I weren't so interested in Grievvers and Olthoi I might consider studying these magical devices, perhaps in time I will grow tired of them...
Oh, look here, you have something on your flag. I'll just wash that out for you.
All clean, here you go.
Verdentine holds the Olthoi Head up reverently peering through the eyeholes.
The Olthoi is a marvel of nature. I would love to see the world they can from, their natural environment must be very harsh and demanding to require so much armor.

Have you thought of making a helmet out of this? I have a friend who crafts items from Olthoi trophies. She lives in Newic, I'm sure she would be happy to make this into a helm for you. She's known as the Olthoi Hunter.
The researcher hefts the claw in his hands.

Extremely lightweight, yet amazingly strong and look at the sharp edge here. They can pierce armor with these things as easily as you do with a sword. Speaking of which, you can have this crafted into a sword by my friend who still lives in Newic. Her name is... come to think of it, I don't know her name. Huh! Everyone just calls her the Olthoi Hunter.
Verdentine eyes grow extremely wide as he surveys the Olthoi Carapace you hand him.
Did you take this from a Queen?
For a brief moment Verdentine looks extremely dangerous, then the anger drains from his features leaving a look of sad resignation.
I wasn't sure if the rumors were true... Now I'll never be able to see her alive, I can only hope that she wasn't the last.
You must be quite a skilled hunter to have recovered this whole. I just can't get over the size of this Carapace... Thank you for showing it to me.

I've heard of these. Apparently they are quite valuable on Marae Lassel. I really need to take a trip to that island to study it's Olthoi. I've even heard rumors of a new Olthoi Queen. There just isn't enough time is there? Oh well, my work here is fascinating too.
Verdentine hands the pincer back to you.
Very interesting, thank you.

I've heard of these. Apparently they are quite valuable on Marae Lassel. I really must to take a trip to that island to study it's Olthoi. I've even heard rumors of a new Olthoi Queen. There just isn't enough time is there? Oh well, my work here is fascinating too.
I don't know how to feel about this. You have managed to kill this unique and marvelous Lady.

I am joyed to be able to examine this specimen, but I also feel anger and sorrow at the possibility that you may have doomed the Olthoi species of this land. Do we have more of a right to this world than they? Who is to say? I know the Olthoi enslaved us. I know they kill us. I just don't think that exterminating them is the only answer.
I am sorry I did not mean to place a burden on your shoulders. You have done a mighty deed for sure.
%n holds the mounted head at arms length. His face contorts in sorrow for a brief moment.
I am... joyed to be able to examine this specimen. I'm sure tales of your deed will be told for years to come. A fine mounting job, Tumerok craftsmanship if I'm not mistaken.

Ah yes, an original Olthoi Helm. My friend the Olthoi Hunter no doubt made this for you quite a long time ago. It truly is a classic design. May it serve you well, at least better than it served its original owner.
Haha, it's not often I have company to laugh with.

A newer version of my friend's famous helm. Look at that craftsmanship! He uses the Olthoi head's natural strengths and adds to them where the shell is weakest. A beautiful helm. You are very lucky to own one.

Here we have one of the most beautiful examples of natural armor. The Olthoi Carapace is perfectly suited to resisting heavy blows and attacks as well as sharp piercing strikes. This cuirass is lighter than most and stronger too, a fine piece of work. Thank you for allowing me to study it, may it protect you always.
%n hefts the weapon in his hand and examines the blades black luster.
A blade lighter than steel and sharper than most non-magical weapons.
Odd that you can fight Olthoi with their own appendages. You would think it would cause them some confusion as well... Perhaps it just makes them angry. A fine sword!
You experience a slight queasy feeling watching Verdentine eat the cake.
Mmmmm chocolate, and you can taste the Olthoi!
Verdentine pokes a hole in the egg with his finger. He eyes the contents for a second and then tips the egg to his mouth and drinks it down.
A wave of nausea washes over you.
Delicious! And it will keep me going while I'm out here in the field. Thank you.
How Clever! It's really a very good likeness of an Olthoi. What will they think of next?
Oh, right, you want your doll back. Here, take it.
Oh! It's not real! Haha, very funny. Of course you wouldn't think it so funny if you had been bitten by one of the little nippers.
Oh, this isn't mine to keep? Well, have it back I guess.

I see you've harvested some of the rare Grievver Acid. Very powerful stuff! I sometimes use it to clean my armor up. By the way, don't open this anywhere around here. If the Grievvers pick up on it they could cause you no end of trouble.

Haha, just kidding! I know what this stuff is and I very seriously doubt I would like the taste of it. However be forewarned, I wouldn't open this here if I were you. The Grievvers have a fierce dislike of the Olthoi and I'm afraid that the smell of this stuff, if in fact Grievvers can smell, would bring them running in droves.
No, I can't have a campfire. It might attract the Grievvers.
Small price to pay really.
I recently tried to get recognition at the Arcanum for my work on Grievvers. Do you know what they told me?

They said chasing bugs is "just an eccentric hobby" not worthy of funding. Well, I don't need the Queen's backing. I'm sure that my work will bear fruit and prove it's worth to those skeptics someday.
I have a theory on how Grievvers perceive the world. They have no evident visual organs, yet they seem to move about quite easily.

From what I have learned and deduced I believe Grievvers come from the same world as the Olthoi, but unlike the Olthoi they were bent to the will of the Shadows. This undoubtedly changed them in ways I cannot say. Perhaps they used to have eyes, perhaps not, I think they may use magics now to attain a view of the world. If so, they can probably see things that we cannot. Or it may be that they...
At some point I may try and get a specimen to dissect and learn more, but my work here is currently more important.
%n gazes dreamily into the distance.

Imagine having the abilities of a Grievver! You could climb almost any surface. Your strength would be magnified many times that of a normal human. You could spin webs, although that seems rather useless unless you want to catch your lunch... You reactions would be enhanced and you might have senses beyond those we are aware of.
I know that sounds silly, but I often daydream about such things.
Did you see that? A little Grievver! I wonder if it's a different species or just a juvenile.
I fear that they may detect my camp here on the hill and figure out a way up. I'm not much of a fighter I'm afraid.

This I know for a fact. The Grievvers cannot abide the presence of Olthoi. They will fight fiercely against them whenever the two come in contact. This leads me to believe that the Grievvers and Olthoi share some common origin.

Grievvers eat whatever they can catch. I often see them dragging rabbits, aurochs and other creatures wrapped in webbing across the valley floor. Yesterday I saw them drag an injured Olthoi to the east of the valley where I expect they have a nest of sorts. Unfortunately, many young warriors and mages new to the world also fall prey to the Grievvers out of inexperience.

What? A minor setback? Ah yes, the lifestones. You wouldn't think that was any worse than the hundreds of other ways we can die and be reborn anew into this world, but Grievvers prefer to eat their food alive I'm afraid. They try to injure their prey and cocoon it for consumption at their convenience. I... I sometimes hear horrible sounds from down there. Be careful here, I beg you.

I believe that the Grievvers have a complex social order. I can often see one deferring to another in combat or during feeding. Yet it doesn't appear to be a purely physical hierarchy since I've seen a smaller Grievver receive deferential treatment. Perhaps they also recognize intelligence or magical ability as dominating traits. It's all very interesting!

I am very interested in insect trophies and body parts. You can learn much about a creature from its remains. If you have any I would greatly enjoy looking them over. Don't worry I'll return them after I've examined them. I do however have a powerful appetite and cannot make the same assurances about food. Haha!

I'm afraid I find the recent Grievver activity in this valley somewhat unsettling. They seem to guard the area against all other creatures. I've never seen Grievvers build a nest, but I think that's just what they are doing. Perhaps the lack of Shadow influence for so long is allowing them to return to a more natural existence. If you think yourself brave enough I would be very grateful to know...
quest: Verdentine takes the Silk and fluffs it in his hands.
That's some very nice Silk! Got it from a Grievver you say? Well you shouldn't try and get anymore for at least two weeks. We have to think about conservation don't we?

Here you go. Very interesting substance, it's a much finer quality than the webbing I've seen all over the valley. You know, I've heard of two machines able to spin fine materials like this into cloth. I seem to remember they were both found in Castles somewhere... let me check my notes.
Yes, here it is!

It says here that there was a Spinning Wheel found in a Castle to the Northeast of Shoushi overrun by skeletons... and here it says that a Loom was recently found in a food cellar at Neydisa Castle. The residents dragged it up to a tower room, but were unable to get it to produce any useable cloth.
I think our insect friends have provided you with the materials required. You might try seeing if you can get the devices to work.

Good luck in your travels my friend! I am going to continue my studies of these fascinating creatures here. Please, only kill them out of necessity so as not to disturb the fragile ecological balance in this area.
Verdentine studies the Silk for a moment.

Yes, a high quality Silk! Looks like you could go and get some more now if you like, but after that I must insist that you not try and harvest more Silk from the Grievvers for at least two weeks. I'm concerned about the colonies well being as I'm sure are you.
Here's your Silk back. Do you know of the two machines able to spin fine materials like this into cloth?
I've read of a Spinning Wheel found in a Castle to the Northeast of Shoushi overrun by skeletons and there was a Loom found in a food cellar at Neydisa Castle.
You might try seeing if you can fashion this Silk into something of use.
Farewell my friend, I am only just beginning to uncover the secrets of how the Grievvers social structure works and I must get back to my observations so as not to miss anything.
chatter: %n writes something into a book of notes, mutters a bit and continues writing.
What are they up to?
Fascinating!

Did you see that!? One of the Grievvers just motioned as if to warn another one! Perhaps this is a basic form of non-verbal communication or maybe a hierarchical order, I must record this and study it further.
Remarkable creatures!

quest: I have already provided you with a pennant.  Display it proudly!

The High Queen has commissioned me to create a pennant for all Isparians currently upon Dereth.  Asheron himself has provided the device - the heraldry of his family.  I am told that this is in honor of our continued bravery and heroics. He and the High Queen have decided that he no longer needs to watch over us, and now Asheron may return to his home.
Take this pennant and display it proudly! But be warned that I am only commissioned to provide you with this once.

I am sorry, friend. I have only the materials to provide pennants to those who were already on Dereth when Asheron returned home. I am sure that you will find other ways to show your courage and honor.

greetings: Very good; I see you can do this task for me.  I suspect my book was stolen by drudges, who have lately taken up residence in the dungeon I filled with lights, the Kindled Path.
Ungrateful creatures.  The dungeon is to the east of here.  Look for the candles that mark the entrance.
Ah, well done.  The drudges seem to like the smell of the book's binding, I guess.

Anyway, here is a reward for you.  From here, you may wish to see what else may be done in Nanto.  By the way, if you've found any broken tapers, I think the Archmage's Apprentice would like them more than I do.
This probably was made of inferior wax, but I will pay you for it.  Next time, take these to the Archmage's Apprentice.
I am a keeper of lights, seeking to illuminate the paths of the lost, as the good Elders would have me do.
I once filled an entire dungeon with glorious candles to help wanderers.  Recently, some creature or other stole my reference book on magical lights.
I suspect my book was stolen by drudges, who have lately taken up residence in the dungeon I filled with lights, the Kindled Path.

quest: While I appreciate your enthusiasm, we've been experiencing less trouble. Try back in a few weeks--maybe things will have changed by then.
Of course, if you've brought me proof of your efforts in the deep, hand it to me so I may reward you.
Hello friend. We've fallen on some hard times here in Martine's Retreat. With Martine being gone for so long, we can only surmise that he is indeed dead. But that is the least of our problems.
About two weeks ago Remmick, our head farmer, came up from the subterranean farm and said that it was madness down there. It seems that a farm hand named Harker had become... touched.
If you wouldn't mind helping us out with getting some of the food and maybe killing Harker, we'd be in your debt. I'd pay you handsomely.
Before you go, you might want to speak to Remmick. He might have some pointers for you.
If you show these to Leandra she might be able to explain the special properties of these gauntlets.
While these aren't as potent as the other gauntlets, they have the distinction of three cantrips.
This should not be possible.
chatter: If you have a moment to spare, please come talk to me.

Well, it looks like you've done pretty well down there. I've got a reward for your efforts--it's only fair that we give you something. You have, after all, returned the productivity to the farm for the time being.

greetings: Indeed, this is the runic script of old Dericost, a language not used in well over 5000 years.  A moment - I shall transcribe a copy for you into Roulean.
There you are.  This was gained from a powerful Revenant you say?  He would appear to have been several millenia old!  I wonder if there are others of his antiquity still walking Dereth?
Hm. This appears to be a portalspace coordinate. Such things are not within my knowledge. You might want to seek out my colleague Marisa bint Fuya.
She would be able to cast a portal to this location. Unfortunately, she's on sabbatical, and has gone to the town of Plateau.
Be warned, though - you will need a substantial party to reach the Lost City, and should you die...
You will be unable to reenter the caves to recover your equipment. Be certain you are prepared before you ask Mairisa to cast the portal!

Ah, but this is not the language of Dericost.  Do you see the sharp, triangular shapes the characters are composed of? This is almost certainly the written word of the Falatacot, a far older, and far less understood culture.
Fanzen San, in Hebian-To, would be able to translate this for you.
I can indeed translate this for you into Roulean.
This is... fascinating. This work seems to explain what the Gelidites were doing in their long exile.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the script of ancient Empyrea.  You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
My apologies, but I cannot read this.  It appears to be the language of the ancient Falatacot.  You should bring this to Fanzen San, in Hebian-To.
Oh dear...
This doesn't bode well. No, not at all. Take a look for yourself.

I fear I cannot help you with this. You see that this writing style is like our own? It appears to be the script used by the High Empyrean culture of the Age of Lore. My specialty is the runic language of Dericost. You should bring this to Bretself the translator, in Cragstone.
This note seems to be written on cured skin... Not human skin, but something similar.  The contents of the note are quite disturbing, and written in an archaic dialect of ancient Dericostian.
Aerfalle... I have seen this name before. An adventurer brought me a note from Rytheran, the Revenant of the Mage Academy near Mount Esper. It was addressed to an Aerfalle. But this... a moment...
Heavens and earth! This speaks of the last Shadow War, and in grave detail. I am... profoundly disturbed by the sights this Aerfalle has witnessed.
Ew! What IS that?
Take it to Bretslef in Cragstone. I don't want to touch it!
%n grabs a flask of water and hurriedly scrubs her hands.
Ah yes, this is interesting. This came from a Mu-Miyah, you say. Curious. This would seem to be some sort of memoir.
I wonder what would provoke such soul searching? Although I have noted that the undead seem prone to rambling reminiscence... I suppose when one is that old, it becomes inevitable.
This is most intriguing! It would seem we have have allies in our war against the forces of Bael'Zharon. Of a sort, anyway.
This is useful. There is an army of undead gathering somewhere in the wilderness. Odd that they have not been seen yet.
It would seem they do not all get along. Old grudges, I suppose.
Heavens and earth, do you know what this is? This is nothing less than the undeads' own analysis of the Shadows' activity.
I have little doubt that this information will be invaluable in the near future. You may have given us a crucial edge.
Your pardon, but I must leave soon to confer with my colleagues and the Consortium of Archmages...
Hm, interesting. Looks like you caught this monster in the middle of writing a report to its superior.
Well. This undead certainly thinks the world owes her. I can't imagine how obnoxious she'd be in person. If there's anything worse than a smelly abomination, it's a smarmy smelly abomination.
Magnificent! The dates in this journal stretch back to the last Shadow War. What an invaluable asset to our studies! It will take some time to go over this thoroughly. Here are the last few entries.
Ah, yes, this appears to be a unique teleport spell. Give me a moment, and I can teach it to you.
Hrm. Well, the letters of this are in the High Empyrean language of the Age of Lore. However, they don't seem to form any words.
I do not recognize this language at all... Try talking to Diyas al-Yat, here in Zaikhal.  He's an odd man who spends his time studying the Virindi.
What is this?  Perhaps Diyas could make some sense of it...
I am sorry, but I cannot read this.  Try talking to the Hebian-To translator, Fanzen San.
An interesting read, a bit fanatical in spot. I have made notes where they are applicable.
Will wonders never cease? This book was difficult because of the damage wrought upon it. As well the text itself was written in a variation of Dericost, akin to that of the Gelid.
This is a personal missive, written very recently. I'd be interested to see if there were more like it.
A second note written in the same hand, and like the first a missive written recently. What are they working on?
The World Shaper. I wonder what that title means? Keep bringing these to me as you find them, please.
Well it appears that these letters are beginning to take on a more active ken. I'd be interested in seeing if there were anymore.
This must be the last of them. It has an air of finality to it. I wonder what sacrifice the writer is speaking about.
I am a scholar of a certain era of Empyrean history, the time of the Millennium War.  If your text is of Dericost, Haebrous, or early Yalain, I may be able to translate it.
Servitude... Wretched...
Never... in all my campaigns...

quest: I have met the man you seek, this Honshu Takeda. He is a good man. He will find his way back to the path of right living. I have sent him to seek grace at the shrine in Sawato. Perhaps if you pray, as he likely did, at the shrine you will see grace as well.
The grace of the unicorn is not the same as the balance of the crane. It is an ephemera that suffuses the soul and fills one with peace.
Your steps are just beginning, fear not the road that they will follow. Tranquility is as the river who calls to the sea.
A reed that does not bend, shatters and is swept away in the current.
As philosophies divide, so do the adherents of the paths. Not all are able to follow the path of the human.
Through the four stones we are shown the way to heaven and perfect life.
Grace allows us to walk through life in perfection.

greetings: An intriguing find. I regret that I am not a man of letters, so I cannot read this. It looks like Empyrean script. You may wish to present this to Bretslef, in the Aluvian capital of Cragstone. It's quite a trip there, though.
What an odd weapon. I have little doubt that the mite found it in the old Empyrean armory. It is well known that they have no handicrafts of their own. It's yours to keep - I have no use for it.

How peculiar. This geode almost looks like an egg, does it not? Can you see the little Knath'taed inside? I don't imagine that such a thing could be useful. Perhaps Aino, the Sho enchantress outside of town, could be of more help with this.
My thanks. The bounty on these small rats is 100 pyreal - the larger ones are worth more.
My thanks. The bounty on these small rats is 200 pyreal - the larger ones are worth more.
My thanks. The bounty on these small rats is 300 pyreal - the larger ones are worth more.
Ugh! How revolting to think such creatures scurry below our beds every night! I am authorized to pay 500 pyreals from the town coffers for such a prize.
Well done, I am authorized to pay 900 pyreals from the town coffers for such a prize.
This trophy proves a fine catch indeed, my friend. Here is your bounty. May the blessings of the poet - and the thanks of Xarabydun - go with you.
Amazing! I would never have guessed that such a large vermin lived beneath my feet. Take this Mana Charge, my friend, and I pray the experience of fighting this beast makes you prosper.
I've never agreed with the taking of scalps, but this certainly proves that you've been clearing the Banderlings that infest the lower levels.
Have you come to help us cleanse the lower levels of vermin? As the Bey of Xarabydun, I will reward you greatly for trophies that prove the death of the beasts that prevent our growth.
chatter: Ah, if only we could clear the lower levels of their pestilence. Then, truly, could Xarabydun become a great city.

greetings: What a pretty piece of shell! But I can't do anything with it.  Sorry.
What a pretty, and large, piece of shell!  I'm afraid I haven't the faintest idea what to do with it, though.
This is a beautiful pearl!  You should match your wardrobe around it!
How disgusting!
There is, however, a sage somewhere in the southern mountain range that actually likes those things.  How revolting...
This is a nice shiny bauble!  I can't do anything with it though.  Maybe one of the outlaws in Bandit Castle can help you.
Here you go. People have been telling me about a strange new plant that's been found in some dungeons and around the landscape. Quite a colorful thing, or so they say.
Here's your armor! I overheard someone talking about the new plants again. They sound so lovely! I'll bet someone with the proper skills could crush them up and make a fine dye.
Enjoy the armor! May it keep the burn off your back. Oh my! The plants are just all I can think about... It's a pity that I can't use them in my craft due to all the harsh chemicals I use.
I never thought I could make such a sturdy hide into a fine shirt like this! I hope it's not to scratchy on your skin!
Here you go!
I find greaves so aesthetically pleasing. Even if they do come from those brutish reedsharks. Perchance have you tried dyeing your other pieces of armor?
A friend gave me a dyeing pot, but I don't seem to be able to dye any of the leather armor I craft from creature hides.
Reedsharks have such rough, ugly skin. Crafting from their skin always punishes my delicate hands!
By the way, have you tried dyeing armor yet? Try as I might, I just can't seem to get the knack of it!
Ah, another masterpiece! Such a drab, gray color though. It's quite a shame that I have to apply so many chemicals to treat the leather, otherwise they could be infused with such color!
It pains my heart to make such dowdy-colored armor. A pity this cannot be dyed.
Have you tried dyeing any other armor yet? Be careful... if you do a poor job you might damage your armor, and that would certainly be dreadful!
Wow, this thing reminds me of those strange Hoary Mattekar hides.  Only, not as hoary, or protective, for that matter.  But there is more material here to work with...
This is rather exotic!  It is sort of a claw shield.
A Mattekar claw?  I don't think I can make clothing out of this one.  Well, here, have this.

Yes, the Hoary Mattekars are now back.  Given the strangeness of creature migrations that have occurred over this past year, I would not be surprised were the Hoary to be a more permanent fixture on Dereth.  Here is your robe.
Oh my! Will you just look at this drab old thing! I'll spruce it up for you and make you the star you were meant to be!
What's this? Warmer than the Hoary that is for sure. Hmm... This seems to be a mattekar who has adapted to a warmer climate. Interesting.
The hide is a little tougher, though not meant for the cold. Against heat however, this should do quite nicely.
The little shreths are kind of cute, aren't they?  It is a pity that people have found a way to use their skin.  Now they will be hunted like most of the other poor creatures of Dereth.
Some of the larger shreths are just coming into their own.  They are aggressive not out of hostility, but out of fear.  Killing them is not the answer!
In killing the shreth of today, we may be dooming our tomorrow.  Perhaps the shreths hold an answer to an unforeseen plague, or some equally monumental task.  I urge you to reconsider hunting them!
This probably came from a baby ursuin somewhere...  Loincloths are so last year.
Ursuin make wonderful garments!  Their coats make lovely coats that are functional too!  Of course I can make a mattekar coat look even better than an ursuin one...
This is a pretty small shank of hide.  But never fear, Yi Yo Jin has never failed at making something both fashionable, and affordable!
Wow!  Ursuin hides are so soft in the spring and summer season!  Maybe I'll take the extra strips from your coat and line my breeches with them...
This tooth would make a fine implement of destruction.  Take it , and strike down my enemies!
Ursuins certainly have large heads.  Personally, I like their coats better than these helms.
This has just the splash of color that you'll need to really shine like a star!
Remember, snakeskin is like make-up.  Too much and it makes you look like a tawdry matron!
This helmet is nice because it goes with anything that you wear.  Sclavus are so useful when they die.
This is large enough to craft into a well fitting cuirass I think.
Well then. I think that this may be the first of a great many new robes to come my friend. Make sure to show your friends.
Not quite as sturdy as the tanned red hide that I worked with before, but it's still strong enough and large enough to craft into a nice robe. Wear it well.
Let's see. The hide is thick and leathery, and aside from the small bony protrusions it's in fine shape. I think a nice set of leggings.
There you go.
Another fine specimen. A little thicker than the last shreth hide I was given to work with. Let me have a moment and I'll... Yes, yes that's it!
Here you go.
Where did you get this? It's rather frightening, and rancid smelling. Well, let me see what I can do with it.
I've seen something like this recently. Came from a carenzi though, it mottled and smelled rank. Much like this. Where are you finding these creatures?
Well, I've done the best I can.
What is this!? I've never seen anything like this. It will make a fine robe I think. Give me a moment.
Yes, there it is done.
I've seen some interesting hides pass my way, but the hides that people have been bringing me most recently are the oddest.
A few more threads...and done!
Be careful out there.
Will miracles never cease?  The Hoary Mattekar has returned!  A beautiful and ferocious creature.  And most people looking at it see nothing but a robe.  Such a shame.  Give me the hide.
chatter: I can take the hides of certain creatures and turn them into items of value.
Have you the skins of armoredillos, gromnies, or reedsharks?  I can use them in my craft.
The wind blows hollowly through the deserted bottom of the hive...

greetings: What a kind gesture of Ahyara's! Thank you for bringing this to me! But didn't she ask you to take this to Nasun first?
Oh, how sweet of Nasun! Thank you for bringing this to me! But didn't he as you to take this to Ahyara first?
How kind of Ahyara to think of me! Could you carry this thank-you note back to her for me?
Oh, what a sweet man Nasun is! I wish I could understand but half of his words, but I know he means well.
Please, would you take him this thank-you note?
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Hey, looks like it got rolled in the mud... Anyway, well done!  Here, take these as a reward.
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Looks like good old F.P. went swimming or something.  Here's your reward.
Looks like you've lucked out!  Our man F.P. has finished his book, finally!  Here you go...
Greetings! Welcome to Yaraq! I am the local representative of the Explorer Society. My job is to help new arrivals in Dereth get settled in and learn their way around.
If you have just arrived in Dereth, my father Lubziklan could really use your help. And if you can help him, he can help you get a good start on your new life here in Dereth.
Seek him out at our house just to the south of town, near the beach. If you need help finding it, you can buy directions from Jubal, the barkeeper.
quest: Yes, I baked that for you. Enjoy!
My father Lubziklan is looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
You found something of Abmim's! Quick, take this to Ma'yad! She must be worried sick!
I believe that Akyafi the Translator was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
Ahha! Thank you for bringing this to me!

I have been contracted by the Dereth Exploration Society to help them in their outreach program towards the Isparians who find themselves newly exiled in Dereth.  Here is a book that explains their mission.
I will also give you a list describing the locations of the nearest stamp and portals to other towns.  If you collect any of the Society's stamped letters, you may bring them back to me for a reward.
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here.  You are a true Explorer!

You will get nothing from me for this. Go explore and find more towns.  The Society Agents in the Sho towns will exchange a piece of jewelry or a wand for this. If you take this to one of the Aluvian towns, you will receive a piece of armor.

greetings: Greetings! I have left my master in Glenden Wood to help the craftsmen of this fine land to hone their crafting skills
Prove your knowledge by bringing me some Fried Anchovy Dough, and I shall reward you.
What, you say you don't know how to make Fried Anchovy Dough?! Why, that is what tests of knowledge are for! Get out there and experiment, my young friend!
Prove your knowledge by bringing me some Fried Cinnamon Dough, and I shall reward you.
What, you say you don't know how to make Fried Cinnamon Dough?! Why, that is what tests of knowledge are for! Get out there and experiment, my young friend!
Prove your knowledge by bringing me some Fried Mushroom Dough, and I shall reward you.
What, you say you don't know how to make Fried Mushroom Dough?! Why, that is what tests of knowledge are for! Get out there and experiment, my young friend!
quest: Practice certainly makes perfect. Perhaps you could bring this back to me in a week? I am saving up for a trip back to Glenden Wood at the moment.
You are on your way to becoming a true master!!
I am currently saving for a trip to visit my master back in Glenden Wood, so I can only help you out once per week.

greetings: Bachus Flufens examines the spear intensely.

Ah, so there was something to their story after all...what an interesting find! But look here...don't these slots along this side suggest that it is missing a part? I wonder if it lies over in the caves directly to the northeast? For the past season I've been able to watch many Tumerok comings and goings here from my front porch. If you were to bring me back the object in its entirety, I'm sure...
Bachus squints carefully at the figurine.

I have never seen an artifact such as this before...some sort of Tumerok figurine? Ah...but it seems as if it is not in its entirety? Perhaps it should be married to another piece? If you bring me back the completed artifact, I will surely reward you!
Bachus gingerly lifts the weapon from your grasp and weighs it in her hands.
A Tumerok War Taiaha! One of the first examples of Tumerok war craft I have ever seen. I must send this on to Aliester--he will be delighted to further his research on Tumerok culture. I thank you!

An interesting find, this. I am not sure what to make of it. But it does not look as if it could fit to the spear I am speaking of. I am isolated here on my little farm--perhaps there is someone else on the island who could help you discover the secrets of its origin.
quest: Bachus tells you, "So you're back, %s. Good to see you. I am always happy when friends stop by, especially around sunset--the view is spectacular from here! I haven't noticed anything out of the ordinary of late, but can never tell what will happen on the island! Perhaps things will have changed even by next week."

Woe is me! The Hea must have overheard that I have been sending travelers to investigate their caverns, for they invaded my house, burned down my apple trees, and ate my bunny rabbits!  I barely escaped here to safety of Redspire in one piece! Fortunately my dear friend Micon has agreed to give me shelter until I am back upon my feet.

They must hold that relic in high esteem indeed. A most fanciful folk, I must say! I heard that it is a legendary spear that they dismantled and enshrined in two separate caverns on the island. It once belonged to a warrior from an opposite faction, I believe. He tried to persuade them back to traditional ways, but they would have none of it. Somehow they dispatched him but retained his spear.....

Perhaps the answer could be found in the caverns to the northwest along the shore.  Try the area around 40.2N 84.7W --at least that's where I saw the Tumeroks heading last. Beware, friend--it's quite likely to be well guarded. I'd go myself, but I must catch up on my journal today. If you would like to read it, here are a few pages that I wrote the other day.
The book. I need the book.
The urn is next. Bring me the urn.
I told you, the book, the urn and then the corpse. You've brought me the book and the urn. I require the corpse.
I have nothing more to offer you now. Your discussion, while engaging, does little to aid me in my study. If there were more for you here I would make you aware. Please, be gone.

Nuhmudira has decided that even those who would see her harmed are worthy of redemption as you have proven by your actions in the past. She requires that you obtain two objects for her before I can grant you the stone that you desire.
The first is a book found in the library and the second is an urn from the crypt. Collect these are return them to me in the order I have listed and you shall be rewarded.
Lady Nuhmudira has given me leave to reward those who have shown her the greatest amount of compassion should they complete one small task for her.
There is a book that can be found in the library of this structure. Return this to me and you will receive your just reward.
It is good to see that you following instructions well. Now... collect the urn and then return it to me.
You have done well thus far. Now bring the urn and I shall see this off to Nuhmudira and give you your reward.
Yes, I will need this object. But I asked for the book first. I must ensure that all items are properly logged for Nuhmudira. Please take this back and give me the book first.
There is only one service that lay before you now. Collect the corpse of the woman that served in these halls and all will be complete.
While it is impressive that you have the foresight necessary to plan ahead. I still must follow a rigid set of instructions. I need the book, followed by the urn and then the corpse.
Please, hand them to me in that order. I would not want to displease Lady Nuhmudira.
This is impressive. Truly it is. But it is also not what I need at this time. I require the urn before you hand me this corpse. Take this back.
Hand me the urn so I can properly catalogue your progression.
Your efforts will not go unrecognized. I shall see that Lady Nuhmudira receives a full report on your progress. For now, take your precious reward.

You must now find a sample of Burun blood. Soak the stone in the blood and it will take on properties that are the antithesis of the Burun. Apply that stone to the -Noble- weapons and it will become a Burun slaying weapon.
That is all.

As you turn to leave, you remember that you'd been advised you to ask a question of Nuhmudira's Student. You turn on your heels and call back. "Has Nuhmudira ever spoken about the night that Oswald attempted to assassinate Elysa?"
Nuhmudira and Oswald have had a good --
Camryn looks a bit flustered, "I think you should leave now, %s."

On an errand from the High Queen? Nuhmudira has decided that she will assist those who will continue to show her aid. The lady has been pulled away by business elsewhere. I am her student, Camryn. I will fulfill the role that she once filled in this place.
Within the halls beyond are three objects that I require. I am not wont to leave my study of this place and have no students here at present to undertake this endeavor. You shall do.
Within the halls beyond are three objects.  Nuhmudira requires them in order. I will catalogue their arrival and ensure that you are properly credited with finding the objects for her.

The first is a book found in the library, the second is an urn from the crypt and the last is the corpse of the woman who held court in this chapel. Collect these and return them to me in the order I have listed and you shall be rewarded.
Though Nuhmudira is unaware of your exploits she is not without mercy. If you desire the stone that much she will grant you the device, if you undertake a set of small tasks for her.
The first is a book found in the library, the second is an urn from the crypt. Collect these are return them to me in the order I have listed and you shall be rewarded.
You have succeeded both quickly and efficiently. For this you shall receive your reward.
In addition, your previous service to Nuhmudira makes you deserving of a reward. I will now teach you the spells that Nuhmudira has devised to assist you in your salvaging efforts.
All is complete. I will write a report to Nuhmudira and see that she is made aware of all that you have done for her. Here is your reward.
Interesting, how did you come by this? It is a very nice gift. Thank you.

greetings: Um... I already fixed this for you. Perhaps you've been out in the sun too long?
I know it gets awfully hot out here. Take this flask and get a drink from the fountain.
Sit down for a while, before you start seeing Olthoi Queens doing a Viamont waltz!
Greetings! I rarely have visitors here in the hills...a pleasure to meet you!

Tell me, would you be able to procure a skeleton's skull for me? I have need of it in my research. Should you find one, I can provide you with a copy of my latest history tome. It's the first of a major multi-volume work!
quest: Good heavens! Do you know what you have here? Do you see these markings? This is a piece of the legendary Silifi of the Crimson Stars!

It looks like the blade, the rubies, and the top two jewel fittings have been broken off. I can repair the haft, but it will only be able to hold three of the five gems, should you manage to find them.
You'll also have to replace the blade. Here, this pamphlet has some suggestions and tips for you.
I'd choose carefully, were I you. As fragile as this is now, you wouldn't be able to remove the spine or the rubies try again.
Another broken haft? That's okay, I can still repair it for you. But, you know ... I really don't think Leikotha is your type.
chatter: Wonderful, wonderful!
Now I may continue my studies. Here is the book I mentioned. I'm sure you'll find it of interest. All my histories sold well on Ispar.

greetings: No my friend. Keep this. It may be useful.
What is this?
%n's eyes bulge out as he reads the plans.
I did not know that drudges were capable of building such a thing. I must report this to my superiors.
Here is a reward for your services.
What an interesting key. Thank you.
quest: I have given the plans to my superiors to be studied. Who would have known that drudges were capable of creating such a machine? We will have to keep an eye on them from now on.
Any luck spotting the great flying beast?
The last sighting was south and west of Fort Tethana, along the western coastline of the Direlands.
I have received reports from adventurers that a great beast has been seen flying across the Direlands. They say it is as big as a house and spits fire and acid.
This beast must be investigated and catalogued. Go and seek out this beast and bring back proof of your findings.
I am searching for someone to do some scouting for me. Unfortunately, you are as yet too weak to complete this task.

greetings: Wonderful!  Can you see the portal energy pulsing within it?
No doubt you have seen and experienced much on this adventure!
I have heard stories that the ancient dead of Dereth talk to each other as we do, and form a society underneath our own...
Let us see where this Kelannik fellow liked to travel.
Why, I do believe that this portal leads to the Mage Academy!  Beware young traveler, this place is not for the faint of heart...
Have you any news of my old colleague Celcynd, of Rithwic?  I have not seen him in many years, and I do fear for his peace of mind.
Hail, traveler. It is pleasant to meet anyone here in the wastes.  Tell me, have you discovered a crypt in these regions called the Burial Temple?
I have heard that the dead walk there, and one in particular always carries a certain black gem I seek for my research.
Through my studies, I have found that the dreadful creature is named Kelannik.
Please retrieve this gem and reutn it to me.  Your courage will not go unrewarded.
Ahh, here is the token of Nuhmudira's esteem.
Thank you.  You may now enter the portal.  I hope you enjoy the selection of goods.
quest: So have you found something?  Please give it to me, and I will give you in exchange a token from Nuhmudira.  She has instructed her Agents to give a Writ of Refuge in return for this token.  Or, you could give the token back to me, and I can give you temporary access to this portal beside me, where you can purchase interesting items of decor for your home.
Greetings, brave adventurer!  Time is short, I fear.  We have discovered a delicate situation.  While the Virindi have apparently been vanquished, not all of their minions have followed suit.

There is a crazed Hollow Minion, residing at the end of these tunnels.  We have never seen such a tenacious hollow minion commanding troops before.  I hope this is the worst of the surprises we face in the near future.

Nuhmudira preserve us.  If you are able to reach and vanquish the Hollow Minion, please see if he has left anything of note behind.  The Arcanum is extremely interested in getting at the root of this problem.  According to the Arcanum, portalspace disruptions around the nine Arrival towns are increasing daily.  We need to put a stop to this immediately.

greetings: Thank you!  I like collecting these.
Have you been to Rithwic yet?  I'd like you to take this letter to Celcynd.  He will pay you for it.
This is meant for Celcynd. Please take it to him.
quest: Why that ungrateful...er, thank you for bringing this to me.  Here is a small reward.
You dare mock my pain when my wounds are fresh?  Maybe if you come back tomorrow I will be able to deal with the matter.
Thanks for picking up that pickaxe for me. Now I can stop worrying about it and get back to business... Barkeep! Another ale over here.
Don't forget to find Djusfa bint Huqis in Zaikhal. She'll know all about what you're looking for.
Yeah, I like the beer here, so what?  I'll do some alchemy later. I could mine some crystals if I had my pickaxe...
chatter: Hiyp The Toad looks at you with a sodden expression

Hey, that's my best pickaxe!  I must have left it down in the, ummm, where was that... oh yeah there was that mine, I was tryin' to get some of those crystals them's in Zaikhal wanted. Maybe it'll help with the bugs, maybe not. Well, there's nothing in that mine, I'll tell ya. So I said to myself, forget it, go have a drink. You trying to get some too? Hmmm, I just may know someone who can get...

greetings: Interesting. This is the preliminary report on what the renegades have been able to learn about the Burun thus far. I'd be interested in and reward you for any further missives.
Interesting. I have seen this before. Others have brought them in to Aun laokhe and other Royal Guards. You can keep them. We're well aware of what is at work there.
A letter explaining something secret, eh? Perhaps this will provide you with better clues as to where true information can be found. You should keep it.
Another letter with information of a secret location. Haven't you found anything worth while yet?
This will provide us with more information than we currently have. You are to be thanked for your efforts.
quest: The guard listens intently as you explain what happened when you brought up the night of the attempted assassination.  "Interesting discovery, %s. It seems as though Antius' suspicions could be well founded. We shall do our best to track Nuhmudira and ensure that she cannot harm Elysa ever again." For your efforts, Antius wants you well payed.
I have been authorized to teach you the fourteen salvaging enhancements that have been crafted for learning the enhancement spells to the skill that Ciandra has created for all Isparians.
Thank you for your efforts, I will see that Antius is informed.

Hail, friend. My name is Ydnew. I have been sent by High Queen Elysa to discuss the frequency with which the Burun have been appearing. Further, I am here to see that we keep close attention on the movements of the Burun and their new allies, the Renegades.

The events of the past few months has brought a great deal of consternation into the High Queen's court. Since Rage Lao mistakenly opened the first portals from the world that these creatures came from, we have wondered what they were. We still know very little, but we are confident that we will learn more about them soon.
In the past few weeks, we have seen a rise in Renegade and Burun activity near the old swamp temple near 25s and 46e.

I have been given leave to reward adventurers who assist us in finding out as much information as they can about the new relationship that the Renegades have forged with these Burun. Please use caution when approaching the temple. We know that they have enclosed the structure and are busy working toward some other nefarious end as we speak.
If you begin to become overwhelmed, please retreat. We have no cause for people to needlessly endanger themselves against this threat.

greetings: Ummm.... yeah... what should I do with this?
You think these fanatics are going to release me if I give them pyreals?!
Just leave me alone.
Where am I? I finally found some nice people who help me escape from those lunatics on that backwards island, and they toss me into this cage threatening me with sacrifice and torture!
You don't think they mean to throw me into their sacrificial pit, do you?
Haha, no, they wouldn't do that... I mean, why would they?
chatter: Help me.

greetings: You wish this sword converted into a dagger?  Very well, I shall do my best. I hope you do not end up with just the hilt, like my last three customers...
Despite his quips, Omaro Nagate skillfully refashions the Sword of Frozen Fury into a Dagger of Frozen Fury
I am just joking. Here you are.
Hello. I have some skills with modifying weapons, though I am still learning the craft.
Oh, thank you! You're most kind.

Good day! I see that you're an adventurous sort. So am I, my dear friend! I must admit that I have been in better spirits than I am at the moment, but the sight of another adventurer has caused a smile to spread across my face.

You see, I have just finished a jaunt across and all around Dereth. I managed to make the walk in about eighty days. I've only recently settled here in the pleasantly arid air of Candeth Keep. I had a particularly nasty run-in with some foul undead near the southern entrance of the Valley of Death.

While making my way into a valley, I was accosted by these foul looking undead beasts. They gave me such a fright that I lost a collection of rare plates I'd received from Baron Eli von Schreft back on Ispar. They're priceless, and I would certainly be pleased if someone were to bring them back to me. If you find them please bring them here.
Thank you for liberating me! I hope you are not injured!  I see Glysander has sent you. I know he is anxious to recover the letters but alas, I cannot continue this quest now.

Here are two letters I have found. I can tell you where to find another letter, or its exact copy. Find Lia Tze in Baishi. She has a letter in her possession, and I was informed she might have a means for you to obtain a replica of Thorsten Cragstone's Armor.  Or you may go to Tou-Tou and seek out a man named Tai Wo. He has a copy of the same letter Lia Tze has and may have knowledge of how to...
Those Tumeroks have me trapped here. I am glad their number has been dealt a severe blow!
Thank you for saving my life!

I was taken prisoner by a group of Tumeroks and locked in this cell. If you can find my talisman I can use it to portal out of this dungeon. The talisman should be with the rest of my belongings somewhere in this dungeon.
chatter: Can anyone please help me?

greetings: This mask is interesting, yet it is too damaged for me to make use of.
What a wonderous metal! It seems to be even more potent than a standard Virindi Mask! If only it weren't broken ...
This would provide a fine base for the wrap worn by our people back on Ispar, but it will need to be repaired before I can do anything with it.
Or you could give this to my apprentice after you have it fixed. He'll restore it to be more like the Virindi that it was taken from.
This would provide an excellent base for a head wrap, but it will need to be repaired before I can do anything with it.
I'm sorry, the carapace of Olthoi are to hard to carve.  Perhaps you can find someone else to help.  I heard to the north they can make these into strong helmets.
Thank you, but I am not a cook. Here, you keep it.
%mn whispers to you, "Aye, I know your secret One-Eyed %tn."

A find worthy of crafting into a robe! But you still require another arm, two legs and a torso. You should be able to assemble those together without my aid. But only a master such as myself would be able to craft such objects into a fully wearable outfit.

A find worthy of crafting into a robe! But you still require another leg, two arms and a torso. You should be able to assemble those together without my aid. But only a master such as myself would be able to craft such objects into a fully wearable outfit.

A find worthy of crafting into a robe! But you still require two arms and two legs. You should be able to assemble those together without my aid. But only a master such as myself would be able to craft such objects into a fully wearable outfit.

A find worthy of crafting into a robe! But you still require two arms and a torso. You should be able to assemble those together without my aid. But only a master such as myself would be able to craft such objects into a fully wearable outfit.
What a fine mask! Such well-preserved fur!
You know, I really hate these creatures.
HA! HA! HA! HA! HA! HA! HA! HA! HA!
Oh, that's funny.
Wonderful craftsmanship! We mask makers are a crafty lot!
I hear Elysa holds the most wonderful costume parties. You should wear this if you're ever lucky enough to receive an invitation!
Think of the havoc you could cause in the marketplace!
Do you smell that? This thing stinks!

This is very odd. This mask is made out of a very strange material. I can unwind it, almost like thread on a spindle. Curious ... Here is my finished product. May it protect you as it did the Avengers of Yasif.
This is an item of power. Truly, it is a work of art.
This will only take me a moment and I think that you will like the outcome. Another twist in the cloth here and yes ... yes, that's it.
This Shroud of Night will guard your face from the desert sands and aid you in your travels.
Ah, how graceful ... and yet quite strong. Let me just work with it a moment ...
Although you watch closely, the mask maker's hands move too quickly and skillfully to follow.

There is no greater hero in our culture than Yasif ibn Salayyar. I have chosen to honor him with this piece. May the face of this great poet allow you to see, as he did, with a sight beyond sight, and grant you wisdom untold.
It is said that a poet can find beauty in even the lowest of forms.  Whoever said this has obviously never met a Drudge.
There are many undead within the confines of the desert.  Perhaps by wearing this you will pass amongst them unnoticed, but they have a way of sensing living flesh...
Hmmm.  I have seen creatures like this before, but not so well equipped.  Wherever did you acquire this trophy?  It's skull is very thick, providing a very strong mask.
There are many of these currently roaming Dereth.  Be careful that wearing this mask does not cause you to be mistaken for one.
I have heard of these creatures roaming the mountains, and recently coming down to the grasslands.  Is this a Mattekar?
There are many of these creatures roaming the desert.  They seem to be increasing in frequency at an incredible rate.
I have seen many of these creatures as well.  They seem to be a creation of the Virindi.  This mask seems to have extremely odd abilities.
Here you go, a new version of the Mosswart Mask.
Here you go, a new version of the Banderling Mask.
That's a stinky fish head! You want one of these fresh masks.
I'm sorry, I'm not a cook.
You want a what? You should never put a ch... Okay... I won't judge you. Here.
These are hard to find. Here, nobody will know who you are in this mask!
You seriously want a mask made from this thing?
Well ok...
Considering that you do not seem pleased with the masks, perhaps you would enjoy this instead?
Tusker heads are large enough to make packs out of.  Here, have one.
Give me a moment and I will craft a fine costume for you from this body.
I've always had a soft spot in my heart for mites.
