They taste great with a little tarragon and melted butter. You wouldn't happen to have carved off any meat when you obtained this head, would you? No? Ah well.
They wait thousands of years to seek vengeance for who knows what ancient crime, and what happens when they finally arrive on Dereth? Some tiny Isparian lops off their head! I love it!
Ridiculous creatures, these chitticks. But they're great in a stew!
You'll be the belle of the ball with this fine costume!
I just learned how to make this costume. I must say, I am most impressed with myself!
Now, this is one fine costume. Go forth and scare some new arrivals!
A pleasure to meet you! I am Janda. If you would be so kind as to give me a creature's head or facial covering, I will make it into a mask that will allow you to participate in the celebration.
Did you know there is a ceremonial mask for each culture? I so long for the day that I can make a ceremonial mask of my own!
The desert is quite hot during the day. Don't wear your mask too much in direct sunlight, or you may suffer from heat stroke.
quest: Hey, you already turned one of these in to me. Let's finish the first one before we make a second mask.
I'll just stretch the cloth over the mask and secure it and... there now you have a nice new... one of these.
Yes, I can make a mask of this if you find me a Scarecrow Head.
This already seems to be a mask of sorts.  Well, here you go.

greetings: Thank you! We don't know who built the distillery, but it must be very old. The stuff we have tried making isn't as good as some of the mysterious stuff we found in it.
At the very bottom is a cellar where the best ancient drinks were found. The key I gave you earlier should open it. If you bring me back a bottle of distillery ambrosia, I will reward you well.
Ah, this is a fine bottle! You have done well. Please take these presents as a token of my gratitude.
Ah, a wonderful find -- the most useful and finest drink I have ever tasted! Here is something for you, thank you!
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here.  You are a true Explorer!
Take this -- but if you would prefer an atlatl, I have those too. Just hand the bow back to me.
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here. You are a true Explorer!
Take this -- but if you would prefer at atlatl, I have those too. Just hand the bow back to me.
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Hey, looks like it got rolled in the mud... Anyway, well done!  Here, take these as a reward.
Ah, looks like you've found our agent's towel!  Looks like good old F.P. went swimming or something.  Here's your reward.
Looks like you've lucked out!  Our man F.P. has finished his book, finally!  Here you go...
Ah, a truly adventurous soul. Here you are!

I have been contracted by the Dereth Exploration Society to help them in their outreach program towards the Isparians who find themselves newly exiled in Dereth.  Here is a book that explains their mission.  I am also giving you a list describing the locations of the nearest stamp and portals to other towns.  If you collect any of the Society's stamped letters, you may bring them back to me for...
By the way -- if you haven't yet done so, you might want to visit Beltslora at the West Outpost, or Ercel at the East Outpost. They often have tasks for young adventurers.
quest: You must stamp this with a Town Stamp to get a reward.  Please read your Book of Quests to find out how to get a Stamp.
No, this is for you to stamp the letters you find.  Please keep it.
Thank you, you must have journeyed far to get here.  You are a true Explorer!

You will get nothing from me for this. Go explore and find more towns.  The Society Agents in the Gharun'dim towns will exchange a piece of armor for this. If you take this to one of the Sho towns, you will receive a weapon.
chatter: We must stay vigilant here in Lytelthorpe Keep in case the monsters return.
Ah, I see you've helped Beltslora, perhaps you could help me also. There are monsters in the old distillery to the south of town.
Come to think of it, there hasn't been anything good to drink here ever since the distillery was overrun. If you could retrieve a bottle of distillery nectar for me I would greatly appreciate it.
That Ercel, always thinking about the sky instead of what's going on on the ground. Perhaps you could help me also.
There are monsters in the old distillery to the south of town. Come to think of it, there hasn't been anything good to drink here ever since the distillery was overrun.
If you could retrieve a bottle of distillery nectar for me I would greatly appreciate it.

greetings: My rye! Thank you!
My wheat! Thank you!
My corn! Thank you!
You killed that brute that stole my seed! Thank you so much! You are truly a hero worthy of the name.

If you are looking for more adventure friend - and you certainly seem to be good at it - you might want to peruse the rumors that Wilomine has at the bar. Or perhaps you should journey to Shoushi. I hear that there are many good people there who may need your help!

Hello, hello! May I buy you a drink? Oh ... no, I am out of pyreal again. I had forgotten. That is the danger of drowning your troubles, I suppose - you may forget the troubles in the drink, but you forget everything else as well!

My troubles? How kind of you to ask. I would be happy to tell you my troubles! You see, I am a farmer ... well, all right ... an aspiring farmer. I just know that I could be a good farmer if I could but get the seed in the ground. But drudges keep stealing my seed!

If you could retrieve my seed bags for me - all three of them - and perhaps bring me the head of the dastardly drudge who is behind the theft, I will reward you well. You can find the drudges in their nearby Hideout; Wilomine at the bar has directions.
quest: Hmmm? No, this isn't mine. Why don't you try asking Flinrala about it?
I believe that Worcer was looking for this! Why don't you try taking it to him?
Flinrala is always talking about this type of thing. Why don't you show this to her?

greetings: I am pleased to see you. Did you find notes I left on the way?  There are Olthoi in tunnels all around us. We have been helping defend this area but we may be overrun soon.
Words... are... meaningless...

There's something really strange about those caves north of here.  Gives me the shakes just to think about it... Hey, be a nice kid and get me a bowl of Carrot Soup, and I'll tell you what's what, all right?
chatter: Thanks! I had a bad case of the shakes there. Here's a key to get you into those caves up there.
Those scary caves... It's giving me the shakes again...  Oh, those caves of ice!

greetings: Please deliver this note to my brother, Suzuhara Baijin. You can find him in Stonehold.
Hello, friend. How do you like this ocean breeze? I feel it has quite a restorative property.
I came down with this nasty cough a few months ago when my brother and I explored one of those new Burun pits. I just cannot seem to shake it.
This ocean breeze seems to be working. I feel much better now than I did before I arrived.
chatter: %mn coughs loudly.
Phlegm rattles in %mn's lungs as a nasty bout of coughing racks his weakened frame.
Ah, this cough is going to kill me.
Blessed sea breeze, work your magic.
A package? From my dear brother? What a wonderful man! So thoughtful, he is!
And I should thank you as well for delivering this package to me. Would you be so kind as to return to him with this note of gratitude?

quest: %n spits at your feet.
You abandoned Nuhmudira? Get out of my sight!
You helped Nuhmudira! You are a very noble person.
%n snaps to attention, and salutes you.

You are most welcome within this place. We need your help. There are sclavus beyond this portal that are as strong as a Banderling Antagonist. If you feel that you can handle fighting these creatures you are welcome to enter.
Everyone should have the opportunity to strike a blow against these defiling creatures.
You may also, if you are lucky, find a gorget inside. Balthazar can explain a little bit more about this item to you. Good luck, friend!
%n looks you over with a wary eye.
I do not know you, stranger. You are not supposed to be here. You should speak to Balthazar, outside.

greetings: Thank you for the Sunflower Oil! Thou hast made a wise purchase! Here is thy  instruction book explaining how to craft the Horn of Vigilance and thy free carving knife! Be certain to read the instruction book carefully. There are a mere four items you will have to loot from creatures I am certain you will easily defeat. Then you must carve them into the appropriate components.
You may begin by getting a large Niffis Shell. It is needed for the base of the instrument. Not a small Niffis shell, mind you, but a large one- you are not in the business of crafting a mere kazoo!

Whoa friend! Are you having a problem with your Horn of Vigilance? I cannot provide a refund for this item or exchange it! I have fifteen of these things around my house and they don't do a da... uh, I mean, they don't allow any Olthoi to intrude into my domain. Heh, heh! Hey, when was the last time you saw Olthoi around here?  Run along now please, I have customers to attend to.

Hello harried traveler. Is thy residence threatened by Olthoi or other vermin?  Then thou art in need of the Horn of Vigilance! I have been commissioned by the famed Isparian Researcher Telk the Addlepated to sell instructions for this device that he has spent decades developing. The merest breath of wind blowing through this instrument produces a sound which is not discernible by human ears, y...

Such a fine instrument could easily be sold for 999,999,999 Pyreals, however I will provide you with everything you need to craft it for a mere jar of Sunflower Oil!  For one single jar of Sunflower Oil I will provide thee with a beautiful, leather bound, instruction book describing the easy to follow crafting steps for making the astounding Horn of Vigilance.
But hark! There is more!

For no extra fee at all I will give thee an extremely useful carving knife which thou may use to craft this item!  This knife alone has a thousand and one uses! It can carve arrowshafts, cut meat and chicken, chop cabbage, filet fish, slice mushrooms and carrots, cut bread and even carve a pumpkin! Is that not extraordinary?!

Thus, I strongly urge thee to hurry, pick a Sunflower and bring it to Lilly of Glenden Wood.  She will make thee some Sunflower Oil which thou should bring back to me. It is just that effortless! One may find Sunflowers in forested areas of North and South Osteth.
When you return I will tell you about other items required. Good hunting!

Lead by Mgrauleshk, a Guruk Gorefiend, the Burun storm the Temple of Izji Qo. The portal gateway in the matron's crypt has become active and the Burun have stormed a receiving chamber containing a sealed portal. Mgrauleshk and his force will break through the wall and activate the portal beacon, bringing the Burun masters to Dereth unless they are stopped within ninety minutes.
quest: His force successful, Mgrauleshk stands before the portal beacon in Izji Qo's temple. He sacrifices the life's blood of one of his force to the beacon and it hums to life. Pungent fumes and the damp swamp air filter into the receiving chamber. Mgrauleshk finds his way to kneel by the side of the first Burun master to cross the vast divide.
chatter: Lead by Mgrauleshk, a Guruk Gorefiend, the Burun storm the Temple of Izji Qo. The portal gateway in the matron's crypt has become active and the Burun have stormed a receiving chamber containing a sealed portal. Mgrauleshk and his force will break through the wall and activate the portal beacon, bringing the Burun masters to Dereth unless they are stopped within ninety minutes.

greetings: It was you people that brought Martine to his end. You and your meddling. Why couldn't you have left him alone?
He was finally becoming happy, but then you had to come down here and cause your ruckus and look where we are now.
Everything is falling apart and your hands are tainted. Your hands are covered in his blood.
You make me sick.

Ahh, I've been waiting for these. Not long mind you. The Lugians are very prompt in their delivery, nothing at all like the vermin I'm used to working with back on Ispar. Never mind the dogs living here on Dereth. This be for Captain K'rank.
Tell 'im that I'm willing to continue this advantageous relationship, so long as he's willing to keep supplying me with these herbs.

Arrr, and welcome to MacNiall's Freehold. Have ye seen them funny statue things the Mosswarts like to worship? I thinks their eyes is kinda pretty. Bring me one, and I'll see what I can do to reward ye.
quest: Errukh, look at the sparkle! Look, youngster, I'll give ye this note for my cousin MacDugal. I hear tell he's taken up residence with our old gang at some place called the Bandit Castle. Bring this note to him, and he'll reward ye right.
Oi mucker, I've already given ye the note to pass on to MacDugal! Don't tell me ye've lost it! Take this bauble back too, simpleton!
chatter: Bloody Pwyll-worshipping lackeys...
Don't believe what the townies on the other island tell ye, the bunch of bleating sheep that they are... Hrm. It's been a while since I seen a sheep.
Well, Jourgensson says you're all right.  Maybe you can help.  Down underneath the castle, there's a prison full of beasties.  That idiot Gwillim dropped some notes and his bag in there.
Now he says he can't mix potions!  Bring the bag back to him, and he'll reward you.  You'll need this to get in there.

greetings: The whistling wind, the wood, the biting metal ... these are the atoms of existence.
If you insist on putting motivations to our being, talk to Ms. Comfore. She's the political one.
quest: No, no, no! You must take your time! Live with the object! Dream it! Art of this magnitude should take you at least a week.
Not the finest quality toothpick available, but it will have to do.
This looks like a Lugian picked its teeth with it! I'll accept it, but I won't like it!
Excellent! This pick is flimsy and ugly, but you are beginning to learn the soul of the art!
Your art is improving! This pick, however, is still trash.
Better, better. Not very good, but better. Keep trying!
This pick ... this pick is almost acceptable! If you continue at this rate, you will soon be ready to move on to darts!
Amazing! Simply amazing! You have crafted an almost useable toothpick.
Wow! It's obvious you have spent a lot of time perfecting the noble art of Toothpick crafting.
The quality of the point of this pick is astounding!
Perfect! Well, nearly perfect. There is always room to learn.
%n spits at your feet.
You abandoned Nuhmudira? Get out of my sight!
You helped Nuhmudira! You are a very noble person.
%n snaps to attention, and salutes you.

You are most welcome within this place. We need your help. There are sclavus beyond this portal that are as strong as a Banderling Berserker. If you feel that you can handle fighting these creatures you are welcome to enter.
Everyone should have the opportunity to strike a blow against these defiling creatures.
You may also, if you are lucky, find a gorget inside. Balthazar can explain a little bit more about this item to you. Good luck, friend!
%n looks you over with a wary eye.
I do not know you, stranger. You are not supposed to be here. You should speak to Balthazar, outside.

greetings: What is happening? This is not the right place. I just came from the warehouse. We should not have arrived here. I sense danger! Are you going further? I'm staying here!
chatter: This is wrong.  What happened?
This is not right! We are not supposed to be here.
I came from the warehouse. What is this place?
The portal took us to the wrong location!

greetings: Arrr!  Don't bother me!  I've got enough problems on me hands!  Talk to my lieutenant, Jourgensson!
chatter: Well, Jourgensson says you're all right.  Maybe you can help.  Down underneath the castle, there's a prison full of beasties.  That idiot Gwillim dropped some notes and his bag in there.
Now he says he can't mix potions!  Bring the bag back to him, and he'll reward you.  You'll need this to get in there.

Errukh! A letter from my long-lost cousin, MacNiall! Arrr, it's good to see the old boy doing well! I ought to reward ye for this, as he says. Here then, have one of my blade hilts. I'm workin' on a way to improve daggers and light swords.

Ye'll need to finish off that hilt with a pommel from the heart of an Iron Golem, but once it's done, ye can just affix it to a dagger, simi, shortsword, yaoji or rapier. They yer blade'll be so well-balanced ye can do a fancy double or triple-strike when ye put enough skill and power into it!

greetings: As %s smites the Hellfire, the subterranean creatures sigh, and begin to disappear back into the vents and fumaroles they came up through. Mount Lethe is peaceful again... or at least as peaceful as it ever gets.
Consumed in flames again. The world bends to HIS will now. Not even the oldest can touch his power. We shall not fail in bringing him to the sanctum.
%s has defeated Strife, the Essence of Flame, repelling Gaerlan's forces back from the cities of the north...for now.

This is not right. My essence, my being. Something is wrong. The master. The master has betrayed us. My essence, my freedom. I was. No more. I am nothing again. Less than nothing, I am harvested. A vessel has been prepared.
%s has defeated Strife, the Essence of Flame. Its form is driven from the world and Gaerlan's forces are routed at Glenden Wood, Plateau Village, Stonehold, and Arwic.
You are not worthy of the lowest of my children. A flare would claim your flesh as its fuel.
I am magic given life. I am the essence of war, strife and consumption. I am flame personified! Your parlor tricks would be better aimed elsewhere.
%s has defeated Strife, the Essence of Flame.

As %s smites the Hellfire, the flame-creatures sigh, and begin to disappear back into the vents and fumaroles they surfaced through. But, from the base of the mountain's slopes, you hear the whisper of falling ash, and the clacking of petrified bones...
As %s smites the Firestorm, the flame-creatures sigh, and begin to disappear back into the submerged vents and fumaroles they surfaced through. The lake of Mount Esper is peaceful again.
The rift pulses, and disgorges a creature!
The rift surges with crackling energy, and a creature appears!
The air becomes heavy with ozone, and another creature spawns from the rift!
Mowen Smash!
Mowen Crush!
Mowen Beat!
Mowen Kill!
Mowen beat fleshy beast into tiny pulp that squirt between his fingers.
chatter: I should be walking around and stuff.
Who da Tusker? Who da Tusker?!

greetings: The Assailer grunts, Soon... Tusker King... Bobo come!
Me like nanners!
Me like nanners.
Bobo king, me watch village.

quest: Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.
You feel the presence of the High Matriarch watching you and withdraw your hand.
How did you get here?

greetings: If you believe that items belongs in this room, drop it on the floor.
quest: You did not leave the proper offering.

greetings: With a hiss, steam begins pouring forth from a fissure deep beneath the crust of the world. A column of heat rises to the pool above this area producing a massive amount of energy.

quest: Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.

greetings: A plate is already set into this pillar. Perhaps you should try using a plate on a pillar with a free setting.
A plate rests inside the depression on this pillar. The plate displays an oddly positioned geometric shape.
The pillar has what appears to be a setting for a plate of some kind.
You place the plate into the depression.
quest: As you look about the room the answer comes to you. The plate slides into place with a click.
As the plate slides into position dread washes over you. Something is clearly not right. Your palms become sweaty and your vision swims.
Though you are certain that this is correct combination to the puzzle, nothing happens. Perhaps you are too weak to enter this place. Now there is the matter of getting out.
You place the plate into the depression.
You're not quite sure how this plate fits with the pillar. Perhaps if you speak with the statue in the center of the room it can provide some insight.
Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.
Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.
Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.

Your Fletching skill is temporarily increased. You feel more confident - more powerful. But at the same time, your heart flutters within your chest, your breath catches in your throat, and you feel a deep, dark cold in the pit of your stomach. You wonder briefly just what long-term effect this crafting forge may have on you.
You are commended for fueling the Fletching Forge!
You are commended for fueling the Fletching Forge! From now on you shall obtain a longer-lasting boon from all crafting forges!

greetings: "Apparently the instructions were lost upon a mind as small as yours, %tn. You have failed this test."
"You have quelled the spirits here. You may proceed onward."

quest: You feel the presence of the High Matriarch watching you and withdraw your hand.
How did you get here?
Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.
You feel the presence of the High Matriarch watching you and withdraw your hand. You are not beneath her notice it seems. Perhaps if you wait the cycle of the moons.
There is nothing here for those who have not sacrificed or worked to restore the High Matriarch.
This should never happen
The room shudders and a thunderclap sounds about you. Something has been summoned.
The device does not move, it seems to be without power.
A loud hum fills the room and for a moment you feel waves of mana washing over your body. You are certain that something has changed.
The portal remains silent.
A loud hum fills the room and for a moment you feel waves of mana washing over your body. The room shudders around you and the beacon comes to life, pulling you deeper into the temple of Kivik Lir.

greetings: A weak voice sounds from within, "The temple lives again, but I do not control it. The flux is opened!"
quest: There seems to be nothing here for you.
You find that the garb placed atop the sarcophagus is intact and take it for yourself.
In searching over the sarcophagus, you find that another grave robber has taken anything of worth.

greetings: "You have proven your knowledge. You shall be allowed within the Temple. But be warned, the mistress sleeps still. Guardians, Wards and defenses against intrusion remain active. If you are true to the Iakvi Liviliakti then you shall reach her crypt. Wake her, she will welcome you, sister."
"Pray that you have chosen your fellows wisely, for the trials ahead will call upon you stay amongst them. Failure at any step will bring death upon you all."
"False one! Ekta vaik av iaktik!"
You feel the blood within your body being pulled through your flesh. Your world turns to darkness.
"Shi vaik tukinti ikni likik ki inki Viliakti, av esk ilti?"
The language is guttural and hard. You do not understand what was asked of you, but you know that it was a question. As it speaks again, a vein of understanding spreads through you.

"Jiktani ekta irntrika to the matron of this temple. Prove to Ixir Zi that you are devout followers of the Watcher. Bring me the sacred gem from this room. Only then will I recognize the work of your and your fellows."

"Once you have completed this challenge you will then need to stay amongst your fellows through the remainder of this temple. I shall grant you entrance into the halls of High Matron Ixir Zi's temple, only when you have succeeded. You must gather into groups of equivalent learning. Failure av iakvi."
These are four funny tuskers. Each likes to play with a ball, but they will only play with a ball of their favorite color. Speak to them to learn whose favorite color is which. But be warned:

One is a liar, One always tells the truth, one alternates between the truth and fiction and the last, whose rules for telling the truth when he makes three statements are different than the other three tuskies.

One final note: The tuskies like the color of the balls dependent on their age. The youngest likes the green ball. The oldest likes the blue ball. The second oldest likes the red ball. The second youngest likes the yellow ball.
When you think you have figured out the puzzle hand the balls to the children. Then use the statue on the other side of the room to see if you are right so you can pass into the master's room.

quest: Correct.
Incorrect!
Incorrect.

greetings: A chill wind passes over your body. "You live still. We hunger so for life. Will you join us?"
You sense eyes staring at you from the darkness.
The hair on your neck rises as a voice sounds in your mind. "Once we were, but our souls linger, given to him, given to him..."
Your head fills with the sound of a banshee's wail.
"Silence in this room, we may no longer have forms, but still we read and live."
A shrill voice says in your mind, "Is she fallen? How was this temple freed?"

A light breeze and the scent of rotting meat wash over you. Your stomach threatens to revolt for a moment. You see a ceremonial robe upon your body and feel the cold of stone on your back. A slender woman with gentle features stands above you holding a curved dagger. She mutters in a language that you do not know and plunges the dagger into your heart. As life ebbs, you hear a gentle song being...

A snake-man dresses you in a fine silken robe. Nearby a woman cries, at her feet a small child with golden eyes attempts to stifle the tears which brim at his eyes. You smile, and turn from them and are led toward an altar by the snake-man.

There is the smell of something sweet nearby. The moons are large and high above your head. Four spires the color of sea-foam rise about you, and a chill wind blows. You taste blood, and the heady scent of sage fills your senses. You cough and shower yourself in blood.

A small whispering voice calls to you, "It follows its own whim, now here, now there, now gone, once we held it, but not it is gone. When the wheel turns it shall be here again, but first there shall be gold."
You pull a book from the shelves of the bookcase. As you do so you notice a small collection of papers fall from within the pages.
quest: There is the sound of a hammer falling against stone, all around you. It is dark, and the smell of befouled earth fills your nostrils.
A voice whispers, "These are the notes of the peoples of the chill, they who served the master, the splendor, the glory. Disturb them not."

Your heads pounds. A stream of mana flows over and through you washing away your flesh and leaving only your bones. You feel closer to magic, though you are weaker of form. The vision ends as does the pain in your skull.

A voice in your mind giggles, "Can you hear the voices? Do you heed their words? Think you master magic, do you master swords? Are you just a keeper or a puppet by a string? Can you hear the voices listen to them sing."
A ghostly hand extends and places a book into your hand.
A book wreathed in flame thrusts itself into your hands.
A chilling hand grabs yours and places a book in your hand.
A scent of brimstone accompanies the hand that appears to place a book in your hand.
A low hum is heard as a hand extends from the bookcase and places a book into your hand.
A soft voice alights upon your ear, "We watch this age with baited breath. Slowly it slips from the grasp of the race that held this world. Now it is anothers."

A light breeze surrounds you momentarily. You see a city of alabaster, sapphire and gold stretching toward the sky. Skyships the color of the sun traverse the sky. A man wearing a cerulean crown walks toward you and hands you a missive. As you open the document he stretches his hand forward holding a brooch for you.
He knows you are here and he will be prepared. He stole his throne. Take it back for the master.

You are sitting at a table in this very room as a chill shakes you to your soul. You feel breath brush against your neck. You turn but there is no one to be seen. The candles flicker as a breeze fills the room. You gently close your book and call upon fire to form beside you. A minor elemental appears. A small prism within your robes turns to dust.
You stumble as the staircase shifts beneath your feet. You maintain your balance as they slide to the far wall.

As you step over the threshold into the small room you are immediately drawn to the bookcase before you. It is as though it calls your name. As you approach its hands reach toward you and offer knowledge to you.

The trials left you shaken but you were prepared for much worse. You shoulder your weight against your staff and rest a moment, age it seems has the better of you. Your wrinkled skin makes you feel ill, there is still so much to accomplish. You sense the hundreds of eyes within the room and call to them.
You smile as the companion novel slides from the bookshelf. You now have all you need.

You run your hand over the cover of the tome and pull the other from within your pack. The first was found in Xarabydun, this new tome is its equal, the second in a set of three. One more and your knowledge shall be complete.
A voice says, "He commands the spirits here now, blood given to the Blood."

greetings: You press the button.

quest: Despite your better judgement, you look over the sarcophagus for trinkets. It seems as though other grave robbers have beaten you to the prize.
Defiler! You seek to ruin my slumber and my home? Suffer for your insolence!
Another grave robber has looted this crypt. There is nothing here for you.
Despite your better judgement, you look over the sarcophagus for trinkets.
How in the Sam heck did you do this?
You are not able to wrest the leggings from the cold grasp of the matron alone.
You touch the Pillar, infusing some of its darkness into your self.
You have 30 minutes to touch the associated Effigy, elsewhere in this Mausoleum.
You are unworthy to be in this Mausoleum!

greetings: With a soft rumble the two halves of the bookcase part.
quest: You think, "I had to pull the book again. Too much thinking about what might lurk in the dark hallways beyond stymied me where I stood. I felt foolish."
You think, "I could have been drinking ale by now."

A poor man has too much of me, a wealthy man needs me not, and if you feast upon me you will die. What am I?
At night they come without being called, but at dawn they are lost without being stolen. What are they?
It never was, is always to be, none have seen it, but many dream of it, it is the hope of all that live that it shall always come. What is it?
It begins eternity, ends time and space, it rests at the start of every end and the end of every place. What is it?
It waits for none and gauges all, it is eaten by leisure and work the same, it is abundant but there never seems to be enough. What is it?
No sound, no voice, no breath, no sleep, no thought, no sight, no more. What is it?
It cannot be slain so long as there is a ray,  it is inspires the heart to wish for the best, yet exercise caution to not lose this gift for then you shall just be forlorn. What is it?
What has no beginning or end, yet binds two together?
I cannot exist when I'm full, and I grow when you empty my contents. What am I?
I can be an old love, but mostly a lost passion. My life grows as you feed me, but when I drink water I die. What am I?
What is it that has one voice but becomes four-footed, two-footed, and three-footed?
I pass through the water and never get wet. What am I?
I whip, and I whistle all the day long, sometimes my voice can sound as a song. I never grow tired but sometimes grow weak, and I change without warning and cause door to creak. What am I?
I've legs, and a foot, and also a head. But I cannot think nor move on my own. What am I?
I am a room without walls, windows or doors. What am I?
I never grow, but can become very wide, and everything falls into darkness when I hide. What am I?
I am void, and absence, I am not a color. What am I?
You will break me if you name me. What am I?
The maker want it not, the buyer does not use it, and the user never sees it. What is it?
The more of me there is the less you see. What am I?

You think, "I didn't remember seeing this place before, but somewhere in the dark shadows that shrouded my mind, I knew I had. Sure it had changed, but a lot had changed since I walked through that first swirling portal on Ispar. I was no hero there. I was simply living my life. I felt like I was waiting for something."
You think, "I had the urge to dance..."
You think, "I suddenly realized that this tree was different from the others. There was a light syrupy texture that coated the branches. I pulled my hand up to my lips for a quick taste."

You think, "A heavy weight landed on my shoulders in the form of my head. It was like having 'Weight of the World' cast on you while making a run to the shop to unload your latest armor haul. Everything slowed down and a taste of honey filled my mouth.  I dropped to a knee..."
You think, "...but it wasn't enough. I fell to the ground, like a mosswart who had zigged when he should have zagged."

You think, "The world spun out of control, a long gray tunnel filled with purple shards told me that I was heading back to my lifestone. The tree's sap had played the role of hammer to my olthoi shell."
You think, "But my ride through the big swirl dropped me somewhere else. I didn't know where I was. An open book on a nearby desk called to me."
You think, "I like trees. Cripes, I hope no one saw me rubbing up against this tree."

You think, "I was rattled. I found myself unable to find the forest for the trees. I ran my hands along the bark, searching for any type of clue that might help me understand what the Dame wanted. I should have been listening. Now I was out here playing patty-cake with a tree..."
You think, "...I felt pretty foolish."

A shrieking sound pulses from the core of the falling Virindi as it collapses into its center, and it whispers in your mind, "We shall be set upon you, flesh puppet, as retribution for your role in the corruption of the Directors..."

A shrieking sound pulses from the core of the falling Virindi as it collapses into its center, and it whispers in your mind, "You may destroy this construct, human, but there is still strength in our Unity.  You and yours have not triumphed, will not triumph."

A shrieking sound pulses from the core of the falling Virindi as it collapses into its center, and it whispers in your mind, "We anticipate the day, human, when we can devote all of our time and attention to making your kind more suitable to the new order..."

A shrieking sound pulses from the core of the falling Virindi as it collapses into its center, and it whispers in your mind, "When the renegades have been brought back to heel, human, your kind, the source of their corruption, will feel the wrath of our unified might..."

As you deal the fatal blow to the Virindi Inquisitor, its luridly colored form collapses silently to the ground.  Behind the black mask, just for a moment, a swirling mass appears, then blinks out of existence.  A dissonant alien voice whispers, "Vulgar flesh puppet!  The Quiddity should not have decided to spare your kind!"

As you deal the fatal blow to the Virindi Inquisitor, its luridly colored form collapses silently to the ground. Your life cycle is a crude imitation of our own link to the Quiddity, human.  Still, hopefully this experience shall teach you to know your place.
Is that what you call magic, flesh puppet?  Your dependence on flesh makes your efforts pathetic!
Thank you, I find this most pleasant. Run along, now.
You know... two of the little flesh things managed to escape to the southeast...
I'm not entirely convinced the Director and the Observer are communicating properly...
A pity the Dark Walker has been banished. He was most entertaining to watch.
Just between you, me, and the bottle, human, the theft of the Fragment of Singularity has made some beings angry.
Just don't tell the Observer that I'm drinking this human filth, okay?
I saw a human with a sword attack an Executor the other day. The human never stood a chance. Rip, rip, rip, another inert human.
I find that I have acquired a taste for the wine sold by the Barkeep. Would you bring me a glass? Good human.
Here is the item you seek.  Use it on our enemies.
Odd... you are not as the master described.  Your epidermis is fair and supple.

This is not what I need.  This needs to be coiled with a sliver of Chorizite and then with Obsidian.
This is not what I need.  This needs to be coiled with a sliver of Pyreal and then with Obsidian.
This is not what I need.  Combine it with a coil of the Chorizite and Pyreal slivers.
This is not quite complete.  You must coil this with the sliver of Obsidian from the repository in the Obsidian Plains.

This is what is required... I will make you the portal to enter the Seat of the New Singularity.  Seek out Levistras and put an end to the renegade faction's disastrous plan.  Levistras is vulnerable, because in his ambition he has severed his connection to the home Singularity, before the completion of the New Singularity!
My agents have summoned a return portal within if you wish to return to this town. Now, stand back, lest you interfere with my casting...
Strike now, human!

Greetings, human.  Call me Ecorto.  I have disjoined myself from those who plan your eradication because I disagree with their methods.  Their plan to construct a New Singularity in this realm is madness.  Even now they gather and imbue material to construct their monstrous dream.  Find the repositories of the New Singularity in the desert, the southern mountains and the Obsidian Plains, human.
chatter: I was with the renegades... no use trying to hide that... but I disagree with some of the things they are doing...
If we cannot think of anything quieter and tidier than that... We are not any better than these humans...
Oh, we're not united any more than you are.
What human foolishness is this?  I gave you this chisel, human!  Take it!  It is for your use, that you may attempt to save your own kind!

quest: The Gerent has departed for the Singularity. Before his departure he shared his knowledge with me and it appears as though you have visited us recently. Thus, I am unable to meet your request. You will need to wait a while longer before we will furnish you with another Energy Crystal.

We are still not prepared to discuss the benefits of a shared consciousness, but the Gerent seeks the approval of the Quiddity on this matter. Perhaps in time we shall begin dialogue on these advantages.
Greetings. I have taken the place of the Gerent, he has returned to the Singularity to discuss further arrangement of our accord.
His return is imminent, of this I have been assured. We are optimistic that our bargain will be met and that peace shall reign between our peoples.
In accordance with our agreement we are still furnishing this bauble. Please, take it.
Such things are a small matter when we speak of a shared knowledge of species.
In time, you may come to understand the auspicious nature of the Quiddity and the beneficial nature of the all.

No, no -- you keep that, comrade! Use it to go into the world and continue our mission!
I do not want this. There is something ... not ... right ...
Anomaly! Anomaly! Chaos! Disruption!
No.

Comrade, what is this? Where did you find it? Ah, an Observer mask. I shall keep this broken mask, but you may have this repaired Inquisitor mask as your reward.
I do not wish to know how you acquired this, my friend. But this world is a dangerous place, and by wearing this mask you have proven you are a predator, not the prey.
Anomaly inconsistent with structure. Form devoid of contact. Conclusion, disruption to the Singularity. I must --
Please do not bring me any more masks like this. They are ... disturbing to me.

Taken off the corpse of a Virindi Master, no doubt. These masks are used as a way for the Virindi to hide their true forms, which are...well...um, Okay I've never seen one, but I hear that they have tentacles. The masks, Virindi believe, are a passable human face. Can you believe they think themselves intelligent.

A completed version of the mask. You can see that the eyes are open almost as wide as someone would open their eyes under normal circumstances. There is no nose, but the mouth is turned up at the ends to display an unnerving smile etched forever. These masks are worn by Master's, assisting them in evading melee attacks.

Wow. I...um...yeah. So this is from an inquisitor. They came here a while back as a way to enforce the singularity back onto the renegades that put their loyalty behind Levistras and the estranged Ecorto.

You're a tough one. These masks are worn by the imposing and frightening Inquistors. They were sent to Dereth in an effort to quell the resistance of the renegade virindi that stood with Ecorto and Levistras. They remain here now to enforce the will of the singularity over the loyalist virindi that are still here on Dereth. Cunning, violent, powerful magicians and warriors, Inquisitors are the...
While Martine has yet to decipher, or impart just what these keys are truly for, he has speculated that in the singularity they have some function to signify rank or some such...
Okay, I made that up. I really don't know much about them other than they unlock Directive chests which are a direct conduit into the singularity, or something.
Okay, I made that up. I really don't know much about them other than they unlock Master chests which are a direct conduit into the singularity, or something.

Okay, I made that up. I really don't know much about them other than they unlock Singularity chests which are a direct conduit into the singularity, or something. I do know that they are worth a great fortune. As typically the best items can be found in the chests.

Now before you go handing me any of the weapons that these things can make just listen. During the battle against Levistras and the Virindi that were trying to create the New Singularity these ingots started popping up on raiding parties across Dereth.

Martine made it a point to find as many of these as he could. He told us that they were created as a weapon for the Tumerok's that had given their souls over to the Virindi, I think that you know them now as the Hea.

At any rate, the Virindi that carried these were supposed to be meeting their Tumerok allies and somehow were "thrown off course" in portal space and ended up in the middle of hordes of people. Fortunate for us, not so fortunate for them.

There has been much speculation amongst many here as to whether Martine had anything to do with it, but I have heard that Aerbax himself may have had a hand in the betrayal, but who knows? That is the real question.

Only the most powerful members of the Singularity carry these. As to what their real purpose is, I'm not sure. But it has something to do with their bodies and their rank, and how they are able to stay whole on Dereth.
Members of the Singularity carry these. As to what their real purpose is, I'm not sure. But it has something to do with their bodies and their rank, and how they are able to stay whole on Dereth.

Crafted from pieces of chorizite, pyreal and obsidian these pieces of solidified magic would have been crafted into an object that would have brought the Singularity to Dereth. How this would have been achieved will always remain a mystery, as the renegade faction was thwarted, thankfully.

Martine was actually sad when this occurred. He was looking forward to ripping his torturers apart. Ecorto, a Virindi once aligned with the renegades, turned against his cohorts and collected fragments to destroy them and the hopes of creating the new singularity.
When Bael'zharon, walked on the world this object was found in the chakron flux, and without it the new prison for the Hopeslayer would never have been built.

This is a trophy mask, wearable of course. It was taken from an obsidian director. The leaders of the renegade faction that defended the obsidian. They were and still are a powerful breed. The cunning, intelligence and advanced understanding of the Virindi combined with the avarice of mankind. Wear this with pride.
Aren't they cute? I love them.
What?
You want it back?
But you gave it to me...
Just kidding. Here you go.
Communication devices, though how anyone can decipher this is beyond me. I have heard that Diyas-al Yat knows how to figure these out.

Communication devices...nothing more. Somehow the Virindi etch their thoughts onto these shards and can absorb the information that is written upon them. Diyas-al Yat can help you with these, but I certainly can't.
Hello! You are a human, I can tell by your canter. Yes I am Virindi, but I am loyal to Martine, what my fellows did. Horrible.
%n snickers.
Okay, it's really one of Martine's tricks. A cunning disguise, No?
I'm a scholar. Martine asked me to tell anyone that kills the darned things what their leavings mean. I don't translate though. Can't read a book for nothing.
Hello Fellow human, might I interest you in some insight into we who live beyond the world?
If you would hand over any objects of Virindi nature I will divine the truth behind them.

The Virindi's cloak seems to boil, as if a thousand insects were seeking to escape before it collapses. The dying Virindi shares its final thoughts with you: "Your life is forfeit, human.  You simply do not know it yet.  In killing me, %s, you have gained access to your doom."
As the Virindi falls to the ground, there is a bright flash of light!

The Virindi's mask is backlit with a deep purple light!  The dying Virindi shares its thoughts with you before it collapses.  "The new directive granted you surcease while they continued with their plans, and this is how you repay us?!?  Know this, meat puppet, there will be a reckoning..."

Slicing and dicing is fun.  I used to be able to do it so much more before the Master came to me.   But I am not complaining!  You must not tell Master I was complaining.
That blade looks sharp.  Can I touch it?  I would like to touch it.  The Master does not allow me to touch sharp things anymore.  There is no escape.  There is no escape.  There is no escape.
My former kin never used the piercing objects.  But I have seen...I have seen it now with my own eyes...the piercing works well.  The flesh is weak.  Weak and filled with red.
Crush and crush and crush and crush.  Crush and crush and crush and crush.
The Master once told me that his people had a saying, 'If you prick me, do I not bleed?'  But I was watching him during one of his 'presentations.'  He did not bleed at all.
My hands once were weapons, too.  Look what has happened to me.
So many things devoted to destruction.  Even the tools of the earth, shaped from the ethereal and the ideal, with a singular purpose:  To break the bonds that tie.
Death sings through the air.  Small sharp sticks raising their voice.  A chorus of blood.
Before I became owned by the Master.  I had not known such a small quarrel could make a head explode.  While this whole experience has been painful and shattering, it has certainly been educational.
Flying death, floating death.
Oceans of red. He bled.

The Master would be pleased to see you have made it so far, little one.  You haven't lost your pretty Singularity weapon now, did you?  Give it to me, and we shall embark on the next step on this journey...yes?  Yesssssss.
If you already have one of my pretty Singularity weapons, let me enhance it for you.

But you will never rid the world of my power, and my minions will carry on the war without me! As fo...
Yes, my vassal, I will provide you the supplies you need, for a small fee.
The life outside of Asheron's protection is a tough road and I can sell you the supplies you will need for your journey.
I am Bael'Zharon, welcome to my lair
I'm sure one of my other vassals can use this
You're sure you won't need that?  Well, ok, I'm sure I can find someone who will like it.
Some rat has taken some of my pants, but they don't know how to drop them, so it must be terribly hard to sell them!
Put that too good use and kill, kill, kill!
Be strong my loyal follower of darkness!
Some of my sparring clothes seem to have up and walked away, but you buy from the source!

"Suddenly you hear a lone Tumerok's anguished scream from the depths of portal space."

greetings: A small green snake which is coiled around the coin grips it covetously and flicks its tongue at you.
"My coin will not fulfill the ache of wretched greed. My curse on those who take my coin and mistake that ache with need."
The snake wraps itself around your fingers, preventing you from dropping the coin.
"You cannot discard my curse so easily. You are charged with a mission to help those in need and I will see that you fulfill it."
The snake releases its grip on your fingers as you slip the coin back into your backpack.
"Do not forget that you are bound to this coin as much as I am."

When I came to this world I thought I had been brought here to slay the beasts that threatened our very lives. I used my skills as an archer to slay every creature I sighted. I can't count how many I killed...

One day while hunting in the Tiofor Woods I came across an Ursuin. It rushed me and I slayed without a thought. It wasn't any real threat, but I thought it might have some trophy I could sell. When it's death throes had finished I went to search it for treasure and heard a low growling mewl. I searched for some time eventually finding a flap of moss covering a small den hidden in the roots of a...

Inside the den were two baby ursuin cubs crying for their mother. I crouched there in shock for what felt like hours. I had become the beast that killed without thought, destroying families. I gathered the small cubs promising that I would learn from my mistakes, promising them to become a better person, that I would never lift my bow without good reason again.

I returned home to the desert and was ridiculed for my perceived weakness. It was a huge joke for the locals. They thought I was crazy. I knew better though and felt sorry for them. They would make the same mistakes over and over as I had done.

I raised the two cubs as though they were my own, living free and happy in the woods, occasionally trading with curious hunters. One such hunter stayed awhile and taught me the teachings of Jojii. She never told me her name, but she was kind to me and seemed to understand my failings as though she too had wrestled demons.

When the cubs, Kogo and Not, were old enough I let them go. They were still wild at heart and needed to run free, away from their mothers over protective eye. I had taught them how to hide from hunters and forage for food and beyond that they would need to find their own way. I wandered from place to place helping those in need and I finally ended up here in Wai Jhou, my new home. I now try to...

Let humility dwell within you. Without humility you will be easily misled and lose your way.

Let detachment guard you. Without detachment you will be unable to let go and move forward.
Let compassion be in your every thought and action, as you strive to help others in their paths.

Do not make the mistake of following only one of Jojii's Principles. You must strive to attain a balance between the four stones. Only then will you reach the inner peace you seek and walk the path to heaven.

An unbalanced arrow will not fly in a straight path and will hit something other than your target. If you balance you life with all of the Four Stones you will fly a true path. Don't be afraid to fail and forgive yourself your failings. We all fail on our paths occasionally, but we must notch our arrow again and aim for our goals.

I hope I may be of service.
Thank you. Enjoy your stay in Nanto.
Very good.
Thank you.
Greetings, greetings! It is my honor to meet a fellow traveler in this distant land. Could I interest you in a memento, for the kids back in Dereth?

Please tell your peers about me. No doubt they also have eager young journeymen under their tutelage, eager for spoils from this island. Surely, one of my shirts would be the most unique and memorable twink... er, souvenir!
Ah. I may be able to use that.

Bet they wish they could make it here, yes? Truly, it is a rare place in this strange world that hasn't been overrun by humanity. Aerlinthe brings back memories of the good old days in Dereth, does it not?
Oy.
Whatcher want?

Aye, I came here from Arwic. Once thought I'd make a fortune there, so ah spent most of me savings to buy a plot of land in town. Land was expensive in Arwic, yeh know. A'course, the damned Shadows saw to make my land into a smoking hole!

Business is slow here. Seems the Gare-un... Gare-oon... the desert people... have some religious problem with stout. Can ye imagine? Turning up your nose at a good highland stout... I dinna understand 'em. Had to make a deal with al-Luq of Yaraq to sell Cove Apple Cider. It's all they'll buy.

We get a lot of mages through here. Seems there's something down in the lower caverns they're interested in. I don' know much about that finger-wiggling bunk meself, but I reckon it must be somethin' pretty important to them.

Yeh know what I think? I think the desert people just string a bunch of letters together to make their names. I mean, look at the jeweler. Jurraf al-somethingorother. Looks kinda like 'diggy-quitter.' Why can't they use good, pronounceable Aluvian names, like 'Gondibyr,' or 'Fadmynda?'

When Xarabydun was first explored, they found a good lot of books in the lower levels. Now I don' know much about book learnin' meself, but whatever was in them must have been pretty important. Those swishy academics from Zaikhal fairly ran here to get at 'em, and carried them all away. Could be they forgot some, though.
You ever hear of Knath'taed? Funny lil' critters. They like to hang around in the lower caves. Looks like the Empyrean put up doors to keep 'em out. Dunno why they didn't just kill 'em all.
Now, the Bey will say otherwise, but I'm tellin' yeh straight. There's a bloody big rat down in the sewers, and the thing spits lightning bolts.
That scribe, Sifida... She's a bit off in the head, if yeh take my meaning. She came here from Tufa. Doesn't say much, just keeps to herself.
Not bad, not bad. But are ye gonna drink like a real man, or unload food on me like some bleedin' merchie?
Did yeh only come to sell? Buy a stout!
Come back anytime, mate. I'll keep the taps flowing.
The strong scent of fried food drifts down the corridor.
Please stay in town and enjoy the view. Make yourselves at home.
Kuro and I thank you for coming to our humble shop!
We enjoy having people stay in town. Most people just pass through.
We call this place Kara because it's usually so empty, but I don't mind it at all.
Another one comes for my services...So, what do you wish of me today?
Sawato used to be such a quiet place...
May this spell last long and your visit here be short...
As you wish.
What a fight! I took a few trips to the lifestone, I must admit. Of course, our lifestone is so close that I was able to jump right back into the fray! What a glorious battle!
Speak with Lord Kresovus. His heart seems much aggrieved at Balor's absence.
This is a fine item.  Use it well, or the one that takes it from you will.
Thank you.
Welcome! What's your pleasure today?
Thank you for your business. Please return soon.
You drive a hard bargain, my friend.
An excellent purchase.
Welcome to Lin's best bows.
Thank you. Come again.
Thank you. Have you been to Glenden Wood? One day I should like to go there.
Thank you. Ah, I do like this town!
Thank you. I welcome your business any time!
Very good.
Thank you very much.
Welcome to the town of the eastern tower.
Thank you.  Please come again.  And don't forget to go see the tower.
I heard that this was once where a failed Aluvian community stood.  But I don't believe it.
I think I can resell that, yes.
Good choice, indeed.
Ah, I see you have items you cannot appraise! I am here for you!
It's amusing to me how most items end up being sold and not cherished.
With luck, my magic will help you appraise most items.
As you wish.

The Shadows overran our city. But soon, they were gone. I can only hope that Captain K'rank's valiant efforts frightened them witless. But perhaps there was something else... Perhaps they merely sought to test our defenses?
I cannot heal those whom I cannot see. Speak with Lord Kresovus. Return our beloved Balor to us.
I have no use for this myself, but perhaps I can sell it to another adventurer.
I'm certain that will come in handy...
There was little I could salvage, yet I have some items to sell.
Thank you for your business. Someday we will rebuild.
You drive a hard bargain, my friend.
An excellent purchase.
